name: A puma at large
trans: 一只在野外自由活动的美洲狮

name: Where must the puma have come from?
trans: 这只美洲狮一定是从哪里来的呢？

name: Pumas are large, cat-like animals which are found in America.
trans: 美洲狮是一种体型较大的、类似猫的动物，它们生活在美洲地区。

name: When reports came into London Zoo that a wild puma had been spotted forty-five miles south of London,
trans: 当伦敦动物园接到报告称在伦敦以南45英里处发现了一只野生美洲狮时……

name: they were not taken seriously.
trans: 他们没有受到重视（或：他们的意见没有被认真对待）。

name: However, as the evidence began to accumulate,
trans: 然而，随着证据的不断积累……

name: experts from the Zoo felt obliged to investigate,
trans: 动物园的专家们觉得有责任对此事进行调查。

name: for the descriptions given by people who claimed to have seen the puma were extraordinarily similar.
trans: 那些声称见过美洲狮的人所提供的描述非常相似。

name: The hunt for the puma began in a small village where a woman picking blackberries saw 'a large cat'only five yards away from her.
trans: 对这只美洲狮的搜寻始于一个小镇。在那里，一位正在采摘黑莓的女子发现了一只“大型猫科动物”，它就站在离她仅五码远的地方。

name: It immediately ran away when she saw it,
trans: 她一看到它，立刻就跑开了。

name: and experts confirmed that a puma will not attack a human being unless it is cornered.
trans: 专家们证实，美洲狮只有在被逼入绝境时才会攻击人类。

name: The search proved difficult,
trans: 这次搜索工作非常困难。

name: for the puma was often observed at one place in the morning and at another place twenty miles away in the evening.
trans: 人们经常在早晨看到那只美洲狮出现在一个地方，而到了晚上，它却出现在二十英里外的另一个地方。

name: Wherever it went, it left behind it a trail of dead deer and small animals like rabbits.
trans: 无论它去了哪里，都会留下死鹿以及兔子等小型动物的尸体作为痕迹。

name: Paw prints were seen in a number of places and puma fur was found clinging to bushes.
trans: 在多个地方都发现了爪印，同时还发现了一些美洲狮的毛发粘在灌木丛上。

name: Several people complained of 'cat-like noises' at night and a businessman on a fishing trip saw the puma up a tree.
trans: 有几个人抱怨晚上听到了类似猫叫声的声音；一位正在钓鱼的商人还看到一只美洲狮爬在树上。

name: The experts were now fully convinced that the animal was a puma,
trans: 专家们现在完全确信这种动物是一只美洲狮。

name: but where had it come from?
trans: 但是，它究竟是从哪里来的呢？

name: As no pumas had been reported missing from any zoo in the country,
trans: 由于该国没有任何动物园报告有美洲狮失踪的情况，

name: this one must have been in the possession of a private collector and somehow managed to escape.
trans: 这件藏品肯定曾经属于某个私人收藏家，后来不知怎么地流落到了外面（即从收藏家的手中流失了）。

name: The hunt went on for several weeks,
trans: 这次搜寻持续了好几周。

name: but the puma was not caught.
trans: 但是那只美洲狮没有被抓住。

name: It is disturbing to think that a dangerous wild animal is still at large in the quiet countryside.
trans: 想到有一只危险的野生动物仍然在宁静的乡村里自由活动，实在令人不安。

name: Thirteen equals one
trans: “十三等于一……”

name: Was the vicar pleased that the clock was striking? Why?
trans: 牧师是否因为时钟重新开始报时而感到高兴呢？为什么呢？

name: Our vicar is always raising money for one cause or another,
trans: 我们的牧师总是为各种慈善事业筹款，

name: but he has never managed to get enough money to have the church clock repaired.
trans: 但他始终没能筹集到足够的钱来修理教堂的时钟。

name: The big clock which used to strike the hours day and night was damaged many years ago and has been silent ever since.
trans: 那座曾经日夜报时的大钟在多年前就损坏了，从那以后就一直处于“沉默”状态。

name: One night, however, our vicar woke up with a start:the clock was striking the hours!
trans: 然而有一天晚上，牧师突然被惊醒了——时钟竟然又开始报时了！

name: Looking at his watch, he saw that it was one o'clock,
trans: 他看了看手表，发现时间是凌晨一点，

name: but the bell struck thirteen times before it stopped.
trans: 但钟声却响了十三下才停止。

name: Armed with a torch, the vicar went up into the clock tower to see what was going on.
trans: 牧师拿着火把走上钟楼，想弄清楚发生了什么。

name: In the torchlight, he caught sight of a figure whom he immediately recognized as Bill Wilkins, our local grocer.
trans: 在火把的光芒中，他看到了一个人影，立刻认出那是当地的杂货商比尔·威尔金斯。

name: 'Whatever are you doing up here Bill?' asked the vicar in surprise.
trans: “比尔，你在这里干什么？”牧师惊讶地问道。

name: 'I'm trying to repair the bell, ' answered Bill.
trans: “我正在尝试修理这个铃铛，”比尔回答道。

name: 'I've been coming up here night after night for weeks now.
trans: “这几周来，我每晚都来到这里。”

name: You see, I was hoping to give you a surprise.'
trans: 你看，我本来想给你一个惊喜的。

name: 'You certainly did give me a surprise!' said the vicar.
trans: “你确实给了我一个惊喜！”牧师说道。

name: 'You've probably woken up everyone in the village as well.
trans: 你可能也把村子里的所有人都吵醒了。

name: Still, I'm glad the bell is working again.'
trans: 不过，我很高兴这个铃铛又能正常使用了。

name: 'That's the trouble, vicar, 'answered Bill. 'It's working all right,
trans: “问题就在这里，牧师，”比尔回答说，“这个装置本身运作得挺正常的。”

name: but I'm afraid that at one o'clock it will strike thirteen times and there's nothing I can do about it.'
trans: 但我担心，到了凌晨一点的时候，钟声会敲响十三下，而我对此无能为力。

name: 'We'll get used to that, Bill, 'said the vicar.
trans: “我们会慢慢习惯的，比尔，”牧师说道。

name: 'Thirteen is not as good as one, but it's better than nothing.
trans: 十三虽然不如一，但总比没有好。

name: Now let's go downstairs and have a cup of tea.'
trans: 现在，我们下楼去喝杯茶吧。

name: An unknown goddess
trans: 一位未知的女神

name: How did the archaeologists know that the statue was a goddess?
trans: 考古学家是如何知道这座雕像是女神的呢？

name: Some time ago, an interesting discovery was made by archaeologists on the Aegean island of Kea.
trans: 不久前，考古学家在爱琴海的基阿岛上有了一个有趣的发现。

name: An American team explored a temple which stands in an ancient city on the promontory of Ayia Irini.
trans: 一支美国团队探索了一座位于阿伊亚·伊里尼（Ayia Irini）海岬上的一座古城的寺庙。

name: The city at one time must have been prosperous, for it enjoyed a high level of civilization.
trans: 这座城市曾经一定非常繁荣，因为它拥有高度发达的文明。

name: Houses -- often three storeys high -- were built of stone.
trans: 房屋通常有三层楼高，全部由石头建造而成。

name: They had large rooms with beautifully decorated walls.
trans: 他们拥有宽敞的房间，房间的墙壁装饰得非常精美。

name: The city was even equipped with a drainage system, for a great many clay pipes were found beneath the narrow streets.
trans: 这座城市甚至配备了排水系统；因为在狭窄的街道下方发现了大量的陶土管道。

name: The temple which the archaeologists explored was used as a place of worship from the fifteenth century B.C. until Roman times.
trans: 考古学家们探索的那座寺庙，从公元前15世纪起就被用作礼拜场所，一直使用到罗马时代。

name: In the most sacred room of the temple, clay fragments of fifteen statues were found.
trans: 在寺庙最神圣的房间里，发现了十五座雕像的陶土碎片。

name: Each of these represented a goddess and had, at one time, been painted.
trans: 每一个（这些物品）都象征着一位女神，它们曾经都被绘制过（即上面都画有女神的形象）。

name: The body of one statue was found among remains dating from the 15th century B.C.
trans: 一尊雕像的躯干是在可追溯至公元前15世纪的遗迹中被发现的。

name: Its missing head happened to be among remains of the fifth century B.C.
trans: 它缺失的头部则属于公元前5世纪的遗迹。

name: This head must have been found in Classical times and carefully preserved.
trans: 这个头部很可能是后来在古典时期被发现的，并且被精心保存了下来。

name: It was very old and precious even then.
trans: 即使在那个时候，这尊雕像也已经非常古老且珍贵了。

name: When the archaeologists reconstructed the fragments, they were amazed to find that the goddess turned out to be a very modern-looking woman.
trans: 当考古学家重新拼凑这些碎片时，他们惊讶地发现，这座女神的形象实际上是一位看起来非常现代的女性。

name: She stood three feet high and her hands rested on her hips.
trans: 她的身高约为三英尺（约90厘米），双手叉腰站立。

name: She was wearing a full-length skirt which swept the ground.
trans: 她穿着一条及地的长裙。

name: Despite her great age, she was very graceful indeed, but, so far, the archaeologists have been unable to discover her identity.
trans: 尽管年代久远，她的姿态依然十分优雅；不过到目前为止，考古学家还未能确定她的身份。

name: The double life of Alfred Bloggs
trans: 阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯的双重生活
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: Why did Alf want a white-collar job?
trans: 为什么阿尔夫想要一份白领工作呢？
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
trans: 如今，从事体力劳动的人往往比在办公室工作的人赚得更多。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as 'white-collar workers' for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work.
trans: 在办公室工作的人通常被称为“白领工人”，原因很简单：他们上班时通常需要穿着衬衫和领带。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
trans: 人类的天性就是这样：很多人往往愿意放弃更高的薪资，只为获得成为白领员工的特权。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman for the Ellesmere Corporation.
trans: 这可能会引发一些有趣（或奇怪）的情况，就像阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯（Alfred Bloggs）的经历一样。他曾为埃尔斯米尔公司（Ellesmere Corporation）担任清洁工。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: When he got married, Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.
trans: 当他结婚的时候，阿尔夫太尴尬了，以至于什么都没敢跟妻子说起自己的工作。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation.
trans: 他只是简单地告诉她，自己为那家公司工作。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: Every morning, he left home dressed in a smart black suit.
trans: 每天早上，他都会穿着一套整洁的黑色西装离开家。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman.
trans: 然后他换上了工作服，接下来的八个小时里一直从事清洁工作（也就是当清洁工）。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: Before returning home at night, he took a shower and changed back into his suit.
trans: 在晚上回家之前，他洗了个澡，然后换回了西装。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: Alf did this for over two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret.
trans: 阿尔夫从事这份工作已经两年多了，他的同事们一直保守着他的秘密。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: Alf's wife has never discovered that she married a dustman and she never will, for Alf has just found another job.
trans: 阿尔夫的妻子从未发现她嫁给了一个清洁工，而且永远也不会发现——因为阿尔夫刚刚找到了另一份工作。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: He will soon be working in an office.
trans: 他很快就会在办公室里工作了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
trans: 虽然他的收入将只有以前的二分之一，但他觉得这种地位的提升远远值得他放弃原来的收入。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him 'Mr.Bloggs', not 'Alf'.
trans: 从现在开始，他每天都会穿西装，别人会称呼他为“布洛格斯先生”，而不再是“阿尔夫”。
lesson: NCE3 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

name: The facts
trans: 事实

name: What was the consequence of the editor's insistence on facts and statistics?
trans: 编辑坚持使用事实和统计数据的结果是什么呢？

name: Editors of newspapers and magazines often go to extremes to provide their readers with unimportant facts and statistics.
trans: 报纸和杂志的编辑们常常不遗余力地提供一些对读者来说其实并不重要的信息或统计数据。

name: Last year a journalist had been instructed by a well-known magazine to write an article on the president's palace in a new African republic.
trans: 去年，一位记者受一家知名杂志的委托，撰写了一篇关于某个新成立的非洲共和国总统官邸的文章。

name: When the article arrived, the editor read the first sentence and then refused to publish it.
trans: 当这篇文章寄到编辑手中时，编辑读了第一句话，随后便决定拒绝发表它。

name: The article began:'Hundreds of steps lead to the high wall which surrounds the president's palace.'
trans: 文章的开头是这样的：“数百级台阶通向环绕总统宫殿的高墙。”

name: The editor at once sent the journalist a fax instructing him to find out the exact number of steps and the height of the wall.
trans: 编辑立即给记者发了一份传真，要求他查明墙的确切台阶数量以及墙的高度。

name: The journalist immediately set out to obtain these important facts, but he took a long time to send them.
trans: 记者立即着手收集这些重要的事实，但他花了很长时间才将这些信息发送出去。

name: Meanwhile, the editor was getting impatient, for the magazine would soon go to press.
trans: 与此同时，编辑们越来越不耐烦了，因为杂志的印刷工作即将开始。

name: He sent the journalist two more faxes, but received no reply.
trans: 他又给那位记者发了两封传真，但仍然没有收到任何回复。

name: He sent yet another fax informing the journalist that if he did not reply soon he would be fired.
trans: 他又发了一封传真，告知那位记者：如果他不能尽快回复，就会被解雇。

name: When the journalist again failed to reply,  the editor reluctantly published the article as it had originally been written.
trans: 当记者再次没有回复时，编辑无奈之下还是按照文章原本的写法将其发表了。

name: A week later, the editor at last received a fax from the journalist.
trans: 一周后，编辑终于收到了那位记者发来的传真。

name: Not only had the poor man been arrested, but he had been sent to prison as well.
trans: 这个可怜的人不仅被逮捕了，还被关进了监狱。

name: However, he had at last been allowed to send a fax in which he informed the editor that he had been arrested
trans: 然而，他终于被允许发送了一份传真，他在传真中告知编辑自己已经被逮捕了。

name: while counting the 1, 084 steps leading to the 15th foot wall which surrounded the president's palace.
trans: 在数着通往第15道围墙的1,084级台阶时，那道围墙环绕着总统的宫殿。

name: Smash-and-grab
trans: “Smash-and-grab”是一种犯罪行为，指的是犯罪分子通过破坏门窗等手段强行闯入商店或公共场所，然后抢夺财物并迅速逃离现场。这种行为通常发生在人群密集、安全措施薄弱的地区。

name: How did Mr. Taylor try to stop the thieves?
trans: 泰勒先生是如何试图阻止那些小偷的？

name: The expensive shops in a famous arcade near Piccadilly were just opening.
trans: 位于皮卡迪利附近的一家著名商业街内的那些高档商店刚刚开业。

name: At this time of the morning, the arcade was almost empty.
trans: 在这个清晨的时刻，游戏厅里几乎空无一人。

name: Mr. Taylor, the owner of a jewellery shop was admiring a new window display.
trans: 泰勒先生是一家珠宝店的老板，他正在欣赏店内的新橱窗陈列。

name: Two of his assistants had been working busily since 8 o'clock and had only just finished.
trans: 他的两名助手从早上8点开始就一直在忙碌地工作，直到现在才刚刚完成工作。

name: Diamond necklaces and rings had been beautifully arranged on a background of black velvet.
trans: 钻石项链和戒指被精心地摆放在黑色天鹅绒的背景上。

name: After gazing at the display for several minutes, Mr. Taylor went back into his shop.
trans: 在盯着显示屏看了几分钟之后，泰勒先生回到了他的店里。

name: The silence was suddenly broken when a large car, with its headlights on and its horn blaring, roared down the arcade.
trans: 突然，一片寂静被打破了——一辆大型汽车冲进了拱廊里，车灯亮着，喇叭声震耳欲聋。

name: It came to a stop outside the jeweller's.
trans: 它停在了珠宝店的外面。

name: One man stayed at the wheel while two others with black stockings over their faces jumped out and smashed the window of the shop with iron bars.
trans: 有一个人继续驾驶汽车，另外两个人则戴着遮住脸部的黑色长袜，从车里跳了出来，用铁棍砸碎了商店的窗户。

name: While this was going on, Mr. Taylor was upstairs.
trans: 就在这件事发生的时候，泰勒先生正在楼上。

name: He and his staff began throwing furniture out of the window.
trans: 他和他的员工开始把家具从窗户扔出去。

name: Chairs and tables went flying into the arcade.
trans: 椅子和桌子都被抛飞到了拱廊里。

name: One of the thieves was struck by a heavy statue,
trans: 其中一个小偷被一座沉重的雕像砸中了。

name: but he was too busy helping himself to diamonds to notice any pain.
trans: 但他忙着为自己谋取钻石，根本没注意到任何疼痛。

name: The raid was all over in three minutes, for the men scrambled back into the car and it moved off at a fantastic speed.
trans: 这次突袭在短短三分钟内就结束了；那些人纷纷跳回车上，车子随后以极快的速度离开了现场。

name: Just as it was leaving,
trans: 就在它即将离开的时候……

name: Mr.Taylor rushed out and ran after it throwing ashtrays and vases,
trans: 泰勒先生冲了出去，追着那个东西扔烟灰缸和花瓶。

name: but it was impossible to stop the thieves.
trans: 但是，根本无法阻止那些小偷。

name: They had got away with thousands of pounds worth of diamonds.
trans: 他们成功偷走了价值数千英镑的钻石。

name: Mutilated Ladies
trans: “被损坏的钞票”

name: Why did Jane cook John's wallet?
trans: 简为什么要把约翰的钱包弄坏呢？

name: Has it ever happened to you?
trans: 你有没有遇到过这种事？

name: Have you ever put your trousers in the washing machine and then remembered there was a large bank note in your back pocket?
trans: 你是否曾经把裤子放进洗衣机，后来才想起后口袋里还有一张大面额的钞票？

name: When you rescued your trousers, did you find the note was whiter than white?
trans: 当你把裤子取出来时，发现那张钞票已经变得雪白一片了……

name: People who live in Britain needn't despair when they make mistakes like this (and a lot of people do)!
trans: 生活在英国的人们遇到这种错误时不必绝望（其实很多人都遇到过这种情况！）

name: Fortunately for them, the Bank of England has a team called Mutilated Ladies
trans: 幸运的是，英格兰银行有一个专门处理此类问题的部门，名为“Mutilated Ladies”（意为“被损坏的钞票处理小组”）。

name: which deals with claims from people who fed their money to a machine or to their dog.
trans: 这个部门负责接收那些不小心把钱放进机器或被狗咬坏的顾客的投诉。

name: Dogs, it seems, love to chew up money!
trans: 看来，狗确实很喜欢咬钱啊！

name: A recent case concerns Jane Butlin whose fiance, John, runs a successful furniture business.
trans: 最近有一个案例与简·巴特林有关：她的未婚夫约翰经营着一家成功的家具公司。

name: John had a very good day and put his wallet containing ￡3, 000 into the microwave oven for safekeeping.
trans: 那天约翰心情很好，为了安全起见，他把装有3000英镑的钱包放进了微波炉里“保管”。

name: Then he and Jane went horse-riding.
trans: 然后他和简一起去骑马了。

name: When they got home, Jane cooked their dinner in the microwave oven and without realizing it, cooked her fiance's wallet as well.
trans: 当他们回到家后，简用微波炉为他们准备了晚餐；不知不觉中，她也把未婚夫的钱包给“煮”坏了（即钱包被微波炉的高温损坏了）。

name: Imagine their dismay when they found a beautifully-cooked wallet and notes turned to ash!
trans: 想象一下他们的沮丧吧：当他们发现那个精心制作的钱包以及里面的钞票全都化成了灰烬时……

name: John went to see his bank manager who sent the remains of wallet and the money
trans: 约翰去见了他的银行经理，银行经理把他的钱包残骸和里面的钱都退还给了他。

name: to the special department of the Bank of England in Newcastle: the Mutilated Ladies!
trans: 致位于纽卡斯尔的英格兰银行特别部门——“那些身体受到伤害的女士们”！

name: They examined the remains and John got all his money back.
trans: 他们检查了那些遗骸，约翰也因此拿回了他所有的钱。

name: 'So long as there's something to identify, we will give people their money back,' said a spokeswoman for the Bank.
trans: “只要能够识别出相关对象或信息，我们就会把钱退还给客户，”该银行的一位女发言人说道。

name: 'Last year, we paid ￡1.5 million on 21,000 claims.'
trans: 去年，我们为21,000起索赔支付了150万英镑。

name: A famous monastery
trans: 一座著名的修道院

name: What are the St.Bernard dogs used for?
trans: 圣伯纳德犬是用来做什么的？

name: The Great St.Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
trans: 大圣伯纳德山口（Great St. Bernard Pass）将瑞士与意大利连接起来。

name: At 2,473 metres, it is the highest mountain pass in Europe.
trans: 海拔2,473米，它是欧洲最高的山口。

name: The famous monastery of St.Bernard,
trans: 著名的圣伯纳德修道院

name: which was founded in the eleventh century, lies about a mile away.
trans: 该机构成立于十一世纪，距离这里大约一英里远。

name: For hundreds of years, St.Bernard dogs have saved the lives of travellers crossing the dangerous Pass.
trans: 几个世纪以来，圣伯纳德犬一直拯救着那些穿越危险山口的旅行者的生命。

name: These friendly dogs, which were first brought from Asia,
trans: 这些友好的狗狗最初是从亚洲引进的。

name: were used as watchdogs even in Roman times.
trans: 即使在罗马时代，这些动物也被用作看门犬（即用于监视或警戒的动物）。

name: Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous,
trans: 既然已经修建了一条穿过山脉的隧道，这个山口的安全性就大大提高了（即：再也不用担心通过这个山口会遇到危险了）。

name: but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
trans: 但是每年，每当有旅行者遇到困难时，那些狗仍然会被派往雪地里去救援他们。

name: Despite the new tunnel,
trans: 尽管有了这条新隧道，

name: there are still a few people who rashly attempt to cross the Pass on foot.
trans: 仍然有一些人贸然尝试徒步穿越这个山口。

name: During the summer months, the monastery is very busy,
trans: 在夏季，这座修道院非常繁忙。

name: for it is visited by thousands of people who cross the Pass in cars.
trans: 因为这里有成千上万的人开车穿过山口前来参观。

name: As there are so many people about, the dogs have to be kept in a special enclosure.
trans: 由于周围有很多人，这些狗必须被关在一个特殊的围栏里。

name: In winter, however, life at the monastery is quite different.
trans: 然而，在冬天，修道院的生活却大不相同了。

name: The temperature drops to -30 degrees,
trans: 气温降到了零下30度。

name: and very few people attempt to cross the Pass.
trans: 而且，很少有人试图穿越这个山口。

name: The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
trans: 僧侣们更喜欢冬天而不是夏天，因为冬天他们有更多的隐私。

name: The dogs have greater freedom, too,
trans: 这些狗也拥有更大的自由。

name: for they are allowed to wander outside their enclosure.
trans: 因为它们被允许在围栏外自由活动。

name: The only regular visitors to the monastery in winter are parties of skiers who go there at Christmas and Easter.
trans: 冬天里，唯一经常造访这座修道院的人是一群滑雪者——他们会在圣诞节和复活节期间来到这里。

name: These young people,
trans: 这些年轻人，

name: who love the peace of the mountains,
trans: 他们热爱山间的宁静，

name: always receive a warm welcome at St.Bernard's monastery.
trans: 在圣伯纳德修道院总是受到热情的欢迎。

name: Flying cats
trans: 会飞的猫

name: How do cats try to protect themselves when falling from great heights?
trans: 当猫从高处坠落时，它们会如何保护自己呢？

name: Cats never fail to fascinate human beings.
trans: 猫总是能让人类着迷。

name: They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans, but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well.
trans: 它们对人类可能表现出友好和亲昵的态度，但同时也过着充满神秘的生活。

name: They never become submissive like dogs and horses.
trans: 与狗或马不同，猫永远不会变得温顺听话。

name: As a result, humans have learned to respect feline independence.
trans: 因此，人类逐渐学会了尊重猫的独立性。

name: Most cats remain suspicious of humans all their lives.
trans: 大多数猫一生都对人类保持警惕。

name: One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives.
trans: 关于猫最让我们感到好奇的一点，就是人们普遍认为它们有九条命。

name: Apparently, there is a good deal of truth in this idea.
trans: 事实上，这个说法确实有一定道理。

name: A cat's ability to survive falls is based on fact.
trans: 猫之所以能够在坠落中存活下来，是有科学依据的。

name: Recently the New York Animal Medical Centre made a study of 132 cats over a period of five months.
trans: 最近，纽约动物医疗中心对132只猫进行了为期五个月的研究。

name: All these cats had one experience in common: they had fallen off high buildings,
trans: 所有这些猫都有一个共同的经历：它们都从高楼上掉了下来。

name: yet only eight of them died from shock or injuries.
trans: 然而，只有八人因休克或受伤而死亡。

name: Of course, New York is the ideal place for such an interesting study, because there is no shortage of tall buildings.
trans: 当然，纽约是进行这项研究的理想地点——因为那里的高楼大厦实在太多了。

name: There are plenty of high-rise windowsills to fall from!
trans: 有很多高楼的窗台，从那里掉下去可就危险了！

name: One cat, Sabrina, fell 32 storeys, yet only suffered from a broken tooth.
trans: 有一只名叫萨布丽娜的猫从32层楼的高度坠落，却只摔断了一颗牙齿。

name: 'Cats behave like well-trained paratroopers,' a doctor said.
trans: “猫的行为就像训练有素的伞兵一样，”一位医生说道。

name: It seems that the further cats fall, the less they are likely to injure themselves.
trans: 看起来，猫掉得越远，它们受伤的可能性就越小。

name: In a long drop, they reach speeds of 60 miles an hour and more.
trans: 在自由落体的过程中，它们的速度可以达到每小时60英里甚至更高。

name: At high speeds, falling cats have time to relax.
trans: 在高速度下落时，猫其实有时间“放松”（即它们的身体会进入一种相对稳定的状态）。

name: They stretch out their legs like flying squirrels.
trans: 他们像飞鼠一样伸开双腿。

name: This increases their air-resistance and reduces the shock of impact when they hit the ground.
trans: 这会增加它们的空气阻力，但同时也能减少它们落地时所受的冲击力。

name: The loss of the Titanic
trans: 泰坦尼克号的沉没
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: What'd have happened if only two of the 16 water-tight compartments had been flooded?
trans: 如果16个防水隔间中只有两个被水淹没，会发生什么呢？
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: The great ship, Titanic sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912.
trans: 如果那16个防水舱中只有两个被水淹没，会发生什么呢？
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: She was carrying 1, 316 passengers and a crew of 891.
trans: 她当时载有1,316名乘客和891名机组人员。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: Even by modern standards, the 46, 000 ton Titanic was a colossal ship.
trans: 这艘名为泰坦尼克号的巨轮于1912年4月10日从南安普顿启航，前往纽约。船上载有1,316名乘客和891名船员。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: At that time, however, she was not only the largest ship that had ever been built, but was regarded as unsinkable, for she had sixteen water-tight compartments.
trans: 即便以现代的标准来看，这艘重达46,000吨的巨轮也堪称庞然大物。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: Even if two of these were flooded, she would still be able to float.
trans: 在当时，它不仅是人类建造过的最大船只，还被认为“永不沉没”——因为它配备了16个防水舱，即使有两个防水舱被水淹没，船只仍能继续漂浮。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: The tragic sinking of this great liner will always be remembered, for she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life.
trans: 这艘宏伟客轮的悲剧性沉没将永远被人们铭记，因为它在首航途中就导致了大量人员伤亡。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: Four days after setting out, while the Titanic was sailing across the icy waters of the North Atlantic,
trans: 然而，这艘宏伟的邮轮的悲剧性沉没将永远被人们铭记——它在首航途中就遭遇了惨重的人员伤亡。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: a huge iceberg was suddenly spotted by a lookout.
trans: 出发四天后，当泰坦尼克号穿越北大西洋的冰冷海域时，一名瞭望员突然发现了一座巨大的冰山。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: After the alarm had been given, the great ship turned sharply to avoid a direct collision.
trans: 警报响起后，船只立即紧急转向，以避免与冰山直接碰撞。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: The Titanic turned just in time, narrowly missing the immense wall of ice which rose over 100 feet out of the water beside her.
trans: 泰坦尼克号及时改变了航向，勉强避开了那堵高达100多英尺的巨大冰墙——那冰墙就耸立在它的旁边、从水面伸出。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: Suddenly, there was a slight trembling sound from below,
trans: 突然，从下方传来了一丝轻微的震动声。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: and the captain went down to see what had happened.
trans: 船长下船去查看发生了什么。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: The noise had been so faint that no one thought that the ship had been damaged.
trans: 噪音非常微弱，以至于没有人认为那艘船受到了损坏。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: Below, the captain realized to his horror that the Titanic was sinking rapidly,
trans: 下面，船长惊恐地发现泰坦尼克号正在迅速下沉。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: for five of her sixteen watertight compartments had already been flooded!
trans: 在她那总共十六个防水舱中，已经有五个被水淹没了！
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: The order to abandon ship was given and hundreds of people plunged into the icy water.
trans: 弃船的命令被下达后，数百人纷纷跳入了冰冷的海水中。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: As there were not enough life-boats for everybody, 1, 500 lives were lost.
trans: 由于救生艇的数量不足以容纳所有人，因此有 1,500 人失去了生命。
lesson: NCE3 · The Loss of the Titanic

name: Not guilty
trans: “无罪”

name: What was the Customs Officer looking for?
trans: 海关官员在寻找什么？

name: Customs Officers are quite tolerant these days, but they can still stop you when you are going through the Green Channel and have nothing to declare.
trans: 海关官员在寻找什么呢？

name: Even really honest people are often made to feel guilty.
trans: 如今的海关官员通常比较宽容，但即便你通过绿色通道且没有任何需要申报的物品，他们仍有可能拦下你。

name: The hardened professional smuggler, on the other hand, is never troubled by such feelings,
trans: 即使是那些非常诚实的人，也常常会因此感到内疚。

name: even if he has five hundred gold watches hidden in his suitcase.
trans: 而那些老练的走私者则完全不会受到这种情绪的困扰——

name: When I returned from abroad recently, a particularly officious young Customs Officer
trans: 即使他们的行李箱里藏着五百块金表。

name: clearly regarded me as a smuggler.
trans: 最近我从国外回来时，一位特别爱管闲事的年轻海关官员明显把我当成了走私者。

name: 'Have you anything to declare?' he asked, looking me in the eye.
trans: “您有什么需要申报的吗？”他直视着我的眼睛问道。

name: 'No,' I answered confidently.
trans: “没有，”我自信地回答。

name: 'Would you mind unlocking this suitcase please? '
trans: “请您把这个行李箱打开好吗？”

name: 'Not at all,' I answered.
trans: “一点也不，”我回答道。

name: The Officer went through the case with great care.
trans: 这位警官非常仔细地审查了整个案件。

name: All the things I had packed so carefully were soon in a dreadful mess.
trans: 我精心打包的所有东西，很快就变得一片狼藉。

name: I felt sure I would never be able to close the case again.
trans: 我当时确信自己再也无法完成这个案子了。

name: Suddenly, I saw the Officer's face light up.
trans: 突然，我看到那位警官的脸上露出了笑容。

name: He had spotted a tiny bottle at the bottom of my case
trans: 他在我的行李箱底部发现了一个小瓶子。

name: and he pounced on it with delight.
trans: 他高兴地抓住了它。

name: 'Perfume, eh?' he asked sarcastically.
trans: “香水，是吗？”他讽刺地问道。

name: 'You should have declared that.
trans: 你本应该声明那一点的。

name: Perfume is not exempt from import duty.  '
trans: 香水同样需要缴纳进口关税。

name: 'But it isn't perfume, I said. 'It's hair gel.  '
trans: “但这不是香水，”我说，“这是发胶。”

name: Then I added with a smile,
trans: 然后我微笑着补充道：

name: 'It's a strange mixture I make myself.
trans: “这是我自制的某种奇怪混合物……”

name: As I expected, he did not believe me.
trans: 正如我所料，他根本不相信我的话。

name: 'Try it!' I said encouragingly.
trans: “试试看吧！”我鼓励地说道。

name: The Officer unscrewed the cap and put the bottle to his nostrils.
trans: 那位警官拧开了瓶盖，将瓶子靠近自己的鼻孔。

name: He was greeted by an unpleasant smell which convinced him that I was telling the truth.
trans: 一股难闻的气味扑面而来，这让他确信我说的是实话。

name: A few minutes later, I was able to hurry away with precious chalk marks on my baggage.
trans: 几分钟后，我终于带着行李匆匆离开了——我的行李上留下了那些珍贵的粉笔痕迹。

name: Life on a desert island
trans: 荒岛上的生活
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: What was exceptional about the two men's stay on the desert island?
trans: 这两位男士在荒岛上的经历有什么特别之处呢？
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: Most of us have formed an unrealistic picture of life on a desert island.
trans: 我们大多数人都对在荒岛上生活有着不切实际的想象。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: We sometimes imagine a desert island to be a sort of paradise where the sun always shines.
trans: 我们有时会想象，荒岛是一种天堂般的地方——那里阳光永远明媚。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: Life there is simple and good.
trans: 那里的生活简单而美好。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: Ripe fruit falls from the trees and you never have to work.
trans: 成熟的果实会从树上掉下来，你根本不需要费任何力气去采摘它们。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: The other side of the picture is quite the opposite.
trans: 事情的另一面则完全相反。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: Life on a desert island is wretched.
trans: 在荒岛上生活是非常艰苦的。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: You either starve to death or live like Robinson Crusoe, waiting for a boat which never comes.
trans: 要么你饿死；要么你像鲁滨逊·克鲁索一样孤独地生活，等待着一艘永远都不会到来的船。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: Perhaps there is an element of truth in both these pictures, but few of us have had the opportunity to find out.
trans: 也许这两张图片都包含一定的真相，但很少有人有机会去验证这一点。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: Two men who recently spent five days on a coral island wished they had stayed there longer.
trans: 两名最近在珊瑚岛上度过了五天时间的男子，希望自己能多待一段时间。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: They were taking a badly damaged boat from the Virgin Islands to Miami to have it repaired.
trans: 他们正将一艘严重损坏的船只从维尔京群岛运往迈阿密进行修理。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: During the journey, their boat began to sink.
trans: 在旅途中，他们的船开始下沉了。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: They quickly loaded a small rubber dinghy with food, matches, and cans of beer and rowed for a few miles across the Caribbean until they arrived at a tiny coral island.
trans: 他们迅速将食物、火柴和几罐啤酒装进了一艘小橡皮艇里，然后划船穿越了加勒比海，行驶了几英里，最终抵达了一个小小的珊瑚岛。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: There were hardly any trees on the island and there was no water, but this did not prove to be a problem.
trans: 岛上几乎没有树木，也没有水源，但这并没有成为什么问题。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: The men collected rainwater in the rubber dinghy.
trans: 那些人用橡胶小船收集雨水。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: As they had brought a spear gun with them, they had plenty to eat.
trans: 因为他们随身携带了一把标枪枪，所以他们有足够的食物吃。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: They caught lobster and fish every day, and as one of them put it 'ate like kings'.
trans: 他们每天都会捕到龙虾和鱼，用其中一个人的话来说：“我们吃得像国王一样丰盛。”
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: When a passing tanker rescued them five days later, both men were genuinely sorry that they had to leave.
trans: 五天后，当一艘路过的油轮救起了他们时，两名男子都真心感到遗憾——因为他们不得不离开那里。
lesson: NCE3 · Life on a Desert Island

name: 'It's only me'
trans: “只有我一个人。”

name: What did the man expect to find under the stairs?
trans: 那个男人原本期望在楼梯下面找到什么呢？

name: After her husband had gone to work, Mrs. Richards sent her children to school and went upstairs to her bedroom.
trans: 在她丈夫上班后，理查兹夫人送孩子们去了学校，然后上楼去了自己的卧室。

name: She was too excited to do any housework that morning, for in the evening she would be going to a fancy-dress party with her husband.
trans: 那天早上她兴奋得根本无心做任何家务，因为晚上她要和丈夫一起去参加一个化装舞会。

name: She intended to dress up as a ghost and as she had made her costume the night before, she was impatient to try it on.
trans: 她打算打扮成鬼的样子，由于她前一天晚上就已经做好了服装，因此迫不及待地想试穿它了。

name: Though the costume consisted only of a sheet, it was very effective.
trans: 虽然这套服装只由一块布制成，但它非常实用（或者说：它的效果非常好）。

name: After putting it on, Mrs. Richards went downstairs.
trans: 穿上它之后，理查兹夫人下楼去了。

name: She wanted to find out whether it would be comfortable to wear.
trans: 她想知道穿起来是否舒适。

name: Just as Mrs. Richards was entering the dining-room, there was a knock on the front door.
trans: 就在理查兹夫人刚走进餐厅的时候，前门突然传来了敲门声。

name: She knew that it must be the baker.
trans: 她知道，一定是那个面包师干的。

name: She had told him to come straight in if ever she failed to open the door and to leave the bread on the kitchen table.
trans: 她曾告诉他：如果她没能打开门，就直接进来，并把面包放在厨房的桌子上。

name: Not wanting to frighten the poor man, Mrs. Richards quickly hid in the small storeroom under the stairs.
trans: 为了不吓到那个可怜的老人，理查兹夫人迅速躲进了楼梯下方的小储藏室里。

name: She heard the front door open and heavy footsteps in the hall.
trans: 她听到前门被打开的声音，以及大厅里沉重的脚步声。

name: Suddenly the door of the storeroom was opened and a man entered.
trans: 突然，储藏室的门被打开了，一个男人走了进来。

name: Mrs. Richards realized that it must be the man from the Electricity Board who had come to read the metre.
trans: 理查兹夫人意识到，来读取电表数据的肯定就是电力公司的工作人员。

name: She tried to explain the situation, saying
trans: 她试图解释当时的情况，说道：

name: 'It's only me', but it was too late.
trans: “只是我一个人而已……”但为时已晚。

name: The man let out a cry and jumped back several paces.
trans: 那个男人突然大叫一声，然后向后跳了几步。

name: When Mrs. Richards walked towards him, he fled, slamming the door behind him.
trans: 当理查兹夫人朝他走去时，他立刻逃跑了，并随手关上了门。

name: A noble gangster
trans: 一位高贵的黑帮头目

name: How did Hawkwood make money in times of peace?
trans: 霍克伍德在和平时期是如何赚钱的？

name: There was a time when the owners of shops and businesses in Chicago had to pay large sums of money to gangsters in return for 'protection'.
trans: 曾经有一段时间，芝加哥的商店和企业的老板们不得不向黑帮支付巨额费用，以换取他们的“保护”。

name: If the money was not paid promptly, the gangsters would quickly put a man out of business by destroying his shop.
trans: 如果钱没有及时支付，黑帮分子会迅速毁掉他的店铺，让他破产。

name: Obtaining 'protection money' is not a modern crime.
trans: 收取“保护费”这种行为其实并非现代才有的犯罪行为。

name: As long ago as the fourteenth century, an Englishman, Sir John Hawkwood, made the remarkable discovery that people would rather pay large sums of money than have their life work destroyed by gangsters.
trans: 早在十四世纪，一位名叫约翰·霍克伍德（Sir John Hawkwood）的英国人就做出了一个惊人的发现：人们宁愿支付大笔金钱，也不愿自己的毕生心血被黑帮毁掉。

name: Six hundred years ago, Sir John Hawkwood arrived in Italy with a band of soldiers and settled near Florence.
trans: 六百年前，约翰·霍克伍德带着一队士兵来到意大利，并在佛罗伦萨附近安顿下来。

name: He soon made a name for himself and came to be known to the Italians as Giovanni Acuto.
trans: 他很快就声名鹊起，在意大利人中被称为乔瓦尼·阿库托（Giovanni Acuto）。

name: Whenever the Italian city-states were at war with each other, Hawkwood used to hire his soldiers to princes who were willing to pay the high price he demanded.
trans: 每当意大利各城邦之间发生战争时，霍克伍德就会将自己的士兵雇佣给那些愿意支付他要求的巨额费用的王子们。

name: In times of peace, when business was bad, Hawkwood and his men would march into a city-state, and after burning down a few farms, would offer to go away if protection money was paid to them.
trans: 在和平时期，当生意不景气时，霍克伍德和他的手下们会进入某个城邦，烧毁一些农场，然后提出只要支付保护费，他们就会离开。

name: Hawkwood made large sums of money in this way.
trans: 霍克伍德就是通过这种方式赚到了大量的钱。

name: In spite of this, the Italians regarded him as a sort of hero.
trans: 尽管如此，意大利人仍将他视为一位英雄。

name: When he died at the age of eighty, the Florentines gave him a state funeral and had a picture painted which was dedicated to the memory of 'the most valiant soldier and most notable leader, Signor Giovanni Haukodue'.
trans: 当他八十岁去世时，佛罗伦萨人为他举行了国葬，并委托画家创作了一幅画像，以纪念这位“最勇敢的战士、最杰出的领袖——乔瓦尼·阿库托先生”。

name: Fifty pence worth of trouble
trans: 五十便士的“代价”
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Did George get anything for his fifty pence? What?
trans: 乔治用他的五十便士买到什么了吗？什么？
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Children always appreciate small gifts of money.
trans: 孩子们总是很乐意接受小额的金钱礼物。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Mum or dad, of course, provides a regular supply of pocket money, but uncles and aunts are always a source of extra income.
trans: 当然，爸爸妈妈会定期给他们零花钱，但叔叔阿姨们也是他们额外的收入来源。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: With some children, small sums go a long way.
trans: 对一些孩子来说，这些小额的钱可以派上大用场。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: If fifty pence pieces are not exchanged for sweets, they rattle for months inside money boxes.
trans: 如果五十便士硬币没有被用来买糖果，它们就会在他们的存钱罐里“叮当作响”好几个月。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Only very thrifty children manage to fill up a money box.
trans: 只有非常节俭的孩子才能真正把存钱罐填满。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: For most of them, fifty pence is a small price to pay for a nice big bar of chocolate.
trans: 对大多数孩子来说，五十便士不过是买一块美味巧克力的小小代价罢了。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: My nephew, George, has a money box but it is always empty.
trans: 我的侄子乔治有一个存钱罐，但里面总是空空如也。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Very few of the fifty pence pieces and pound coins I have given him have found their way there.
trans: 我给他的那些五十便士硬币和一英镑硬币，几乎没有一个真正进了那个存钱罐。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: I gave him fifty pence yesterday and advised him to save it.
trans: 昨天我又给了他五十便士，并建议他要把钱存起来。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Instead, he bought himself fifty pence worth of trouble.
trans: 相反，他给自己惹来了五十便士的麻烦（或者说：他的行为让自己陷入了麻烦）。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: On his way to the sweet shop, he dropped his fifty pence and it bounced along the pavement and then disappeared down a drain.
trans: 在去糖果店的路上，他掉了那50便士硬币；硬币沿着人行道弹跳着滚去，最后掉进了下水道里不见了。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: George took off his jacket,
trans: 乔治脱下了他的夹克。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: rolled up his sleeves and pushed his right arm through the drain cover.
trans: 他卷起了袖子，然后将右臂伸进了排水口的盖子里。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: He could not find his 50 pence piece anywhere, and what is more, he could not get his arm out.
trans: 他到处都找不到那枚50便士的硬币，更糟糕的是，他甚至无法将自己的手臂伸出去。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: A crowd of people gathered round him and a lady rubbed his arm with soap and butter, but George was firmly stuck.
trans: 一群人围了上来，一位女士用肥皂和黄油擦拭他的手臂，但乔治仍然牢牢地粘在那里动弹不得。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: The fire brigade was called and two fire fighters freed George using a special type of grease.
trans: 消防队被叫来了，两名消防员使用了一种特殊的润滑剂成功救出了乔治。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: George was not too upset by his experience because the lady who owns the sweet shop heard about his troubles and rewarded him with a large box of chocolates.
trans: 乔治对他的遭遇并不太在意，因为那家糖果店的老板听说了他的麻烦后，送了他一盒大巧克力作为奖励。
lesson: NCE3 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

name: Mary had a little lamb
trans: 玛丽有一只小羊羔。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Was Dimitri right to apologize to his neighbour? Why not?
trans: 迪米特里向邻居道歉，这样做对吗？为什么不呢？
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Mary and her husband Dimitri lived in the tiny village of Perachora in southern Greece.
trans: 玛丽和她的丈夫迪米特里住在希腊南部的一个小村庄——佩拉霍拉（Perachora）。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: One of Mary's prize possessions was a little white lamb which her husband had given her.
trans: 玛丽最珍视的物品之一是一只白色的小羊羔，这是她丈夫送给她的。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: She kept it tied to a tree in a field during the day and went to fetch it every evening.
trans: 她白天把它拴在田野里的一棵树上，每晚都会去把它取回来。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: One evening, however the lamb was missing.
trans: 然而，有一天晚上，那只小羊不见了。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: The rope had been cut, so it was obvious that the lamb had been stolen.
trans: 绳子已经被剪断了，因此很明显这只小羊是被偷走了。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: When Dimitri came in from the fields, his wife told him what had happened.
trans: 当迪米特里从田里回来时，他的妻子告诉了他发生的事情。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Dimitri at once set out to find the thief.
trans: 迪米特里立刻着手寻找小偷。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: He knew it would not prove difficult in such a small village.
trans: 他知道，在这么一个小的村庄里，这件事应该不会很难解决。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: After telling several of his friends about the theft,
trans: 在向他的几个朋友讲述了这起盗窃事件之后，
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Dimitri found out that his neighbour, Aleko, had suddenly acquired a new lamb.
trans: 迪米特里发现他的邻居阿莱科突然养了一只小羊。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Dimitri immediately went to Aleko's house and angrily accused him of stealing the lamb.
trans: 迪米特里立刻去了阿列科的家，愤怒地指责他偷了那只小羊。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: He told him he had better return it or he would call the police.
trans: 他告诉他最好把东西还回来，否则他就报警。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Aleko denied taking it and led Dimitri into his backyard.
trans: 阿列科否认自己拿走了那个东西，然后带着迪米特里去了他的后院。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: It was true that he had just bought a lamb he explained, but his lamb was black.
trans: 他解释说，他确实刚买了一只小羊，不过那只小羊是黑色的。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Ashamed of having acted so rashly, Dimitri apologized to Aleko for having accused him.
trans: 由于自己的行为过于鲁莽，迪米特里向阿莱科道歉，为自己冤枉了他而感到羞愧。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: While they were talking it began to rain and Dimitri stayed in Aleko's house until the rain stopped.
trans: 他们正在谈话的时候，天开始下雨了。迪米特里便待在阿莱科的家里，直到雨停。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: When he went outside half an hour later, he was astonished to find that the little black lamb was almost white.
trans: 半小时后，当他走到外面时，惊讶地发现那只小黑羊几乎变成了白色。
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: Its wool, which had been dyed black, had been washed clean by the rain!
trans: 那块原本被染成黑色的羊毛，被雨水冲洗得干干净净了！
lesson: NCE3 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

name: The longest suspension bridge in the world
trans: 世界上最长的悬索桥
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: How is the bridge supported?
trans: 这座桥是如何被支撑起来的？
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Verrazano, an Italian about whom little is known, sailed into New York Harbour in 1524 and named it Angouleme.
trans: 维拉扎诺（Verrazano）是一位鲜为人知的意大利人。他在1524年航行至纽约港，并将其命名为“昂古莱姆”（Angouleme）。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: He described it as 'a very agreeable situation located within two small hills in the midst of which flowed a great river.'
trans: 他将其描述为“一个非常宜人的地方，位于两座小山之间；这两座小山中间流淌着一条大河。”
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Though Verrazano is by no means considered to be a great explorer, his name will probably remain immortal,
trans: 虽然韦拉扎诺绝不能被视为一位伟大的探险家，但他的名字很可能会永垂不朽。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: for on November 21st, 1964, the longest suspension bridge in the world was named after him.
trans: 因为在1964年11月21日，世界上最长的悬索桥被以他的名字命名。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: The Verrazano Bridge, which was designed by Othmar Ammann, joins Brooklyn to Staten Island.
trans: 维拉扎诺大桥（Verrazano Bridge）由奥特马尔·阿曼（Othmar Ammann）设计，它连接了布鲁克林（Brooklyn）和斯塔滕岛（Staten Island）。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: It has a span of 4, 260 feet.
trans: 它的跨度为 4,260 英尺。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: The bridge is so long that the shape of the earth had to be taken into account by its designer.
trans: 这座桥非常长，以至于设计者在建造时必须考虑到地球的曲率（即地球的球形形状）。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Two great towers support four huge cables.
trans: 两座高大的塔架支撑着四根巨大的缆绳。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: The towers are built on immense underwater platforms made of steel and concrete.
trans: 这些塔楼建在巨大的水下平台上，这些平台由钢铁和混凝土制成。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: The platforms extend to a depth of over 100 feet under the sea.
trans: 这些平台延伸至海面下100英尺以上的深度。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: These alone took sixteen months to build.
trans: 仅这些部分的建设就花费了十六个月的时间。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Above the surface of the water, the towers rise to a height of nearly 700 feet.
trans: 在水面之上，这些塔楼的高度接近700英尺。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: They support the cables from which the bridge has been suspended.
trans: 这些结构用于支撑桥梁所悬挂的缆绳。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Each of the four cables contains 26, 108 lengths of wire.
trans: 这四根电缆中的每一根都包含 26 × 108 根电线。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: It has been estimated that if the bridge were packed with cars, it would still only be carrying a third of its total capacity.
trans: 据估计，即使这座桥上挤满了汽车，它所承载的重量也仅相当于其总承载能力的三分之一。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: However, size and strength are not the only important things about this bridge.
trans: 然而，这座桥的重要性并不仅仅体现在它的规模和承重能力上。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Despite its immensity, it is both simple and elegant,
trans: 尽管它规模庞大，但它却既简洁又优雅。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: fulfilling its designer's dream to creat 'an enormous object drawn as faintly as possible'.
trans: 实现了设计师的梦想：创作出一个“尽可能纤细、轮廓模糊的巨大物体”。
lesson: NCE3 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World

name: Electric currents in modern art
trans: 现代艺术中的电流（注：此处“electric currents”可能为比喻，实际含义需结合上下文确定）
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: How might some of the exhibits have been dangerous?
trans: 有些展品为什么会具有危险性呢？
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Modern sculpture rarely surprises us any more.
trans: 有些展品为何可能具有危险性？
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
trans: 现代雕塑早已不再让我们感到惊讶。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
trans: 认为现代艺术只能通过博物馆来欣赏，这种观点是错误的。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Strange forms stand in gardens, and outside buildings and shops.
trans: 即使是对艺术毫无兴趣的人，也应该注意到公共场所中展示的现代雕塑作品——那些奇形怪状的雕塑矗立在花园里、建筑物和商店的外面。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: We have got quite used to them.
trans: 我们已经习惯了它们的存在。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
trans: 有些所谓的“现代”艺术品已经展出了近八十年。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: In spite of this, some people--including myself--were surprised by a recent exhibition of modern sculpture.
trans: 尽管如此，包括我在内的一些人，还是被最近的一场现代雕塑展览所震撼。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: The first thing I saw when I entered the art gallery was a notice which said: 'Do not touch the exhibits, some of them are dangerous!'
trans: 当我走进艺术画廊时，首先看到的是一张告示，上面写着：“请勿触摸展品，其中一些具有危险性！”
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: The objects on display were pieces of moving sculpture.
trans: 展出的作品都是可以移动的雕塑。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Oddly shaped forms that are suspended from the ceiling and move in response to a gust of wind are quite familiar to everybody.
trans: 那些形状奇特、悬挂在天花板上的物体，会随着一阵风吹动而移动——这种景象对每个人来说都十分熟悉。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: These objects, however, were different.
trans: 然而，这些物体有所不同。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Lined up against the wall, there were long thin wires attached to metal spheres.
trans: 他们被排成一列，靠在墙上；每根细长的金属丝都连接着一个金属球。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: The spheres had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
trans: 这些球体被磁化了，因此它们会不断地相互吸引或相互排斥。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: In the centre of the hall,
trans: 在大厅的中央，
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: there were a number of tall structures which contained coloured lights.
trans: 有许多高大的建筑物，这些建筑物上装有彩色的灯光。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: These lights flickered continuously like traffic lights which have gone mad.
trans: 这些灯光不停地闪烁，就像那些失控的交通信号灯一样。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes and red lamps flashed on and off angrily.
trans: 从小巧的黑色盒子中迸发出火花；红色的灯笼则愤怒地闪烁着（即灯笼的颜色不断变红、变暗）。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: It was rather like an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment.
trans: 这有点像一场展示史前电子设备的展览。
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: These peculiar forms not only seemed designed to shock people emotionally, but to give them electric shocks as well!
trans: 这些奇特的设计不仅旨在从情感上震撼人们，还似乎能够给他们带来电击般的刺激！
lesson: NCE3 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

name: A very dear cat
trans: 一只非常珍贵的猫

name: Why was Rastus 'very dear' in more ways than one?
trans: 为什么拉斯特斯在很多方面都“非常特别”（或者说“非常珍贵”）呢？

name: Kidnappers are rarely interested in animals, but they recently took considerable interest in Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay's cat.
trans: 为什么拉斯特斯在很多方面都“非常珍贵”呢？

name: Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay, a very wealthy old lady, has shared a flat with her cat, Rastus, for a great many years.
trans: 埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人是一位非常富有的老太太，她多年来一直和她的猫拉斯图斯合住一套公寓。

name: Rastus leads an orderly life.
trans: 绑匪通常对动物不感兴趣，但他们最近却对埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人的猫产生了浓厚的兴趣。

name: He usually takes a short walk in the evenings and is always home by seven o'clock.
trans: 埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人是一位非常富有的老太太，多年来她一直和她的猫拉斯特斯共同居住在一套公寓里。

name: One evening, however he failed to arrive.
trans: 拉斯特斯的生活非常有条理：他每天晚上都会去散散步，总是在七点前回家。

name: Mrs. Ramsay got very worried.
trans: 然而有一天晚上，他却没有按时回家。

name: She looked everywhere for him but could not find him.
trans: 拉姆齐夫人非常担心，她到处寻找拉斯特斯，却始终找不到他。

name: Three days after Rastus' disappearance, Mrs. Ramsay received an anonymous letter.
trans: 在拉斯特斯失踪三天后，她收到了一封匿名信。

name: The writer stated that Rastus was in safe hands and would be returned immediately if Mrs. Ramsay paid a ransom of ￡1, 000.
trans: 信中写道，拉斯特斯现在安全无恙，但如果她支付1000英镑的赎金，拉斯特斯就会立刻被归还。

name: Mrs.Ramsay was instructed to place the money in a cardboard box and to leave it outside her door.
trans: 拉姆齐夫人被告知要把钱放在一个纸板箱里，然后放在她家门外。

name: At first, she decided to go to the police,
trans: 起初，她决定报警，

name: but fearing that she would never see Rastus again--the letter had made that quite clear--she changed her mind.
trans: 但想到可能再也见不到拉斯特斯了——信里已经明确说明了这一点——她改变了主意。

name: She withdrew ￡1000 from her bank and followed the kidnapper's instructions.
trans: 她从银行取出了1000英镑，然后照绑匪的指示行事。

name: The next morning, the box had disappeared but Mrs.Ramsay was sure that the kidnapper would keep his word.
trans: 第二天早上，那个纸板箱不见了，不过拉姆齐夫人确信绑匪会遵守他的承诺。

name: Sure enough, Rastus arrived punctually at seven o'clock that evening.
trans: 果然，拉斯特斯在当晚七点准时出现了。

name: He looked very well, though he was rather thirsty, for he drank half a bottle of milk.
trans: 他看起来状态很好，只是有点渴，因为他喝了一半瓶牛奶。

name: The police were astounded when Mrs. Ramsay told them what she had done.
trans: 当拉姆齐夫人向警方讲述自己的所作所为时，他们感到非常惊讶。

name: She explained that Rastus was very dear to her.
trans: 她解释说，拉斯特斯对她来说非常珍贵；

name: Considering the amount she paid, he was dear in more ways than one!
trans: 考虑到她付出的代价，他的价值远不止金钱那么简单……

name: Pioneer pilots
trans: 先锋飞行员

name: What was the name of the first plane to fly across the English Channel?
trans: 第一架飞越英吉利海峡的飞机叫什么名字？

name: In 1908 Lord Northcliffe offered a prize of ￡1, 000 to the first man who would fly across the English Channel.
trans: 1908年，诺斯克利夫勋爵（Lord Northcliffe）宣布设立一项奖金，金额为1,000英镑，奖励第一个成功飞越英吉利海峡的人。

name: Over a year passed before the first attempt was made.
trans: 过了整整一年，才有人第一次尝试去做这件事。

name: On July 19th, 1909, in the early morning,
trans: 1909年7月19日，清晨时分……

name: Hubert Latham took off from the French coast in his plane the 'Antoinette IV.'
trans: 休伯特·拉瑟姆驾驶他的飞机“安托瓦内特IV号”从法国海岸起飞了。

name: He had travelled only seven miles across the Channel when his engine failed and he was forced to land on the sea.
trans: 他刚刚飞越英吉利海峡七英里，引擎就发生了故障，他不得不迫降在海面上。

name: The 'Antoinette' floated on the water until Latham was picked up by a ship.
trans: “安托瓦内特”号漂浮在水面上，直到拉瑟姆被一艘船救起。

name: Two days later, Louis Bleriot arrived near Calais with a plane called 'No.XI'.
trans: 两天后，路易·布莱里奥驾驶着一架名为“No.XI”的飞机抵达了加莱附近。

name: Bleriot had been making planes since 1905 and this was his latest model.
trans: 布莱里奥自1905年起就开始制造飞机，而这架飞机是他最新的设计作品。

name: A week before, he had completed a successful overland flight during which he covered twenty-six miles.
trans: 一周前，他完成了一次成功的陆上飞行，飞行距离达到了26英里。

name: Latham, however, did not give up easily.
trans: 然而，拉瑟姆并没有轻易放弃。

name: He, too, arrived near Calais on the same day with a new 'Antoinette'.
trans: 他也在同一天，乘坐一艘新的“Antoinette”号船只，抵达了加莱附近。

name: It looked as if there would be an exciting race across the Channel.
trans: 看起来将会有一场跨越英吉利海峡的精彩比赛。

name: Both planes were going to take off on July 25th, but Latham failed to get up early enough.
trans: 这两架飞机都原定于7月25日起飞，但拉瑟姆没能早起。

name: After making a short test flight at 4.15 a.m., Bleriot set off half an hour later.
trans: 在凌晨4点15分进行了一次短暂的试飞后，布莱里奥于半小时后再次起飞了。

name: His great flight lasted thirty-seven minutes.
trans: 他的这次精彩飞行持续了三十七分钟。

name: When he landed near Dover, the first person to greet him was a local policeman.
trans: 当他降落在多佛附近时，第一个迎接他的是一名当地警察。

name: Latham made another attempt a week later and got within half a mile of Dover,
trans: 一周后，拉瑟姆再次尝试前进，最终距离多佛仅剩下半英里之遥。

name: but he was unlucky again.
trans: 但他又一次运气不佳了。

name: His engine failed and he landed on the sea for the second time.
trans: 他的引擎发生了故障，他第二次坠入了大海。

name: Daniel Mendoza
trans: 丹尼尔·门多萨

name: How many unsuccessful attempts did Mendoza make before becoming Champion of all England?
trans: 门多萨在成为全英格兰冠军之前，失败了多少次？

name: Boxing matches were very popular in England two hundred years ago.
trans: 两百年前，拳击比赛在英格兰非常流行。

name: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.
trans: 在那个时候，拳击手们为了奖金而徒手搏斗。

name: Because of this, they were known as 'prizefighters'.
trans: 正因如此，他们被称为“格斗选手”（prizefighters）。

name: However, boxing was very crude,
trans: 然而，当时的拳击运动还非常原始、不成熟（或者说技术非常粗糙）。

name: for there were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
trans: 因为当时没有任何规则可言，拳击手在比赛中很可能会受到严重伤害，甚至丧命。

name: One of the most colourful figures in boxing history was Daniel Mendoza, who was born in 1764.
trans: 拳击历史上最富有传奇色彩的人物之一是丹尼尔·门多萨（Daniel Mendoza），他出生于1764年。

name: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
trans: 手套的使用直到1860年才被引入；那一年，昆斯贝里侯爵制定了第一套比赛规则。

name: Though he was technically a prizefighter,
trans: 虽然从技术层面讲他是一名职业拳击手，

name: Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport, for he brought science to the game.
trans: 门多萨为将这种原始的斗殴比赛转变为一项真正的体育运动做出了巨大贡献；因为他为这项运动引入了科学化的训练方法与管理理念。

name: In his day, Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity.
trans: 在蒙德萨的时代，他享有极高的声望和广泛的知名度。

name: He was adored by rich and poor alike.
trans: 无论贫富，大家都非常喜爱他。

name: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
trans: 门多萨在十四岁参加了一场拳击比赛后，迅速走红了。

name: This attracted the attention of Richard Humphries who was then the most eminent boxer in England.
trans: 这引起了理查德·汉弗莱斯（Richard Humphries）的注意，他当时是英格兰最著名的拳击手。

name: He offered to train Mendoza and his young pupil was quick to learn.
trans: 他主动提出指导门多萨，而门多萨这个年轻的学生学习能力非常强，进步很快。

name: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.
trans: 事实上，门多萨很快就取得了巨大的成功，以至于汉弗莱斯转而与他为敌。

name: The two men quarrelled bitterly and it was clear that the argument could only be settled by a fight.
trans: 这两个人激烈地争吵起来，很明显，这场争执只能通过打架来解决。

name: A match was held at Stilton, where both men fought for an hour.
trans: 比赛在斯蒂尔顿举行，两名选手激烈交锋了一个小时。

name: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza, but he was defeated.
trans: 公众在门多萨身上投入了大量资金，但他最终还是失败了。

name: Mendoza met Humphries in the ring on a later occasion and he lost for a second time.
trans: 后来，门多萨在擂台上与汉弗莱斯再次交锋，结果再次落败。

name: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries and became Champion of England.
trans: 直到 1790 年的第三场比赛中，他才终于击败了汉弗莱斯，成为了英格兰冠军。

name: Meanwhile, he founded a highly successful Academy and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils.
trans: 与此同时，他创办了一所非常成功的学院，甚至连拜伦勋爵也成为了他的学生之一。

name: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as ￡100 for a single appearance.
trans: 他赚了巨额财富，单次出场就能获得高达100英镑的报酬。

name: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
trans: 然而，他生活极其奢侈，因此总是负债累累。

name: After he was defeated by a boxer called Gentleman Jackson, he was quickly forgotten.
trans: 在被一位名叫“绅士杰克逊”的拳击手击败后，他很快就被人们遗忘了。

name: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
trans: 由于未能偿还债务，他锒铛入狱，并于1836年在贫困中去世。

name: By heart
trans: 牢记在心；熟记

name: Which actor read the letter in the end, the aristocrat or the gaoler?
trans: 最后是谁读了那封信——是那位贵族，还是狱卒？

name: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
trans: 有些剧目非常成功，以至于可以连续上演多年。

name: In many ways, this is unfortunate for the poor actors who are required to go on repeating the same lines night after night.
trans: 在很多方面，这对那些可怜的演员来说确实很不公平——他们不得不夜复一夜地重复同样的台词。

name: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
trans: 人们会认为他们应该对各自的职责了如指掌，因此永远不会有出错的机会。

name: Yet this is not always the case.
trans: 然而，情况并不总是如此。

name: A famous actor in a highly successful play was once cast in the role of an aristocrat who had been imprisoned in the Bastille for twenty years.
trans: 一位在非常成功的戏剧中表现出色的著名演员，曾饰演过这样一个角色：一位被关押在巴士底狱长达二十年的贵族。

name: In the last act, a gaoler would always come on to the stage with a letter which he would hand to the prisoner.
trans: 在最后一幕中，总是会有一个狱卒走上舞台，递给囚犯一封信。

name: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
trans: 尽管人们期望这位贵族在每次演出时都能宣读这封信，但他始终坚持要求必须将这封信完整地写出来（即不能只是口头朗读，而必须以书面形式呈现）。

name: One night, the gaoler decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if,
trans: 一天晚上，狱卒决定捉弄他的同事，想看看对方是否……

name: after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
trans: 经过这么多次表演后，他已经能够将那封信的内容牢记在心了。

name: The curtain went up on the final act of the play and revealed the aristocrat sitting alone behind bars in his dark cell.
trans: 戏剧的最后一幕开始了：那位贵族独自坐在黑暗的牢房里，被关在铁栅栏后面。

name: Just then, the gaoler appeared with the precious letter in his hands.
trans: 就在这时，狱卒出现了，他手里拿着那封珍贵的信。

name: He entered the cell and presented the letter to the aristocrat.
trans: 他走进牢房，将那封信交给了那位贵族。

name: But the copy he gave him had not been written out in full as usual.
trans: 但他交给对方的那份副本并没有像往常一样被完整地写出来（即：副本中的内容并不完整）。

name: It was simply a blank sheet of paper.
trans: 那只是一张空白的纸而已。

name: The gaoler looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learnt his lines.
trans: 狱卒急切地观看着，渴望看到他的“搭档演员”是否终于记住了自己的台词。

name: The noble stared at the blank sheet of paper for a few seconds.
trans: 那位贵族盯着那张空白的纸张看了几秒钟。

name: Then, squinting his eyes, he said: 'The light is dim. Read the letter to me.'
trans: 然后，他眯起眼睛说：“光线太暗了。把那封信读给我听吧。”

name: And he promptly handed the sheet of paper to the gaoler.
trans: 然后他立刻把那张纸交给了狱卒。

name: Finding that he could not remember a word of the letter either,
trans: 结果发现，他也完全想不起来那封信里写了什么内容。

name: the gaoler replied: 'The light is indeed dim, sire.  I must get my glasses.  '
trans: 狱卒回答说：“光线确实很暗，大人。我得去拿我的眼镜。”

name: With this, he hurried off the stage.
trans: 说完这些，他便匆忙走下了舞台。

name: Much to the aristocrat's amusement,
trans: 令那位贵族感到十分有趣的是……

name: the gaoler returned a few moments later with a pair of glasses and the usual copy of the letter which he proceeded to read to the prisoner.
trans: 过了一会儿，狱卒拿着一副眼镜和那封熟悉的信回来了，然后开始把信的内容读给囚犯听。

name: One man's meat is another man's poison
trans: 对一个人来说可能是美味的食物，对另一个人来说可能就是毒药。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: What was it about snails that made the writer collect them for his friend on that day in particular?
trans: 究竟是蜗牛的什么特性，让作者在那天特意为他的朋友收集了它们呢？
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten and what cannot be eaten.
trans: 当人们试图决定哪些食物可以食用、哪些不可以食用时，他们的思维往往会变得非常不合逻辑（即：他们的判断标准变得混乱、不合理）。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: If you lived in the Mediterranean, for instance, you would consider octopus a great delicacy.
trans: 例如，如果你生活在地中海地区，你会认为章鱼是一种非常美味的佳肴。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: You would not be able to understand why some people find it repulsive.
trans: 你可能无法理解为什么有些人会觉得某些事物令人反感（或令人厌恶）。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat-the normally accepted practice in many northern countries.
trans: 另一方面，一想到要用动物油脂来煎土豆，你就会感到恶心——而在许多北方国家，这种做法却是被普遍接受的。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.
trans: 令人遗憾的事实是，我们大多数人都被教导要吃某些特定的食物，并且一生都坚持吃这些食物。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.
trans: 没有哪种生物像普通的花园蜗牛那样同时受到过如此多的赞美和批评（或：没有哪种生物像花园蜗牛一样，既受到过极高的赞誉，也遭受过大量的批评）。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: Cooked in wine, snails are a great luxury in various parts of the world.
trans: 用葡萄酒烹制的蜗牛，在世界各地都被视为一种高级的美食。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
trans: 有无数的人，从很小的时候起，就学会了将蜗牛与食物联系在一起。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: My friend, Robert, lives in a country where snails are despised.
trans: 我的朋友罗伯特住在一个人们非常厌恶蜗牛的国家。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: As his flat is in a large town, he has no garden of his own.
trans: 由于他的公寓位于一个较大的城镇里，所以他并没有自己的花园。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: For years he has been asking me to collect snails from my garden and take them to him.
trans: 多年来，他一直让我从我的花园里采集蜗牛，然后带给他。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day, after a heavy shower,
trans: 这个想法我一直不太感兴趣，但有一天，在一场大雨之后……
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prize plants.
trans: 我正好在花园里散步，突然发现大量的蜗牛正在我的那些珍贵的植物上爬来爬去。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.
trans: 一时冲动之下，我收集了几十件物品，把它们装进一个纸袋里，然后拿给了罗伯特。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
trans: 罗伯特见到我非常高兴，对我的小礼物也同样感到满意。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: I left the bag in the hall and Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.
trans: 我把包忘在走廊里了，然后我和罗伯特一起进了客厅，在那里我们聊了几个小时。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.
trans: 我完全把那些蜗牛的事给忘了，直到罗伯特突然说：“你必须留下来吃晚饭。”
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: Snails would, of course, be the main dish.
trans: 当然，蜗牛会是主菜。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: I did not fancy the idea and I reluctantly followed Robert out of the room.
trans: 我并不喜欢这个主意，但还是不情愿地跟着罗伯特走出了房间。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: To our dismay,
trans: 令我们失望的是……
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: we saw that there were snails everywhere:
trans: 我们发现到处都有蜗牛。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: they had escaped from the paper bag
trans: 他们从那个纸袋里逃出来了。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: and had taken complete possession of the hall! I have never be able to look at a snail since then.
trans: 他们完全控制了那个大厅！从那以后，我再也不敢看蜗牛了。
lesson: NCE3 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison

name: A skeleton in the cupboard
trans: （用于形容家里或某人身上隐藏的、不愿被人知道的丑事或秘密）柜子里的一具骷髅（比喻令人不快或尴尬的秘密）
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: Who was Sebastian?
trans: 塞巴斯蒂安是谁？
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: We often read in novels how a seemingly respectable person
trans: 我们在小说中经常看到这样的情节：一个表面上看起来很体面、值得尊敬的人……
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: or family has some terrible secret which has been concealed from strangers for years.
trans: 或者这个家庭隐藏着一个可怕的秘密，这个秘密多年来一直被对外人隐瞒着。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: The English language possesses a vivid saying to describe this sort of situation.
trans: 英语中有一句非常生动的表达，用来形容这种情况。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: The terrible secret is called 'a skeleton in the cupboard'.
trans: 这个可怕的秘密被称作“柜子里的骷髅”（即一个令人不寒而栗的秘密）。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: At some dramatic moment in the story, the terrible secret becomes known and a reputation is ruined.
trans: 在故事中的某个关键时刻，那个可怕的秘密被揭露了，从而导致一个人的声誉彻底毁掉。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: The reader's hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine,
trans: 当读者读到小说的最后几页时，会发现女主角……（这里的“that the heroine”后面应该有具体的描述或情节，但原文被省略了。）
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: a dear old lady who had always been so kind to everybody, had, in her youth, poisoned every one of her five husbands.
trans: 一位一直对所有人都非常友善的善良老妇人，在她年轻时，竟然毒死了她的五位丈夫。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
trans: 这类事情发生在小说里固然没什么问题（即：小说中描绘这类情节是完全可以接受的）。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn,
trans: 在某种程度上，我们每个人都有自己不想让最亲密的朋友知道的秘密。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: but few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
trans: 但只有少数人真正有不可告人的秘密（或不堪回首的过去）。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton, and he is very proud of the fact.
trans: 我认识的唯一一个有“不可告人秘密”的人是乔治·卡尔顿，而他对此感到非常自豪。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: George studied medicine in his youth.
trans: 乔治年轻时学习过医学。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: Instead of becoming a doctor, however, he became a successful writer of detective stories.
trans: 然而，他并没有成为医生，而是成为了一名成功的侦探小说作家。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: I once spent an uncomfortable weekend which I shall never forget at his house.
trans: 我曾在他的家里度过了一个极其不愉快的周末，那个经历我永远都不会忘记。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: George showed me to the guestroom which, he said, was rarely used.
trans: 乔治带我去了客房，他说这个房间很少有人使用。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: He told me to unpack my things and then come down to dinner.
trans: 他让我先把行李收拾好，然后再下来吃晚饭。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: After I had stacked my shirts and underclothes in two empty drawers, I decided to hang one of the two suits I had brought with me in the cupboard.
trans: 我把衬衫和内衣整理好后，放进了两个空抽屉里；接着，我决定把带来的两套西装中的一套挂在衣柜里。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: I opened the cupboard door and then stood in front of it petrified.
trans: 我打开了橱柜的门，然后站在那里，吓得动弹不得。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: A skeleton was dangling before my eyes.
trans: 一具骷髅悬挂在我的眼前。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
trans: 门突然移动了一下，导致它轻微地摇晃起来；这让我觉得门仿佛随时都会朝我扑过来一样。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: Dropping my suit, I dashed downstairs to tell George.
trans: 我立刻放下西装，冲下楼去告诉乔治。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: This was worse than 'a terrible secret'; this was a real skeleton!
trans: 这比“一个可怕的秘密”还要糟糕；那简直是一具真正的骷髅！
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: But George was unsympathetic.
trans: 但乔治却毫无同情之心。
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: 'Oh, that,' he said with a smile as if he were talking about an old friend.
trans: “哦，那个啊，”他笑着说，仿佛在谈论一个老朋友一样，
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: 'That's Sebastian. You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time.'
trans: “那是塞巴斯蒂安。你忘了，我曾经也是一名医学生。”
lesson: NCE3 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

name: The Cutty Sark
trans: “Cutty Sark”是一艘著名的帆船，以其独特的船型和卓越的航海性能而闻名于世。

name: What piece of bad luck prevented the Cutty Sark from winning the race?
trans: 是什么倒霉的事情导致“Cutty Sark”号没能赢得这场比赛呢？

name: One of the most famous sailing ships of the nineteenth century, the Cutty Sark, can still be seen at Greenwich.
trans: 作为19世纪最著名的帆船之一，“Cutty Sark”至今仍可以在格林尼治博物馆看到。

name: She stands on dry land and is visited by thousands of people each year.
trans: 她站在陆地上，每年都有成千上万的人前来参观她。

name: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
trans: 她仿佛是一面令人印象深刻的镜子，让人们想起过去那些宏伟的船只。

name: Before they were replaced by steamships,
trans: 在它们被蒸汽船取代之前，

name: sailing vessels like the Cutty Sark were used to carry tea from China and wool from Australia.
trans: 像“Cutty Sark”这样的帆船曾被用来从中国运输茶叶，从澳大利亚运输羊毛。

name: The Cutty Sark was one of the fastest sailing ships that has ever been built.
trans: “Cutty Sark”是有史以来建造的最快的帆船之一。

name: The only other ship to match her was the Thermopylae.
trans: 唯一能与她相媲美的船只就是“Thermopylae”号了。

name: Both these ships set out from Shanghai on June 18th, 1872 on an exciting race to England.
trans: 这两艘船都于1872年6月18日从上海出发，参加了一场前往英国的激动人心的竞赛。

name: This race, which went on for exactly four months, was the last of its kind.
trans: 这场比赛持续了整整四个月，也是这类比赛中的最后一场比赛。

name: It marked the end of the great tradition of ships with sails and the beginning of a new era.
trans: 这标志着帆船这一伟大传统的终结，以及一个新时代的开始。

name: The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae,
trans: 在比赛开始后，最先抵达爪哇的两艘船只中，第一艘是“Thermopylae”号。

name: but on the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took the lead.
trans: 但在印度洋上，库蒂·萨克号（Cutty Sark）却取得了领先地位。

name: It seemed certain that she would be the first ship home,
trans: 看起来她肯定会成为第一个返回家的“船只”（即第一个完成任务的成员）。

name: but during the race she had a lot of bad luck.
trans: 但在比赛中，她遭遇了很多不幸（或者说：她遇到了很多麻烦或困难）。

name: In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm during which her rudder was torn away.
trans: 八月份，她遭遇了一场猛烈的风暴，风暴中她的舵被彻底损坏（即被风暴中的力量扯掉了）。

name: The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side and it became impossible to steer her.
trans: “Cutty Sark”号开始左右摇晃，根本无法再控制它的航向了。

name: A temporary rudder was made on board from spare planks and it was fitted with great difficulty.
trans: 他们在船上用多余的木板制作了一个临时舵，并且安装这个临时舵的过程非常困难。

name: This greatly reduced the speed of the ship, for there was a danger that if she travelled too quickly,
trans: 这大大降低了船的速度，因为如果船行驶得太快，就存在危险。

name: this rudder would be torn away as well.
trans: 这个舵也会被扯掉的。

name: Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
trans: 正因如此，Cutty Sark失去了领先优势。

name: After crossing the Equator, the captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted,
trans: 在越过赤道后，船长停靠在一个港口，更换了船上的舵。

name: but by now the Thermopylae was over five hundred miles ahead.
trans: 但那时，Thermopylae号已经领先了五百多英里。

name: Though the new rudder was fitted at tremendous speed, it was impossible for the Cutty Sark to win.
trans: 尽管新的舵被迅速安装上了，Cutty Sark号还是无法赶上它。

name: She arrived in England a week after the Thermopylae.
trans: Cutty Sark号在Thermopylae号之后一周才抵达英格兰。

name: Even this was remarkable, considering that she had had so many delays.
trans: 考虑到途中经历了许多延误，这一成绩已经非常了不起了。

name: There is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder she would have won the race easily.
trans: 毫无疑问，如果她没有失去舵，她本可以轻松赢得比赛。

name: Wanted: a large biscuit tin
trans: 所需物品：一个大号的饼干盒
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: Who won the prize for the biggest biscuit?
trans: 谁赢得了“最大饼干”奖呢？
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: No one can avoid being influenced by advertisements.
trans: 没有人能够完全不受广告的影响。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: Much as we may pride ourselves on our good taste,
trans: 尽管我们常常为自己的品味感到自豪，
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: we are no longer free to choose the things we want,
trans: 但实际上我们已不再能够自由选择自己真正想要的东西，
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: for advertising exerts a subtle influence on us.
trans: 因为广告对我们产生了潜移默化的影响。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: In their efforts to persuade us to buy this or that product,
trans: 为了说服我们购买某种产品，
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: advertisers have made a close study of human nature and have classified all our little weaknesses.
trans: 广告商们深入研究了人类的心理，并掌握了我们所有的弱点。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: Advertisers discovered years ago that all of us love to get something for nothing.
trans: 多年前，广告商们就发现：我们都喜欢免费获得东西。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: An advertisement which begins with the magic word FREE can rarely go wrong.
trans: 任何以“免费”这个词开头的广告几乎都不会失败。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: These days, advertisers not only offer free samples,
trans: 如今，广告商们不仅提供免费样品，……
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: but free cars, free houses, and free trips round the world as well.
trans: 还有免费的汽车、免费的房子，以及免费的环球旅行机会。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: They devise hundreds of competitions which will enable us to win huge sums of money.
trans: 他们设计了数百种比赛，这些比赛将帮助我们赢得巨额奖金。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: Radio and television have made it possible for advertisers to capture the attention of millions of people in this way.
trans: 广播和电视使得广告商能够以这种方式吸引数百万人的注意力。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: During a radio programme, a company of biscuit manufacturers once asked listeners to bake biscuits and send them to their factory.
trans: 在一次广播节目中，一家饼干制造商公司邀请听众们自己制作饼干，然后把制作好的饼干寄送到他们的工厂。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: They offered to pay $10 a pound for the biggest biscuit baked by a listener.
trans: 他们提出愿意以每磅10美元的价格购买听众们烤制的最大尺寸的饼干。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: The response to this competition was tremendous.
trans: 这次比赛的反响非常热烈（或：这次比赛的响应非常强烈）。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: Before long, biscuits of all shapes and sizes began arriving at the factory.
trans: 不久之后，各种形状和大小的饼干开始运送到工厂里。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: One lady brought biscuit on a wheelbarrow. It weighed nearly 500 pounds.
trans: 一位女士用手推车运送了那些饼干；这些饼干的总重量接近500磅。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: A little later, a man came along with a biscuit which occupied the whole boot of his car.
trans: 过了一会儿，一个男人走了过来，他带来的饼干占据了他汽车整个后备箱的空间。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: All the biscuits that were sent were carefully weighed.
trans: 所有被寄出的饼干都经过了仔细的称重。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: The largest was 713 pounds. It seemed certain that this would win the prize.
trans: 最大的那个重达713磅；看起来它肯定会赢得这个奖项。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: But just before the competition closed,
trans: 但在比赛即将结束之前，
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: a lorry arrived at the factory with a truly colossal biscuit which weighed 2, 400 pounds.
trans: 一辆卡车将一块重量高达2,400磅的巨型饼干送到了工厂。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: It had been baked by a college student who had used over 1, 000 pounds of flour, 800 pounds of sugar,
trans: 这面包是由一名大学生制作的；他使用了超过1000磅的面粉和800磅的糖。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: 200 pounds of fat, and 400 pounds of various other ingredients.
trans: 200磅的脂肪，以及400磅的其他各种成分。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: It was so heavy that a crane had to be used to remove it from the lorry.
trans: 它太重了，必须使用起重机才能将其从卡车上卸下来。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: The manufacturers had to pay more money than they had anticipated, for they bought the biscuit from the student for $24, 000.
trans: 制造商们不得不支付比预期更多的费用，因为他们以 24,000 美元的价格从那位学生手中买下了这些饼干。
lesson: NCE3 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

name: Nothing to sell and nothing to buy
trans: 没有什么可以卖的，也没有什么可以买的。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: What is the most important thing for a tramp?
trans: 对于一个流浪者来说，最重要的是什么？
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: It has been said that everyone lives by selling something.
trans: 有人说过，每个人都是通过出售某种东西来谋生的。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: In the light of this statement, teachers live by selling knowledge,
trans: 根据这一说法，教师的工作就是通过传授知识来谋生。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: philosophers by selling wisdom and priests by selling spiritual comfort.
trans: 哲学家通过传授智慧来谋生，而牧师则通过提供精神慰藉来获得收入。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: Though it may be possible to measure the value of material goods in terms of money,
trans: 虽然可以用金钱来衡量物质财富的价值，
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: it is extremely difficult to estimate the true value of the services which people perform for us.
trans: 很难准确估计人们为我们提供的服务的真正价值。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: There are times when we would willingly give everything we possess to save our lives,
trans: 有时候，为了挽救自己的生命，我们甚至愿意放弃自己拥有的一切。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: yet we might grudge paying a surgeon a high fee for offering us precisely this service.
trans: 然而，我们可能会不愿意为外科医生支付高额的费用，仅仅因为他们为我们提供了这项服务。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: The conditions of society are such that skills have to be paid for in the same way that goods are paid for at a shop.
trans: 当前的社会状况决定了：技能的价值必须像商品在商店里被出售时那样，通过金钱来体现（即技能也需要通过金钱来获得）。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: Everyone has something to sell.
trans: 每个人都有东西可以出售。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: Tramps seem to be the only exception to this general rule.
trans: 流浪汉似乎是这条普遍规则的唯一例外。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: Beggars almost sell themselves as human beings to arouse the pity of passers-by.
trans: 乞丐们几乎是在“出卖自己的人格”，以激起路人的同情心。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: But real tramps are not beggars.
trans: 但是，真正的流浪者并不是乞丐。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: They have nothing to sell and require nothing from others.
trans: 他们没有什么可以出售的，也不需要从别人那里得到任何东西。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: In seeking independence, they do not sacrifice their human dignity.
trans: 在追求独立的过程中，他们并没有牺牲自己的人格尊严。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: A tramp may ask you for money, but he will never ask you to feel sorry for him.
trans: 一个流浪汉可能会向你乞讨钱财，但他永远不会要求你同情他。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: He has deliberately chosen to lead the life he leads and is fully aware of the consequences.
trans: 他自己是主动选择了这样的生活方式，并且完全清楚这样做会带来什么样的后果。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: He may never be sure where the next meal is coming from,
trans: 他可能永远都无法确定下一顿饭从哪里来（也就是说，他可能永远不知道自己下一顿饭的食物来源或来源地）。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: but he is free from the thousands of anxieties which afflict other people.
trans: 但他摆脱了那些困扰其他人的成千上万种焦虑情绪。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: His few material possessions make it possible for him to move from place to place with ease.
trans: 他仅有的一些物质财富使他能够轻松地从一个地方搬到另一个地方。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: By having to sleep in the open, he gets far closer to the world of nature than most of us ever do.
trans: 由于不得不在户外露宿，他比我们大多数人更接近大自然的世界。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: He may hunt, beg, or steal occasionally to keep himself alive;
trans: 他可能会偶尔通过打猎、乞讨或偷窃来维持生计。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: he may even, in times of real need, do a little work; but he will never sacrifice his freedom.
trans: 在真正需要的时候，他或许也会稍微工作一下；但他永远不会牺牲自己的自由。
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: We often speak of tramps with contempt and put them in the same class as beggars,
trans: 我们常常轻蔑地看待流浪者，把他们和乞丐归为同一类，
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: but how many of us can honestly say that we have not felt a little envious of their simple way of life and their freedom from care?
trans: 但又有多少人能坦诚地说，自己没有羡慕过他们简单的生活方式以及无忧无虑的生活状态呢？
lesson: NCE3 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy

name: Five pounds too dear
trans: 价格贵了五英镑……

name: Why was even five pounds 'too dear' ?
trans: 为什么哪怕只有五磅的重量也被认为“太贵”了呢？

name: Small boats loaded with wares sped to the great liner as she was entering the harbour.
trans: 当那艘大型客轮驶入港口时，载满货物的小船迅速朝它驶去。
