name: Before she had anchored, the men from the boats had climbed on board
trans: 在她抛下锚之前，那些来自小船上的男人就已经爬上了船。

name: and the decks were soon covered with colourful rugs from Persia,
trans: 很快，这些甲板上就铺上了来自波斯的彩色地毯。

name: silks from India, copper coffee pots, and beautiful handmade silverware.
trans: 来自印度的丝绸、铜制的咖啡壶，以及精美的手工银器。

name: It was difficult not to be tempted.
trans: 很难抗拒这种诱惑。

name: Many of the tourists on board had begun bargaining with the tradesmen,
trans: 船上的许多游客已经开始与商贩们讨价还价了。

name: but I decided not to buy anything until I had disembarked.
trans: 但我决定在下车之前不购买任何东西。

name: I had no sooner got off the ship than I was assailed by a man who wanted to sell me a diamond ring.
trans: 我刚下船，就立刻被一个男人缠住了——他想要向我推销一枚钻石戒指。

name: I had no intention of buying one,
trans: 我本来就没有打算买一个的。

name: but I could not conceal the fact that I was impressed by the size of the diamonds.
trans: 但我无法隐瞒这样一个事实：这些钻石的尺寸确实让我印象深刻。

name: Some of them were as big as marbles.
trans: 其中一些球的大小和弹珠差不多。

name: The man went to great lengths to prove that the diamonds were real.
trans: 这个人付出了巨大的努力来证明这些钻石是真品。

name: As we were walking past a shop, he held a diamond firmly against the window and made a deep impression in the glass.
trans: 当我们经过一家商店时，他用力将那颗钻石压在窗户上，从而在玻璃上留下了一个明显的印记。

name: It took me over half an hour to get rid of him.
trans: 我花了半个多小时才把他弄走。

name: The next man to approach me was selling expensive pens and watches.
trans: 下一个向我走来的人在推销昂贵的钢笔和手表。

name: I examined one of the pens closely. It certainly looked genuine.
trans: 我仔细检查了其中一支笔，它看起来确实很 genuine（即非常逼真、质量上乘）。

name: At the base of the gold cap, the words 'made in the U.S.A.' had been neatly inscribed.
trans: 在金质奖杯的底部，刻着“Made in the U.S.A.”（美国制造）这几个字，字迹非常工整。

name: The man said that the pen was worth ￡50, but as a special favour, he would let me have it for ￡30.
trans: 那个人说这支笔的价值是 50 英镑，但作为一项特别的优惠，他愿意以 30 英镑的价格把笔卖给我。

name: I shook my head and held up five fingers indicating that I was willing to pay ￡5.
trans: 我摇了摇头，然后竖起了五根手指，表示我愿意支付 5 英镑。

name: Gesticulating wildly, the man acted as if he found my offer outrageous,
trans: 那个男人疯狂地比划着手势，表现得好像我的提议让他感到非常愤怒（或难以接受）。

name: but he eventually reduced the price to 10 pounds.
trans: 但他最终将价格降到了10英镑。

name: Shrugging my shoulders I began to walk away when,
trans: 我耸了耸肩，正准备走开时，突然……

name: a moment later, he ran after me and thrust the pen into my hands.
trans: 过了一会儿，他追上来，把那支笔塞到了我的手里。

name: Though he kept throwing up his arms in despair, he readily accepted the ￡5 I gave him.
trans: 尽管他不断绝望地举起双手表示抗拒，但他还是欣然接受了我给他的那5英镑。

name: I felt especially pleased with my wonderful bargain--until I got back to the ship.
trans: 我对这笔“超值”的交易感到非常满意——直到我回到船上。

name: No matter how hard I tried,
trans: 无论我多么努力，

name: it was impossible to fill this beautiful pen with ink and to this day it has never written a single word!
trans: 这枝漂亮的钢笔根本无法装上墨水；直到今天，它仍然一个字也没写过！

name: Funny or not?
trans: 有趣吗？还是不有趣？

name: What is the basis of 'sick' humour?
trans: “病态”幽默（即那些令人不适、甚至反感的幽默）的依据是什么呢？

name: Whether we find a joke funny or not largely depends on where we have been brought up.
trans: 我们是否觉得某个笑话好笑，很大程度上取决于我们的成长环境（即我们是在什么样的环境中长大的）。

name: The sense of humour is mysteriously bound up with national characteristics.
trans: 幽默感似乎与一个国家的民族特性有着某种神秘的联系（或者说，幽默感是受民族特性影响的）。

name: A Frenchman, for instance, might find it hard to laugh at a Russian joke.
trans: 例如，一个法国人可能会觉得很难理解或笑出一个俄罗斯人的笑话。

name: In the same way, a Russian might fail to see anything amusing in a joke
trans: 同样地，一个俄罗斯人可能根本看不出某个笑话有什么好笑的地方。

name: which would make an Englishman laugh to tears.
trans: 这肯定会把一个英国人笑得眼泪都出来了。

name: Most funny stories are based on comic situations.
trans: 大多数有趣的故事都是基于一些滑稽、搞笑的情境创作的。

name: In spite of national differences, certain funny situations have a universal appeal.
trans: 尽管存在文化差异，但某些有趣的情境却具有普遍的吸引力（即能够引起全球人们的共鸣）。

name: No matter where you live,
trans: 无论你住在哪里，

name: you would find it difficult not to laugh at, say, Charlie Chaplin's early films.
trans: 比如说，查理·卓别林早期的电影，你很难不觉得它们非常有趣、甚至想发笑。

name: However, a new type of humour, which stems largely from U.S., has recently come into fashion.
trans: 然而，最近一种新型的幽默风格开始流行起来，这种幽默主要源自美国。

name: It is called 'sick humour'. Comedians base their jokes on tragic situations like violent death or serious accidents.
trans: 这被称为“病态幽默”（sick humour）。喜剧演员的笑料往往基于一些悲剧性场景，比如暴力死亡或严重事故。

name: Many people find this sort of joke distasteful.
trans: 很多人觉得这种类型的笑话很令人反感（或：很无趣、很糟糕）。

name: The following example of 'sick humour' will enable you to judge for yourself.
trans: 以下这个“病态幽默”（sick humour）的例子，可以让你自己判断一下这种幽默风格到底如何。

name: A man who had broken his right leg was taken to hospital a few weeks before Christmas.
trans: 一名右腿骨折的男子在圣诞节前几周被送往医院。

name: From the moment he arrived there,
trans: 从他到达那里的那一刻起，

name: he kept on pestering his doctor to tell him when he would be able to go home.
trans: 他一直缠着医生，想知道自己什么时候可以回家。

name: He dreaded having to spend Christmas in hospital.
trans: 他非常害怕不得不在医院里度过圣诞节。

name: Though the doctor did his best, the patient's recovery was slow.
trans: 尽管医生尽了最大努力，患者的康复进程仍然很缓慢。

name: On Christmas day, the man still had his right leg in plaster.
trans: 在圣诞节那天，那个人的右腿仍然打着石膏。

name: He spent a miserable day in bed thinking of all the fun he was missing.
trans: 他在床上度过了痛苦的一天，一直在想着自己错过的所有乐趣。

name: The following day, however, the doctor consoled him by telling him
trans: 然而，第二天医生安慰他说：

name: that his chances of being able to leave hospital in time for New Year celebrations were good.
trans: 他按时出院、能够参加新年庆祝活动的几率很大。

name: The man took heart and sure enough, on New Year's Eve he was able to hobble along to a party.
trans: 那男人重新振作起来，果然在除夕夜时，他还能一瘸一拐地赶到参加派对。

name: To compensate for his unpleasant experiences in hospital,
trans: 为了弥补他在医院里所经历的不愉快经历，

name: the man drank a little more than was good for him.
trans: 那个人喝的酒比对他身体有益的量要多一些。

name: In the process, he enjoyed himself thoroughly and kept telling everybody how much he hated hospitals.
trans: 在这个过程中，他玩得非常开心，还不停地告诉所有人他有多讨厌医院。

name: He was still mumbling something about hospitals at the end of the party when he slipped on a piece of ice and broke his left leg.
trans: 派对结束时，他还在嘟囔着关于医院的事情；突然，他踩到一块冰，摔倒了，导致左腿骨折。

name: The death of a ghost
trans: 一个“幽灵”的死亡
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Why did the two brothers keep the secret?
trans: 为什么这两兄弟要保守这个秘密呢？
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: For years, villagers believed that Endley farm was haunted.
trans: 多年来，村民们一直相信恩德利农场有鬼魂出没。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: The farm was owned by two brothers, Joe and Bob Cox.
trans: 这个农场由两兄弟共同拥有，他们分别是乔（Joe Cox）和鲍勃（Bob Cox）。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: They employed a few farmhands, but no one was willing to work there long.
trans: 他们雇了一些农场工人，但没有人愿意在那里长期工作。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Every time a worker gave up his job, he told the same story.
trans: 每次有工人辞职时，他都会讲述同一个故事。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Farm labourers said that they always woke up to find that work had been done overnight.
trans: 农场工人表示，他们每天醒来后都会发现：前一晚的工作已经全部完成了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Hay had been cut and cowsheds had been cleaned.
trans: 干草已经被割下，牛棚也已经被清理干净了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: A farm worker, who stayed up all night, claimed to have seen a figure cutting corn in the moonlight.
trans: 一位整夜未眠的农场工人声称，他在月光下看到有人正在收割玉米。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: In time, it became an accepted fact that the Cox brothers employed a conscientious ghost that did most of their work for them.
trans: 随着时间的推移，人们逐渐接受了这样一个事实：Cox兄弟雇佣了一个“尽职尽责”的幽灵，这个幽灵为他们完成了大部分工作。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: No one suspected that there might be someone else on the farm who had never been seen.
trans: 没有人怀疑农场里可能还有另一个从未被任何人发现过的人。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: This was indeed the case.
trans: 事实确实如此。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: A short time ago, villagers were astonished to learn that the ghost of Endley had died.
trans: 不久前，村民们惊讶地得知：恩德利的鬼魂终于“去世”了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Everyone went to the funeral, for the 'ghost' was none other than Eric Cox,
trans: 大家都参加了葬礼，因为那个“鬼魂”其实就是埃里克·考克斯。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: a third brother who was supposed to have died as a young man.
trans: 第三个兄弟本应在年轻时就去世的。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: After the funeral, Joe and Bob revealed a secret which they had kept for over fifty years.
trans: 葬礼结束后，乔和鲍勃透露了一个他们保守了五十多年的秘密。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Eric had been the eldest son of the family, very much older than his two brothers.
trans: 埃里克是家里的长子，比他的两个弟弟年纪大很多。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: He had been obliged to join the army during the Second World War.
trans: 在第二次世界大战期间，他被迫加入了军队。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: As he hated army life, he decided to desert his regiment.
trans: 由于他极其厌恶军队生活，他决定逃离自己的部队。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: When he learnt that he would be sent abroad,
trans: 当他得知自己将被派往国外时，
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: he returned to the farm and his father hid him until the end of the war.
trans: 他回到了农场，他的父亲把他藏了起来，直到战争结束。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: Fearing the authorities, Eric remained in hiding after the war as well.
trans: 由于害怕当局的追捕，埃里克在战争结束后仍然选择隐藏起来，没有公开露面。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: His father told everybody that Eric had been killed in action.
trans: 他的父亲告诉所有人，埃里克在战斗中牺牲了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: The only other people who knew the secret were Joe and Bob.
trans: 唯一知道这个秘密的人还有乔和鲍勃。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: They did not even tell their wives.
trans: 他们甚至都没有告诉自己的妻子。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: When their father died they thought it their duty to keep Eric in hiding.
trans: 当他们的父亲去世后，他们认为有责任继续隐藏埃里克（Eric）的身份。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: All these years, Eric had lived as a recluse.
trans: 这些年来，埃里克一直过着隐居的生活。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: He used to sleep during the day and work at night,
trans: 他过去常常在白天睡觉，晚上工作。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: quite unaware of the fact that he had become the ghost of Endley.
trans: 他完全不知道自己已经变成了“恩德利”的幽灵（即：他已经变成了一个没有实体、只能以某种无形方式存在的人或存在）。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: When he died, however, his brothers found it impossible to keep the secret any longer.
trans: 然而，当他去世后，他的兄弟们发现再也无法保守这个秘密了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Death of a Ghost

name: A lovable eccentric
trans: 一个可爱的怪人（或：一个行为古怪但令人喜爱的独特人物）

name: Why did the shop assistant refuse to serve Dickie?
trans: 为什么店员拒绝为迪基提供服务呢？

name: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
trans: 真正的怪人从来都不会刻意去吸引别人的注意。

name: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
trans: 他们无视社会规范，却完全没有意识到自己正在做出什么“与众不同”的事情（即他们的行为其实并不符合社会常规）。

name: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
trans: 这无疑为他们赢得了他人的喜爱与尊重，因为他们为平淡无奇的日常生活增添了色彩（即带来了乐趣和变化）。

name: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
trans: 直到去世，理查德·科尔森一直是我们镇上最杰出的人物之一。

name: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman,
trans: 他是一位精明且富有的商人。

name: but most people in the town hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
trans: 但镇上的大多数人对他这一面的生活几乎一无所知。

name: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
trans: 在我们所有人眼中，他都被称为“迪基”（Dickie）；他的古怪行为早在他去世之前就已经成了一个广为流传的“传奇”。

name: Dickie disliked snobs intensely.
trans: 迪基极其讨厌那些自命不凡的人（即势利小人）。

name: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
trans: 尽管他拥有一辆豪车，但他几乎从不使用它，总是更喜欢步行出行。

name: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
trans: 即使下着大雨，他也拒绝打伞。

name: One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
trans: 有一天，他在一场大雨中淋湿了身体，随后走进了一家价格昂贵的商店。

name: He wanted to buy a ￡300 watch for his wife,
trans: 他想给妻子买一块价值300英镑的手表。

name: but he was in such a bedraggled condition that an assistant refused to serve him.
trans: 但他当时的样子实在太狼狈不堪了，以至于连服务员都拒绝为他服务。

name: Dickie left the shop without a word and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
trans: 迪基一言不发地离开了商店，然后回来时手里拿着一个大布袋。

name: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
trans: 由于它非常重，他就把它扔在了柜台上。

name: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
trans: 助理让他离开，但迪基根本没理会，反而要求见经理。

name: Recognizing who the customer was,
trans: 认出了这位顾客是谁，

name: the manager was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely.
trans: 经理非常抱歉，并严厉地训斥了那位助理。

name: When Dickie was given the watch, he presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
trans: 当迪基收到那块手表时，他把那个布袋送给了助手。

name: It contained ￡300 in pennies.
trans: 里面装有 300 英镑的便士（即 300 个 1 英镑的硬币）。

name: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left--30, 000 pennies in all!
trans: 他坚持要求助手在离开前数一数钱；总共有 30,000 枚便士！

name: On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
trans: 另一次，他邀请了一些著名的评论家来参观他的私人现代绘画收藏。

name: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press,
trans: 这个展览在媒体上受到了极大的关注。

name: for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists,
trans: 尽管这些画作本应出自著名艺术家的手笔，

name: they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
trans: 实际上，这些画都是迪基画的。

name: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
trans: 他花了四年时间来策划这个精心设计的“玩笑”，只是为了证明批评家们并不总是明白自己在说什么。

name: A lost ship
trans: 一艘失踪的船只

name: Did the crew of the Elkor find what they were looking for? Why?
trans: 埃尔科号（Elkor）的船员们找到他们想要的东西了吗？为什么？

name: The salvage operation had been a complete failure.
trans: 这次打捞作业彻底失败了。

name: The small ship, Elkor, which had been searching the Barents Sea for weeks, was on its way home.
trans: 那艘名为“Elkor”的小船已经在巴伦支海搜寻了数周，现在正返回家中。

name: A radio message from the mainland had been received by the ship's captain instructing him to give up the search.
trans: 船长接收到了一则来自大陆的无线电消息，命令他停止搜索。

name: The captain knew that another attempt would be made later,
trans: 船长知道，稍后还会有人再次尝试。

name: for the sunken ship he was trying to find had been carrying a precious cargo of gold bullion.
trans: 因为他试图寻找的那艘沉船，当时正载着一批珍贵的黄金货物。

name: Despite the message, the captain of the Elkor decided to try once more.
trans: 尽管收到了那条消息，埃尔科号（Elkor）的船长还是决定再试一次。

name: The sea bed was scoured with powerful nets and there was tremendous excitement on board when a chest was raised from the bottom.
trans: 海床被强大的渔网彻底清理过；当一个箱子从海底被打捞上来时，船上的所有人都兴奋不已。

name: Though the crew were at first under the impression that the lost ship had been found,
trans: 虽然船员们最初以为那艘失踪的船只已经被找到了，

name: the contents of the chest proved them wrong.
trans: 箱子里的物品证明他们是错的。

name: What they had in fact found was a ship which had been sunk many years before.
trans: 他们实际上发现的是一艘多年前就已经沉没的船只。

name: The chest contained the personal belongings of a seaman, Alan Fielding.
trans: 这个箱子里装着水手艾伦·菲尔丁的个人物品。

name: There were books, clothing and photographs, together with letters which the seaman had once received from his wife.
trans: 那里有书籍、衣物和照片，还有一些信件——这些都是那位水手曾经从他的妻子那里收到的。

name: The captain of the Elkor ordered his men to salvage as much as possible from the wreck.
trans: 埃尔科号（Elkor）的船长命令他的船员们从残骸中尽可能多地抢救出有用的物品。

name: Nothing of value was found,
trans: 没有发现任何有价值的东西。

name: but the numerous items which were brought to the surface proved to be of great interest.
trans: 但是，那些被发掘出来的众多物品都引起了极大的兴趣。

name: From a heavy gun that was raised, the captain realized that the ship must have been a cruiser.
trans: 当那门大炮被抬起来时，船长意识到这艘船应该是一艘巡洋舰。

name: In another chest which contained the belongings of a ship's officer,
trans: 在另一个箱子里，装着一名船员的个人物品。

name: there was an unfinished letter which had been written on March 14th, 1943.
trans: 有一封未完成的信，写于1943年3月14日。

name: The captain learnt from the letter that the name of the lost ship was the Karen.
trans: 从这封信中，船长得知那艘失踪的船只的名字叫“Karen”。

name: The most valuable find of all was the ship's log book, parts of which it was still possible to read.
trans: 最珍贵的发现是那艘船的航海日志；其中的一部分内容仍然可以辨认出来。

name: From this the captain was able to piece together all the information that had come to light.
trans: 通过这些信息，船长得以整理出所有已经公开的事实和细节。

name: The Karen had been sailing in a convoy to Russia when she was torpedoed by an enemy submarine.
trans: 那艘名为“Karen”的船当时正与一支船队一起前往俄罗斯，途中被敌方潜艇发射的鱼雷击中。

name: This was later confirmed by a naval official at the Ministry of Defence after the Elkor had returned home.
trans: 这一事件在“Elkor”号返回国内后，得到了国防部海军官员的证实。

name: All the items that were found were sent to the War Museum.
trans: 船上发现的所有物品都被送到了战争博物馆。

name: A day to remember
trans: 一个值得铭记的日子

name: What incident began the series of traffic accidents?
trans: 是什么事件引发了这一连串的交通事故？

name: We have all experienced days when everything goes wrong.
trans: 是什么事件引发了这一连串的交通事故？

name: A day may begin well enough, but suddenly everything seems to get out of control.
trans: 我们都经历过那些一切都出错的日子。

name: What invariably happens is that a great number of things choose to go wrong at precisely the same moment.
trans: 一天可能开始得很顺利，但突然间，一切似乎都失控了。

name: It is as if a single unimportant event set up a chain of reactions.
trans: 不可避免的是，许多事情会在同一时刻同时出错。

name: Let us suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time.
trans: 就好像某个看似微不足道的事件引发了一连串的连锁反应。

name: The telephone rings and this marks the prelude to an unforeseen series of catastrophes.
trans: 假设你正在准备饭菜，同时也在照看婴儿。

name: While you are on the phone, the baby pulls the tablecloth off the table,
trans: 电话突然响了，而这成了随后一系列意外事件的导火线。

name: smashing half your best crockery and cutting himself in the process.
trans: 你正在打电话时，婴儿把桌布从桌子上扯了下来，打碎了你一半最好的餐具，还划伤了自己。

name: You hang up hurriedly and attend to baby, crockery, etc.
trans: 你匆忙挂断电话，然后开始处理婴儿和餐具的问题……

name: Meanwhile, the meal gets burnt.
trans: 与此同时，饭菜被烧焦了。

name: As if this were not enough to reduce you to tears, your husband arrives, unexpectedly bringing three guests to dinner.
trans: 仿佛这些还不够让你心烦意乱似的，你的丈夫突然回来了，还带着三位客人一起来吃晚饭。

name: Things can go wrong on a big scale as a number of people recently discovered in Parramatta, a suburb of Sydney.
trans: 最近，在悉尼的郊区帕拉马塔，许多人发现了这样一个事实：当涉及到大规模的活动或项目时，事情很可能会出错（即可能会出现各种问题或故障）。

name: During the rush hour one evening two cars collided and both drivers began to argue.
trans: 一天晚上的高峰时段，两辆车发生了碰撞，两名司机随即开始争吵。

name: The woman immediately behind the two cars happened to be a learner.
trans: 就坐在那两辆车后面的那位女士，恰好是一名正在学习驾驶的新手。

name: She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car.
trans: 她突然陷入了恐慌，立刻停下了车子。

name: This made the driver following her brake hard.
trans: 这导致跟在她后面的司机也紧急踩下了刹车。

name: His wife was sitting beside him holding a large cake.
trans: 他的妻子坐在他旁边，手里拿着一个大蛋糕。

name: As she was thrown forward,
trans: 当她被向前抛出时……

name: the cake went right through the windscreen and landed on the road.
trans: 蛋糕直接穿过了挡风玻璃，落在了路上。

name: Seeing a cake flying through the air,
trans: 看到一个蛋糕在空中飞过……

name: a lorry driver who was drawing up alongside the car, pulled up all of a sudden.
trans: 一名正在靠近那辆汽车的卡车司机突然停了下来。

name: The lorry was loaded with empty beer bottles and hundreds of them slid off the back of the vehicle and on to the road.
trans: 卡车上装满了空啤酒瓶，结果有数百个瓶子从卡车后部滑落到了路上。

name: This led to yet another angry argument. Meanwhile, the traffic piled up behind.
trans: 这又引发了一场激烈的争吵。与此同时，后面的交通也陷入了堵塞。

name: It took the police nearly an hour to get the traffic on the move again.
trans: 警察花了将近一个小时才让交通恢复正常。

name: In the meantime, the lorry driver had to sweep up hundreds of broken bottles.
trans: 在此期间，卡车司机不得不把那些破碎的瓶子全部清理干净。

name: Only two stray dogs benefited from all this confusion, for they greedily devoured what was left of the cake.
trans: 只有两只流浪狗从这场混乱中得到了好处——它们贪婪地吃掉了剩下的残羹剩饭。

name: It was just one of those days!
trans: 唉，这不过是又平常的一天罢了！

name: A happy discovery
trans: 一个令人高兴的发现

name: What was the 'happy discovery' ?
trans: 这个“令人高兴的发现”是什么呢？

name: Antique shops exert a peculiar fascination on a great many people.
trans: 古董店对许多人来说具有独特的吸引力。

name: The more expensive kind of antique shop where rare objects are beautifully displayed in glass cases
trans: 那种价格较高的古董店，里面的稀有物品都被精心地陈列在玻璃展柜中。

name: to keep them free from dust is usually a forbidding place.
trans: 为了防止这些物品积灰，这样的地方通常需要特别维护或管理。

name: But no one has to muster up courage to enter a less pretentious antique shop.
trans: 不过，进入那些不那么讲究排场的古董店时，根本不需要鼓起什么勇气。

name: There is always hope that in its labyrinth of musty, dark, disordered rooms a real rarity will be found amongst the piles of assorted junk that litter the floors.
trans: 总有一种希望：在那充满霉味、黑暗且杂乱无章的房间里，人们或许能在散落在地板上的各种杂物堆中找到某件真正珍贵的东西。

name: No one discovers a rarity by chance.
trans: 没有人是偶然发现稀有物品的。

name: A truly dedicated bargain hunter must have patience,
trans: 一个真正热衷于寻找便宜货的人，必须具备耐心。

name: and above all, the ability to recognize the worth of something when he sees it.
trans: 最重要的是，当他看到某样东西时，能够认识到它的价值。

name: To do this, he must be at least as knowledgeable as the dealer.
trans: 为了做到这一点，他至少必须具备与经销商同等的知识水平。

name: Like a scientist bent on making a discovery,
trans: 就像一位致力于做出重大发现的科学家一样……

name: he must cherish the hope that one day he will be amply rewarded.
trans: 他必须珍惜这个希望：总有一天，他会得到丰厚的回报。

name: My old friend, Frank Halliday, is just such a person.
trans: 我的老朋友弗兰克·霍利迪，就是这样的一个人。

name: He has often described to me how he picked up a masterpiece for a mere ￡50.
trans: 他经常跟我讲述自己是如何以仅仅 50 英镑的价格买到了一件杰作的。

name: One Saturday morning, Frank visited an antique shop in my neighbourhood.
trans: 一个星期六的早晨，弗兰克去了我家附近的一家古董店。

name: As he had never been there before, he found a great deal to interest him.
trans: 由于他以前从未去过那里，因此发现了许多令他感兴趣的东西。

name: The morning passed rapidly and Frank was about to leave when he noticed a large packing case lying on the floor.
trans: 早晨过得很快，弗兰克正准备离开时，他注意到地上放着一个大包裹箱。

name: The dealer told him that it had just come in, but that he could not be bothered to open it.
trans: 经销商告诉他，这个商品刚刚到货，但他懒得去打开它。

name: Frank begged him to do so and the dealer reluctantly prised it open.
trans: 弗兰克恳求他这么做，于是发牌员不情愿地打开了那个东西。

name: The contents were disappointing.
trans: 这些内容令人失望。

name: Apart from an interesting-looking carved dagger, the box was full of crockery, much of it broken.
trans: 除了那把外观精美的雕刻匕首外，盒子里还装满了陶器，其中大部分都已经破碎了。

name: Frank gently lifted the crockery out of the box and suddenly noticed a miniature painting at the bottom of the packing case.
trans: 弗兰克小心翼翼地将餐具从盒子里取出来，突然发现包装箱的底部有一幅微型画。

name: As its composition and line reminded him of an Italian painting he knew well, he decided to buy it.
trans: 由于这幅画的构图和线条让他联想到一幅他非常熟悉的意大利画作，他决定买下它。

name: Glancing at it briefly the dealer told him that it was worth ￡50.
trans: 经销商匆匆看了一眼后告诉他，这幅画的价值是50英镑。

name: Frank could hardly conceal his excitement, for he knew that he had made a real discovery.
trans: 弗兰克几乎无法掩饰自己的兴奋之情，因为他知道自己发现了一件真正的珍宝。

name: The tiny painting proved to be an unknown masterpiece by Correggio and was worth hundreds and thousands of pounds.
trans: 后来发现，这幅小小的画作实际上是科雷乔（Correggio）的一幅未被广泛知晓的杰作，其价值高达数十万英镑。

name: Justice was done
trans: 正义得到了伸张。

name: The word 'justice' is given two different meanings in the text.
trans: 在这段文字中，“justice”这个词被赋予了两种不同的含义。

name: What is the distinction between them?
trans: 它们之间的区别是什么？

name: The word justice is usually associated with courts of law.
trans: “正义”这个词通常与法庭联系在一起。

name: We might say that justice has been done when a man's innocence or guilt has been proved beyond doubt.
trans: 我们可以说，当一个人的清白或罪行被确凿无疑地证明时，正义就得到了伸张。

name: Justice is part of the complex machinery of the law.
trans: 正义是法律这一复杂体系的重要组成部分。

name: Those who seek it, undertake an arduous journey and can never be sure that they will find it.
trans: 那些追寻它的人，必须踏上一段艰辛的旅程；而且他们永远无法确定自己是否真的能够找到它。

name: Judges, however wise or eminent, are human and can make mistakes.
trans: 然而，无论法官多么明智或德高望重，他们终究也是人，因此也可能会犯错。

name: There are rare instances when justice almost ceases to be an abstract concept.
trans: 在极少数情况下，正义几乎不再只是一个抽象的概念；它真正得以体现，成为现实。

name: Reward or punishment are meted out quite independent of human interference.
trans: 奖励或惩罚的给予几乎完全不受人类干预的影响。

name: At such times, justice acts like a living force.
trans: 在这样的时刻，正义就像一股充满活力的力量。

name: When we use a phrase like 'it serves him right',
trans: 当我们使用“这是他应得的”这样的表达时，

name: we are, in part, admitting that a certain set of circumstances has enabled justice to act of its own accord.
trans: 在某种程度上，我们承认：某些特定的情况促使正义得以自行发挥作用（即正义得以在没有人为干预的情况下得以实现）。

name: When a thief was caught on the premises of a large jewellery store one morning,
trans: 一天早晨，一个小偷在一家大型珠宝店的店内被抓获。

name: the shop assistants must have found it impossible to resist the temptation to say 'it serves him right'.
trans: 店员们肯定忍不住想说：“他活该。”

name: The shop was an old converted house with many large, disused fireplaces and tall, narrow chimneys.
trans: 这家商店是一栋经过改造的旧房子，里面有许多大型、已经废弃的壁炉，以及高而狭窄的烟囱。

name: Towards midday, a girl heard a muffled cry coming from behind one of the walls.
trans: 临近中午时分，一个女孩听到从某面墙后面传来的微弱哭声。

name: As the cry was repeated several times,
trans: 当那声呼喊被重复了几次之后……

name: she ran to tell the manager who promptly rang up the fire brigade.
trans: 她跑去告诉了经理，经理立刻拨打了消防队的电话。

name: The cry had certainly come from one of the chimneys,
trans: 那声哭喊肯定是从其中一根烟囱里传出来的。

name: but as there were so many of them, the firemen could not be certain which one it was.
trans: 但由于火源太多，消防员们无法确定具体是哪一个火源在燃烧。

name: They located the right chimney by tapping at the walls and listening for the man's cries.
trans: 他们通过敲击墙壁并聆听那个人的呼喊声，最终找到了正确的烟囱。

name: After chipping through a wall which was eighteen inches thick,
trans: 在凿穿了一面厚度为十八英寸的墙壁之后……

name: they found that a man had been trapped in the chimney.
trans: 他们发现有一名男子被困在了烟囱里。

name: As it was extremely narrow, the man was unable to move,
trans: 由于通道非常狭窄，那个人根本无法移动。

name: but the fire fighters were eventually able to free him by cutting a huge hole in the wall.
trans: 但是消防员最终通过在墙上切出一个大洞，成功将他救了出来。

name: The sorry-looking, blackened figure that emerged,
trans: 那个看起来破败不堪、被烧焦的物体……

name: admitted at once that he had tried to break into the shop during the night but had got stuck in the chimney.
trans: 他立刻承认，自己确实在夜里试图闯入那家商店，但结果被困在了烟囱里。

name: He had been there for nearly ten hours.
trans: 他已经在那里待了将近十个小时了。

name: Justice had been done even before the man was handed over to the police.
trans: 正义早已得到伸张，甚至在那个人被交给警方之前就已经如此了。

name: A chance in a million
trans: 百万分之一的机会
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: What was the chance in a million?
trans: 那概率得有多大啊？简直微乎其微，几乎为零！
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: We are less credulous than we used to be.
trans: 我们不再像过去那样容易轻信他人或事物了。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion
trans: 在十九世纪，小说家们通常会为自己的故事画上一个圆满的结局。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences--most of them wildly improbable.
trans: 通过向读者展示一系列看似巧合的事件——其中大多数其实都极不可能发生。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero's mother.
trans: 读者们欣然接受了这样一个事实：那位默默无闻的女仆其实就是这位英雄的母亲。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time
trans: 一个被认定已经去世的“失散多年的兄弟”，其实一直都活着。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero's downfall. And so on.
trans: 他们暗中策划着要毁掉英雄……诸如此类的事情。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
trans: 现代读者会认为这种天真的解决方案完全不可接受。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
trans: 然而，在现实生活中，某些情况确实会巧合地交织在一起，产生一些连十九世纪的小说家都难以置信的奇妙事件。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman,
trans: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我的祖父给我讲过一个德国出租车司机弗朗茨·布斯曼的故事。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
trans: 找到了一个被认为在二十年前就已经去世的兄弟。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
trans: 在与妻子一起散步时，他停下来与一位工人交谈。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband
trans: 在他们离开后，巴斯曼夫人评论说那个工人和她丈夫长得非常像。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: and even suggested that he might be his brother.
trans: 甚至有人猜测他可能是那个人的兄弟。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Franz poured scorn on the idea,
trans: 弗朗茨对这个想法嗤之以鼻。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
trans: 他特别提到，他的哥哥在战争中阵亡了。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story,
trans: 尽管布斯曼夫人对这件事了如指掌，
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
trans: 她认为自己可能是对的，但这种可能性微乎其微（只有百万分之一）。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.
trans: 几天后，她派了一个男孩去问那个工人，他的名字是不是汉斯·布斯曼（Hans Bussman）。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz's long-lost brother.
trans: 不用说，这个男人的名字是汉斯·布斯曼，他确实是弗朗茨失散已久的兄弟。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: When the brothers were reunited,
trans: 当兄弟俩重聚时，
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
trans: 汉斯解释了自己是如何活下来的。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: After having been wounded towards the end of the war,
trans: 在战争接近尾声时受伤之后，
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
trans: 他被送到了医院，也因此与他的部队分开了。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
trans: 这家医院遭到了轰炸，汉斯只好徒步回到了西德。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
trans: 与此同时，他的部队失踪了，关于他的所有记录也被毁掉了。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed
trans: 汉斯回到了他的家庭住宅，但房子已经被炸毁了。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
trans: 邻居们中没有人知道那些居民后来怎么样了。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid,
trans: 假设他的家人在一次空袭中遇难了……
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
trans: 汉斯在五十英里外的一个村庄安顿了下来，从那以后他就一直住在那里。
lesson: NCE3 · A Chance in a Million

name: The Westhaven Express
trans: 西黑文特快（Westhaven Express）

name: What was the mistake the author made?
trans: 作者犯了什么错误？

name: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.
trans: 我们已经习惯了火车会准点到达这一情况。

name: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.
trans: 经过多年的“训练”（即长期使用铁路时刻表），我们大多数人都对铁路时刻表产生了无比的信任——这种信任几乎是坚定不移的。

name: Ships may be delayed by storms;
trans: 船只可能会因为风暴而延误。

name: flights may be cancelled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time.
trans: 航班可能会因为恶劣天气而被取消；但火车必须准时运行。

name: Only an exceptionally heavy snow fall might temporarily dislocate railway services.
trans: 只有当降雪量异常大时，铁路服务才可能暂时受到影响（即无法正常运行）。

name: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.
trans: 当出现问题时，人们很容易将责任归咎于铁路管理部门。

name: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.
trans: 事实上，当错误发生时，这些错误更有可能是我们自己造成的，而不是他们的。

name: After consulting my railway timetable, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven.
trans: 在查看了铁路时刻表后，我满意地发现有一趟直达韦斯特黑文的快车。

name: It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes.
trans: 它直接从我的当地电视台发射出去，整个传输过程仅耗时一小时十七分钟。

name: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.
trans: 当我登上火车时，我注意到有很多人也是当地居民。

name: At the time, this did not strike me as odd.
trans: 当时，我并没有觉得这有什么奇怪的。

name: I reflected that there must be a great many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
trans: 我想，除了我之外，肯定还有很多人希望能够利用这项优质的服务。

name: Neither was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.
trans: 当火车在威德利（Widley）这个位于铁路线上几英里外的小车站停下来的时候，我也没有感到惊讶。

name: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.
trans: 即使是一列速度极快的特快列车，也会因为信号灯的指示而被迫减速或停车。

name: But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder.
trans: 但是当火车在一个又一个车站上缓慢停留、迟迟不前时，我开始感到疑惑了。

name: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
trans: 我突然意识到：这辆快车并不是以每小时90英里的速度飞驰在铁轨上，而只是以每小时30英里的速度缓慢前行而已。

name: One hour and seventeen minutes passed and we had not even covered half the distance.
trans: 一个小时十七分钟过去了，我们甚至还没有走完一半的路程。

name: I asked a passenger if this was the Westhaven Express, but he had not even heard of it.
trans: 我问了一位乘客这是否是“Westhaven Express”列车，但他甚至从未听说过这趟列车。

name: I determined to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived.
trans: 我们一到达，我就决定立即提出投诉。

name: Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the station master at Westhaven.
trans: 两小时后，我正在西黑文（Westhaven）愤怒地与车站站长交谈。

name: When he denied the train's existence, I borrowed his copy of the timetable.
trans: 当他否认火车的存在时，我就借用了他的时刻表。

name: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
trans: 当我告诉他这个信息已经以黑白文字的形式明确记录在文件中时，我的声音里带着一丝胜利的喜悦。

name: Glancing at it briefly, he told me to look again.
trans: 他匆匆瞥了一眼后，让我再仔细看一遍。

name: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page.
trans: 一个微小的星号指引我找到了页面底部的脚注。

name: It said: 'This service has been suspended.'
trans: 脚注上写着：“该服务已被暂停。”

name: The first calendar
trans: 第一个日历

name: What is the importance of the dots, lines, and symbols engraved on stone, bones and ivory?
trans: 刻在石头、骨头和象牙上的点、线以及符号究竟有什么重要性呢？

name: Future historians will be in a unique position when they come to record the history of our own times.
trans: 未来的历史学家在记录我们这个时代的历史时，将会处于一个非常独特的地位。

name: They will hardly know which facts to select from the great mass of evidence that steadily accumulates.
trans: 他们几乎无法从不断积累的大量证据中判断出应该选择哪些事实。

name: What is more, they will not have to rely solely on the written word.
trans: 此外，他们将不必仅仅依赖书面文字来获取信息或表达自己的观点。

name: Films, videos, CDs and CD-ROMs are just some of the bewildering amount of information they will have.
trans: 电影、视频、CD以及CD-ROM只是他们所拥有的海量信息中的一部分而已。

name: They will be able, as it were, to see and hear us in action.
trans: 他们将能够，可以说是，看到我们行动的样子，听到我们的声音。

name: But the historian attempting to reconstruct the distant past is always faced with a difficult task.
trans: 但是，试图重建遥远过去的历史学家总是面临着一项艰巨的任务。

name: He has to deduce what he can from the few scanty clues available.
trans: 他必须从那些为数不多、且信息极其有限的线索中尽可能多地推断出有用的信息。

name: Even seemingly insignificant remains can shed interesting light on the history of early man.
trans: 即使是一些看似微不足道的遗骸，也能为我们提供关于早期人类历史的有趣线索。

name: Up to now, historians have assumed that calendars came into being with the advent of agriculture,
trans: 到目前为止，历史学家们一直认为日历的出现是与农业的诞生同时发生的。

name: for then man was faced with a real need to understand something about the seasons.
trans: 因为那时，人类确实迫切需要了解关于季节变化的规律。

name: Recent scientific evidence seems to indicate that this assumption is incorrect.
trans: 最近的科学证据似乎表明，这一假设是不正确的。

name: Historians have long been puzzled by dots, lines and symbols which have been engraved on walls, bones, and the ivory tusks of mammoths.
trans: 历史学家们长期以来一直对这些刻在墙壁上、骨头以及猛犸象象牙上的点、线条和符号感到困惑。

name: The nomads who made these markings lived by hunting and fishing during the last Ice Age which began about 35, 000 B.C. and ended about 10, 000 B.C.
trans: 制造这些标记的游牧民族在最后一次冰河时代（大约始于公元前35000年，结束于公元前10000年）以狩猎和捕鱼为生。

name: By correlating markings made in various parts of the world,
trans: 通过将世界各地留下的标记进行关联分析，

name: historians have been able to read this difficult code.
trans: 历史学家们已经成功解读了这段难以理解的代码。

name: They have found that it is connected with the passage of days and the phases of the moon.
trans: 他们发现这种现象与时间的流逝以及月亮的盈亏周期有关。

name: It is, in fact, a primitive type of calendar.
trans: 实际上，这是一种非常原始的日历形式。

name: It has long been known that the hunting scenes depicted on walls were not simply a form of artistic expression.
trans: 人们早就知道，墙上描绘的狩猎场景并非仅仅是一种艺术表达形式。

name: They had a definite meaning, for they were as near as early man could get to writing.
trans: 这些符号具有明确的含义，因为它们几乎是早期人类所能使用的最接近“书写”的方式了。

name: It is possible that there is a definite relation between these paintings and the markings that sometimes accompany them.
trans: 这些画作与有时出现在它们上面的标记之间可能存在某种明确的关联（或：这些画作与那些标记之间很可能存在着某种特定的联系）。

name: It seems that man was making a real effort to understand the seasons 20, 000 years earlier than has been supposed.
trans: 看来，早在人们原先认为的时间之前2万年，人类就已经在努力理解四季的变化规律了。

name: Nothing to worry about
trans: 没什么好担心的。

name: What was the differnce between Bruce's behaviour and that of other people?
trans: 布鲁斯的行为与其他人的行为有什么不同？

name: The rough road across the plain soon became so bad that we tried to get Bruce to drive back to the village we had come from.
trans: 穿过平原的崎岖道路状况越来越糟糕，我们便决定让布鲁斯开车把我们送回我们出发的村庄。

name: Even though the road was littered with boulders and pitted with holes, Bruce was not in the least perturbed.
trans: 尽管路上布满了巨石，还有许多坑洞，布鲁斯却丝毫没有感到不安。

name: Glancing at his map, he informed us that the next village was a mere twenty miles away.
trans: 他看了一眼地图，然后告诉我们下一个村庄只有二十英里远。

name: It was not that Bruce always underestimated difficulties.
trans: 并不是说布鲁斯总是低估困难；事实上，他并不总是这样。

name: He simply had no sense of danger at all.
trans: 他完全没有任何危险意识。

name: No matter what the conditions were, he believed that a car should be driven as fast as it could possibly go.
trans: 无论条件如何，他都认为汽车应该被开到尽可能快的速度。

name: As we bumped over the dusty track, we swerved to avoid large boulders.
trans: 当我们行驶在布满灰尘的小路上时，我们不断地转向以避开那些巨大的岩石。

name: The wheels scooped up stones which hammered ominously under the car.
trans: 车轮卷起了石子，这些石子在汽车下方发出令人不安的撞击声。

name: We felt sure that sooner or later a stone would rip a hole in our petrol tank or damage the engine.
trans: 我们确信，迟早会有石头划破我们的油箱，或者损坏发动机。

name: Because of this, we kept looking back, wondering if we were leaving a trail of oil and petrol behind us.
trans: 正因如此，我们不断回头查看，担心自己是否留下了石油和汽油的痕迹。

name: What a relief it was when the boulders suddenly disappeared,
trans: 当那些巨石突然消失的时候，真是让人松了一口气啊。

name: giving way to a stretch of plain where the only obstacles were clumps bushes.
trans: 这片区域逐渐变成了开阔的平原；唯一的障碍是一些零星的灌木丛。

name: But there was worse to come. Just ahead of us there was a huge fissure.
trans: 但更糟糕的事情还在后面。就在我们前方，有一条巨大的裂缝。

name: In response to renewed pleadings, Bruce stopped.
trans: 在听到再次提出的请求后，布鲁斯停了下来。

name: Though we all got out to examine the fissure, he remained in the car.
trans: 虽然我们都下车去查看那条裂缝，但他却留在了车里。

name: We informed him that the fissure extended for fifty yards and was two feet wide and four feet deep.
trans: 我们告诉他，那条裂缝长达五十码（约45.7米），宽度为两英尺（约0.6米），深度为四英尺（约1.2米）。

name: Even this had no effect.
trans: 即使这样，也没有任何效果。

name: Bruce went into a low gear and drove at a terrifying speed,
trans: 布鲁斯突然降低了车速，然后以惊人的速度继续行驶。

name: keeping the front wheels astride the crack as he followed its zigzag course.
trans: 他驾驶车辆沿着这条蜿蜒曲折的小路前行，确保前轮始终保持在裂缝的边缘上（即前轮不会掉进裂缝里）。

name: Before we had time to worry about what might happen, we were back on the plain again.
trans: 在我们还有时间去担心可能发生的事情之前，我们又回到了那片平原上。

name: Bruce consulted the map once more and told us that the village was now only fifteen miles away.
trans: 布鲁斯再次查看了地图，然后告诉我们那个村庄现在距离我们只有十五英里了。

name: Our next obstacle was a shallow pool of water about half a mile across.
trans: 我们的下一个障碍是一个大约半英里宽的浅水池。

name: Bruce charged at it, but in the middle, the car came to a grinding halt.
trans: 布鲁斯驾车冲了过去，但车子在半路上突然停了下来。

name: A yellow light on the dashboard flashed angrily and Bruce cheerfully announced that there was no oil in the engine!
trans: 仪表盘上的黄灯闪烁着，布鲁斯高兴地宣布：发动机里没有油了！

name: Who's who
trans: 谁是谁？

name: How did the policeman discover that the whole thing was a joke?
trans: 警察是怎么发现这一切其实只是个玩笑的呢？

name: It has never been explained why university students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else.
trans: 从来没有人解释过，为什么大学生似乎比其他人更喜欢搞恶作剧（尤其是那些带有实际效果的恶作剧）。

name: Students specialize in a particular type of practical joke: the hoax.
trans: 学生们专精于一种特定类型的恶作剧——那就是“骗局”（即通过虚假信息或欺骗手段来制造混乱或误导他人）。

name: Inviting the fire brigade to put out a nonexistent fire is a crude form of deception which no self-respecting student would ever indulde in.
trans: 邀请消防队去扑灭根本不存在的“火灾”，这种行为属于赤裸裸的欺骗手段；任何有自尊心的学生都不会做出这种事。

name: Students often create amusing situations which are funny to everyone except the victims.
trans: 学生们经常制造一些有趣的、滑稽的情境，但这些情境只有受害者自己觉得不好笑，其他人反而都觉得很好笑。

name: When a student recently saw two workmen using a pneumatic drill outside his university,
trans: 最近，一名学生在自己的大学外面看到两名工人正在使用气动钻机。

name: he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen
trans: 他立即拨打了报警电话，并告诉警方有两名学生装扮成工人。

name: were tearing up the road with a pneumatic drill.
trans: 他们正用气动钻在道路上钻孔（即破坏道路的路面）。

name: As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a policeman ordered them to go away,
trans: 他一挂断电话，就走到工人们跟前，告诉他们：“如果警察命令他们离开，他们就必须服从。”

name: they were not to take him seriously.
trans: 他们不应该把他当回事。

name: He added that a student had dressed up as a policeman and was playing all sorts of silly jokes on people.
trans: 他还补充说，有个学生打扮成警察的样子，对周围的人开了各种滑稽的玩笑。

name: Both the police and the workmen were grateful to the student for this piece of advance information.
trans: 警察和工人们都非常感谢这名学生提供的这一重要线索（或：提前提供的信息）。

name: The student hid in an archway nearby where he could watch and hear everything that went on.
trans: 那个学生躲在附近的一个拱门里，从那里他可以观察到发生的一切，也能听到所有的声音。

name: Sure enough, a policeman arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to go away.
trans: 果然，一名警察来到了现场，并礼貌地要求工人们离开。

name: When he received a very rude reply from one of the workmen, he threatened to remove them by force.
trans: 当他收到其中一名工人的粗鲁回复时，他威胁说要强行将他们赶走。

name: The workmen told him to do as he pleased and the policeman telephoned for help.
trans: 工人们让他随意行事，而警察则拨打了求救电话。

name: Shortly afterwards, 4 more policemen arrived and remonstrated with the workmen.
trans: 不久之后，又有 4 名警察赶到，他们对工人们提出了抗议（或：他们与工人们发生了争执）。

name: As the men refused to stop working, the police attempted to seize the pneumatic drill.
trans: 由于那些工人拒绝停止工作，警方试图没收那台气动钻机。

name: The workmen struggled fiercely and one of them lost his temper.
trans: 工人们拼命地干活，其中一个人终于失去了耐心（发火了）。

name: He threatened to call the police.
trans: 他威胁说要报警。

name: At this, the police pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary as the men were already under arrest.
trans: 此时，警方讽刺地指出：其实这根本没必要，因为那些人早已被逮捕了。

name: Pretending to speak seriously, one of the workmen asked if he might make a telephone call before being taken to the station.
trans: 装出一副认真的样子，其中一名工人询问是否可以在被带到警察局之前打个电话。

name: Permission was granted and a policeman accompanied him to a pay phone.
trans: 获得了许可后，一名警察陪同他前往了一部公用电话。

name: Only when he saw that the man was actually telephoning the police did he realize that they had all been the victims of a hoax.
trans: 直到看到那个人真的在报警时，他才意识到他们所有人其实都成了一个骗局的受害者。

name: Illusions of pastoral peace
trans: 田园宁静的假象

name: What particular anxiety spoils the country dweller's visit to the theatre?
trans: 是什么特定的焦虑情绪，破坏了这个国家居民去剧院观看演出的体验（或者说：是什么因素让他们的剧院之旅变得不愉快/令人失望的？）

name: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
trans: 乡村的宁静生活从来都没有吸引过我。

name: City born and city bred,
trans: 我出生并成长在这座城市。

name: I have always regarded the country as something you look at through a train window, or something you occasionally visit during the weekend.
trans: 我一直认为这个国家就像是通过火车窗户看到的风景，或者是一个偶尔在周末才会去参观的地方。

name: Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
trans: 我的大多数朋友都住在城市里，然而每当提到乡村时，他们总是表现出极大的热情和向往。

name: Though they extol the virtues of the peaceful life,
trans: 尽管他们推崇和平生活的种种美德，

name: only one of them has ever gone to live in the country and he was back in town within six months.
trans: 他们当中只有一个人真正搬去那个国家居住，不过他在六个月后就回到了城里。

name: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
trans: 即使他现在也仍然抱有一种错觉，认为乡村生活比城市生活优越。

name: He is forever talking about the friendly people, the clean atmosphere, the closeness to nature and the gentle pace of living.
trans: 他总是谈论那里友好的人民、清新的空气、与自然的亲密关系，以及悠闲的生活节奏。

name: Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn,
trans: 他坚持认为：没有任何东西能够与清晨的第一声鸡鸣、以及鸟儿啁啾的声音相媲美。

name: the sight of the rising sun glinting on the trees and pastures.
trans: 朝阳的光芒在树木和牧场上闪烁的景象。

name: This idyllic pastoral scene is only part of the picture.
trans: 这幅田园诗般的景象只不过是整个画面的一部分罢了。

name: My friend fails to mention the long and friendless winter evenings in front of the TV--virtually the only form of entertainment.
trans: 我的朋友从未提到那些漫长而孤独的冬夜：那些夜晚，他们只能坐在电视机前，电视几乎是他们唯一的娱乐来源。

name: He says nothing about the poor selection of goods in the shops,
trans: 他对商店里商品质量差、选择范围有限的问题只字未提。

name: or about those unfortunate people who have to travel from the country to the city every day to get to work.
trans: 或者，那些不幸的人——他们每天不得不从乡下赶到城市去上班。

name: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.
trans: 我实在无法理解：为什么人们愿意每天忍受长达四小时的通勤时间，只为了获得住在乡下的那种“微不足道”的特权。

name: They could be saved so much misery and expense if they chose to live in the city where they rightly belong.
trans: 如果他们选择回到自己真正应该居住的城市，就能避免那么多痛苦和开支了。

name: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
trans: 如果你能够舍弃乡村生活中那些宁静、惬意的乐趣，你会发现城市能够为你提供生活中最美好的东西。

name: You never have to travel miles to see your friends.
trans: 你再也不需要长途跋涉去见你的朋友了。

name: They invariably live nearby and are always available for an informal chat or an evening's entertainment.
trans: 他们总是住在附近，随时可以陪你闲聊或一起享受晚上的娱乐时光。

name: Some of my acquaintances in the country come up to town once or twice a year to visit the theatre as a special treat.
trans: 我国内的一些熟人每年会来城里一两次，专门为了看戏剧而享受这份特别的乐趣。

name: For them this is a major operation which involves considerable planning.
trans: 对他们来说，这是一项规模较大的行动，需要周密的规划。

name: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
trans: 随着戏剧接近尾声，他们开始怀疑自己是否还能赶上回家的最后一班火车。

name: The city dweller never experiences anxieties of this sort.
trans: 城市居民从来不会经历这种焦虑。

name: The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.
trans: 最新的展览、电影或戏剧演出，都只需乘坐公交车很短的距离就能到达。

name: Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.
trans: 购物也总是一种令人愉悦的体验。

name: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
trans: 选择如此丰富多样，以至于你永远不必将就于次优的选择。

name: Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city and stagger home loaded with as many of the exotic items as they can carry.
trans: 乡下人一到城里购物，就会变得兴奋不已，他们会尽可能多地购买各种异国风味的商品，然后摇摇晃晃地带着这些东西回家。

name: Nor is the city without its moments of beauty.
trans: 这座城市也有它美丽的时刻。

name: There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
trans: 在寒冷潮湿的冬夜里，广告散发出的温暖光芒总有一种令人感到舒适的感觉。

name: Few things could be more impressive than the peace that descends on deserted city streets at weekends
trans: 没有什么比周末时那些荒凉的城市街道上降临的宁静更令人印象深刻的了。

name: when the thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
trans: 当每天成千上万的上班族都待在家里（位于乡村地区）时……

name: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers, who appreciate all these things,
trans: 我一直很困惑：为什么城市居民——他们明明很享受这些便利和美好的事物——却……（原句似乎不完整，因此无法准确翻译后半部分的意思。）

name: obstinately pretend that they would prefer to live in the country.
trans: 他们固执地假装自己更喜欢住在乡下。

name: Modern cavemen
trans: 现代“穴居人”

name: With what does the writer compare the Gouffre Berger?
trans: 作者将“贝杰尔洞穴”（Gouffre Berger）比作什么？

name: Cave exploration, or pot-holing, as it has come to be known, is a relatively new sport.
trans: 洞穴探险，也就是现在人们常说的“pot-holing”，其实是一项相对较新的运动。

name: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery that lures people down to the depths of the earth.
trans: 也许，正是对孤独的渴望，或是希望做出意外发现的心情，驱使人们前往地球的深处。

name: It is impossible to give a satisfactory explanation for a pot-holer's motives.
trans: 对于那些懒惰、逃避责任的人（即“pot-holers”）的动机，根本不可能给出一个令人满意的解释。

name: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.
trans: 对他来说，洞穴具有与高山对登山者同样的独特吸引力。

name: They arouse instincts which can only be dimly understood.
trans: 它们唤醒了一些我们只能勉强理解的本能。

name: Exploring really deep caves is not a task for the Sunday afternoon rambler.
trans: 探索那些极其深邃的洞穴，绝不是适合在周日午后闲逛时去完成的任务。

name: Such undertakings require the precise planning and foresight of military operations.
trans: 这样的行动需要精确的军事计划和深远的预见性。

name: It can take as long as eight days to rig up rope ladders and to establish supply bases before a descent can be made into a very deep cave.
trans: 在进入一个非常深的洞穴之前，搭建绳梯并建立补给基地可能需要长达八天的时间。

name: Precautions of this sort are necessary, for it is impossible to foretell the exact nature of the difficulties which will confront the pot-holer.
trans: 采取这样的预防措施是必要的，因为我们无法预先预测那些可能会困扰（或困扰某人）的困难的具体性质。

name: The deepest known cave in the world is the Gouffre Berger near Grenoble.
trans: 世界上已知最深的洞穴是位于格勒诺布尔附近的贝尔热洞穴（Gouffre Berger）。

name: It extends to a depth of 3, 723 feet.
trans: 它的深度达到了3,723英尺。

name: This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunnelled a course through a flaw in the rocks.
trans: 这个巨大的峡谷是由一条地下溪流形成的；这条溪流在岩石的裂缝中穿行，逐渐侵蚀出了这条通道。

name: The entrance to the cave is on a plateau in the Dauphine Alps.
trans: 洞穴的入口位于多菲内阿尔卑斯山脉的一个高原上。

name: As it is only six feet across, it is barely noticeable.
trans: 由于它的宽度只有六英尺，几乎看不出来它的存在。

name: The cave might never have been discovered had not the entrance been spotted by the distinguished French pot-holer, Berger.
trans: 如果那个洞穴的入口没有被那位著名的法国酒鬼伯杰发现的话，它可能永远都不会被人发现。

name: Since its discovery, it has become a sort of pot-holers' Everest.
trans: 自从它被发现以来，它就成了那些喜欢在废墟中探险的人们的“珠穆朗玛峰”——一个令人向往、充满挑战的目标。

name: Though a number of descents have been made, much of it still remains to be explored.
trans: 尽管已经有人多次尝试探索那里，但仍有很大一部分区域尚未被人类发现或探索。

name: A team of pot-holers recently went down the Gouffre Berger.
trans: 最近，一支由洞穴探险者组成的团队进入了贝尔热洞（Gouffre Berger）。

name: After entering the narrow gap on the plateau,
trans: 在进入高原上的那个狭窄缝隙之后……

name: they climbed down the steep sides of the cave until they came to a narrow corridor.
trans: 他们沿着洞穴陡峭的侧壁向下爬行，直到来到一条狭窄的通道前。

name: They had to edge their way along this,
trans: 他们不得不沿着这条路小心翼翼地前行。

name: sometimes wading across shallow streams, or swimming across deep pools.
trans: 有时候需要涉水穿过浅流；有时候则需要游过深水区。

name: Suddenly they came to a waterfall which dropped into an underground lake at the bottom of the cave.
trans: 突然，他们来到了一处瀑布前；那瀑布的水流直接注入了洞穴底部的一个地下湖泊中。

name: They plunged into the lake, and after loading their gear on an inflatable rubber dinghy, let the current carry them to the other side.
trans: 他们跳进了湖里，然后将装备装上了一个充气橡胶小艇，让水流将他们带到对岸。

name: To protect themselves from the icy water, they had to wear special rubber suits.
trans: 为了防止被冰冷的水冻伤，他们不得不穿上特制的橡胶防护服。

name: At the far end of the lake, they came to huge piles of rubble which had been washed up by the water.
trans: 在湖的尽头，他们看到了一堆堆巨大的废墟，这些废墟是被水冲上岸来的。

name: In this part of the cave, they could hear an insistent booming sound
trans: 在这个洞穴的区域内，他们能听到一种持续不断的、低沉的轰鸣声。

name: which they found was caused by a small waterspout shooting down into a pool from the roof of the cave.
trans: 他们发现，这种现象是由于一个小型“水龙卷”从洞穴的屋顶冲下来，落入了一个水池中而引起的。

name: Squeezing through a cleft in the rocks, the pot-holers arrived at an enormous cavern, the size of a huge concert hall.
trans: 穿过岩石间的裂缝，那些洞穴探险者终于来到了一处巨大的洞穴——其规模相当于一座大型音乐厅。

name: After switching on powerful arc lights,
trans: 在打开强力的弧光灯之后，

name: they saw great stalagmites--some of them over forty feet high--rising up like tree-trunks to meet the stalactites suspended from the roof.
trans: 他们看到了那些巨大的石笋——其中一些高达四十多英尺——这些石笋像树干一样矗立着，与从屋顶悬挂下来的钟乳石相接。

name: Round about, piles of limestone glistened in all the colours of the rainbow.
trans: 周围，成堆的石灰岩闪烁着彩虹般的各种色彩。

name: In the eerie silence of the cavern, the only sound that could be heard was made by water which dripped continuously from the high dome above them.
trans: 在洞穴那令人毛骨悚然的寂静中，唯一能听到的声音，就是从他们头顶的高耸穹顶上不断滴落的水声。

name: Fully insured
trans: 全面投保

name: Who owned the pie dish and why?
trans: 谁拥有那个派盘，为什么？

name: Insurance companies are normally willing to insure anything.
trans: 那个派盘是谁的？为什么需要投保？

name: Insuring public or private property is a standard practice in most countries in the world.
trans: 保险公司通常愿意为任何物品提供保险服务。

name: If, however, you were holding an open air garden party or a fete it would be equally possible to insure yourself in the event of bad weather.
trans: 在世界上大多数国家，为公共或私人财产投保都是常规做法。

name: Needless to say, the bigger the risk an insurance company takes, the higher the premium you will have to pay.
trans: 不过，如果你在户外举办派对，也可以为可能发生的恶劣天气情况购买保险。

name: It is not uncommon to hear that a shipping company has made a claim for the cost of salvaging a sunken ship.
trans: 显然，保险公司承担的风险越大，你需要支付的保费也就越高。

name: But the claim made by a local authority to recover the cost of salvaging a sunken pie dish must surely be unique.
trans: 我们经常听到航运公司因打捞沉船而提出索赔；不过，地方政府为打捞一个沉没的派盘而提出的索赔，无疑是非常罕见的。

name: Admittedly it was an unusual pie dish, for it was eighteen feet long and six feet wide.
trans: 这个派盘确实很不寻常——它的长度为18英尺，宽度为6英尺。

name: It had been purchased by a local authority so that an enormous pie could be baked for an annual fair.
trans: 它是被当地政府购买的，用于为年度集市制作一个巨大的派。

name: The pie committee decided that the best way to transport the dish would be by canal so they insured it for the trip.
trans: 派盘运输委员会认为通过运河运输是最合适的方式，因此他们为这次运输购买了保险。

name: Shortly after it was launched, the pie committee went to a local inn to celebrate.
trans: 产品发布后不久，负责组织庆祝活动的委员会成员们便前往了一家当地的酒馆进行庆祝。

name: At the same time, a number of teenagers climbed on to the dish and held a little party of their own.
trans: 与此同时，一些青少年爬上了那个盘子，并在那里举办了一场属于自己的小型聚会。

name: Dancing proved to be more than the dish could bear,
trans: 跳舞的强度超出了这道菜（或：这个场景）所能承受的范围（即：跳舞的动作过于激烈或持续时间过长，导致其他方面受到影响）。

name: for during the party it capsized and sank in seven feet of water.
trans: 在派对期间，那艘船翻了，然后沉入了七英尺深的水中。

name: The pie committee telephoned a local garage owner who arrived in a recovery truck to salvage the pie dish.
trans: 派饼制作委员会联系了一位当地的汽车修理厂老板，他驾驶着一辆救援卡车前来帮忙取回那个用来盛派饼的容器。

name: Shivering in their wet clothes, the teenagers looked on while three men dived repeatedly into the water to locate the dish.
trans: 那些青少年穿着湿衣服，瑟瑟发抖地站在那里，看着三个男人一次又一次地跳入水中，试图寻找那个丢失的盘子。

name: They had little difficulty in finding it, but hauling it out of the water proved to be a serious problem.
trans: 他们找到它并不费什么劲，但将其从水中拖出来却成了一个严重的问题。

name: The sides of the dish were so smooth that it was almost impossible to attach hawsers and chains to the rim without damaging it.
trans: 这个盘子的边缘非常光滑，几乎不可能在不损坏它的情况下将缆绳或链条固定在盘子的边缘上。

name: Eventually chains were fixed to one end of the dish and a powerful winch was put into operation.
trans: 最终，那些链条被固定在盘子的一端；随后，一台强大的绞车也被启动了起来。

name: The dish rose to the surface and was gently drawn towards the canal bank.
trans: 那个物体浮到了水面上，然后被轻轻地拉向了运河岸边。

name: For one agonizing moment, the dish was perched precariously on the bank of the canal,
trans: 有那么一瞬间，那个盘子摇摇欲坠地放在运河的岸边，情况非常危险。

name: but it suddenly overbalanced and slid back into the water.
trans: 但它突然失去了平衡，又滑回了水中。

name: The men were now obliged to try once more.
trans: 这些人现在不得不再次尝试。

name: This time they fixed heavy metal clamps to both sides of the dish so that they could fasten the chains.
trans: 这次，他们在盘子的两侧安装了沉重的金属夹具，以便固定链条。

name: The dish now had to be lifted vertically because one edge was resting against the side of the canal.
trans: 由于盘子的一边紧贴着运河的侧壁，因此必须将其垂直抬起。

name: The winch was again put into operation and one of the men started up the truck.
trans: 绞车再次被启动，其中一名男子启动了卡车。

name: Several minutes later, the dish was successfully hauled above the surface of the water.
trans: 几分钟后，盘子终于被成功吊到了水面上方。

name: Water streamed in torrents over its sides with such force that it set up a huge wave in the canal.
trans: 大量的水从盘子边缘倾泻而下，形成了巨大的波浪。

name: There was a danger that the wave would rebound off the other side of the bank and send the dish plunging into the water again.
trans: 存在这样的风险：这股波浪可能会从河岸的另一侧反弹回来，导致盘子再次落入水中。

name: By working at tremendous speed, the men managed to get the dish on to dry land before the wave returned.
trans: 在波浪返回之前，这些人以极快的速度完成了操作，最终将盘子安全地移到了陆地上。

name: Speed and comfort
trans: 速度与舒适性

name: Which type of transport does the writer prefer, do you think?
trans: 你认为作者更喜欢哪种交通工具呢？

name: People travelling long distances frequently have to decide whether they would prefer to go by land, sea, or air.
trans: 长途旅行的人经常需要决定是选择陆路、海路还是航空方式来出行。

name: Hardly anyone can positively enjoy sitting in a train for more than a few hours.
trans: 几乎没有人能够真正享受在火车上坐上几个小时以上的时光。

name: Train compartments soon get cramped and stuffy.
trans: 火车车厢很快就会变得拥挤不堪、空气也不流通（即非常闷热）。

name: It is almost impossible to take your mind off the journey.
trans: 几乎不可能让你把注意力从这段旅程上移开。

name: Reading is only a partial solution, for the monotonous rhythm of the wheels clicking on the rails soon lull you to sleep.
trans: 阅读只能提供部分缓解；车轮在铁轨上单调地咔嗒作响，这种声音很快就会让你入睡。

name: During the day, sleep comes in snatches.
trans: 白天里，睡眠总是断断续续的。

name: At night, when you really wish to go to sleep, you rarely manage to do so.
trans: 到了晚上，当你真的想入睡的时候，却往往难以入睡。

name: If you are lucky enough to get a sleeper,
trans: 如果你有幸买到一张“睡票”（即价格较低、座位较为舒适的火车票），

name: you spend half the night staring at the small blue light in the ceiling, or fumbling to find your ticket for inspection.
trans: 你整晚都在盯着天花板上的那个蓝色小灯看，或者费力地寻找需要检查的车票。

name: Inevitably you arrive at your destination almost exhausted.
trans: 最终，你几乎精疲力尽地到达了目的地。

name: Long car journeys are even less pleasant, for it is quite impossible even to read.
trans: 长途驾车旅行更加令人不适，因为在这种情况下甚至连看书都几乎不可能做到。

name: On motorways you can, at least, travel fairly safely at high speeds,
trans: 在高速公路上，至少你可以以较高的速度安全地行驶。

name: but more often than not, the greater part of the journey is spent on roads with few service stations and too much traffic.
trans: 但大多数情况下，旅途中的大部分时间都是在那些服务站稀少、交通拥堵严重的道路上度过的。

name: By comparison, ferry trips or cruises offer a great variety of civilized comforts.
trans: 相比之下，渡轮旅行或游轮旅行提供了多种舒适的设施和服务。

name: You can stretch your legs on the spacious decks, play games,
trans: 你可以在宽敞的甲板上伸展双腿、玩游戏，

name: meet interesting people and enjoy good food--always assuming, of course, that the sea is calm.
trans: 结识有趣的人，享受美味的美食——当然，这一切的前提都是海面必须风平浪静。

name: If it is not, and you are likely to get seasick, no form of transport could be worse.
trans: 如果情况并非如此（即你并不会因此感到晕船），那么任何形式的交通工具都可能比这更糟糕（即都会让你感到不适）。

name: Even if you travel in ideal weather, sea journeys take a long time.
trans: 即使你在理想的天气条件下旅行，海上航行仍然需要很长时间。

name: Relatively few people are prepared to sacrifice holiday time for the pleasure of travelling by sea.
trans: 只有少数人愿意牺牲假期时间，去享受海上旅行的乐趣。

name: Aeroplanes have the reputation of being dangerous and even hardened travellers are intimidated by them.
trans: 飞机一直被认为是一种危险的交通工具，就连那些经验丰富的旅客也会对它们感到恐惧。

name: They also have the disadvantage of being an expensive form of transport.
trans: 它们的另一个缺点是：这种交通方式的成本相对较高（即费用较为昂贵）。

name: But nothing can match them for speed and comfort.
trans: 但是，在速度和舒适度方面，没有任何东西能比得上它们。

name: Travelling at a height of 30, 000 feet, far above the clouds, and at over 500 miles an hour is an exhilarating experience.
trans: 在30,000英尺的高空飞行——远远高于云层之上——并以每小时500英里的速度前进，确实是一种令人兴奋的体验。

name: You do not have to devise ways of taking your mind off the journey, for an aeroplane gets you to your destination rapidly.
trans: 你不必费心去寻找方法来转移自己的注意力，因为飞机能迅速将你送到目的地。

name: For a few hours, you settle back in a deep armchair to enjoy the flight.
trans: 你可以躺在舒适的扶手椅上，放松身心，享受这段飞行时光。

name: The real escapist can watch a film and sip champagne on some services.
trans: 真正的“逃避现实者”会边看电影边享用香槟。

name: But even when such refinements are not available, there is plenty to keep you occupied.
trans: 但即使没有这些改进措施，也有很多事情可以让你保持忙碌。

name: An aeroplane offers you an unusual and breathtaking view of the world.
trans: 从飞机上，你可以看到一个独特而令人惊叹的世界景象。

name: You soar effortlessly over high mountains and deep valleys.
trans: 你轻松地翱翔在高山之上，穿过幽深的山谷。

name: You really see the shape of the land.
trans: 你真的能够清楚地看到这片土地的轮廓和地形特征。

name: If the landscape is hidden from view,
trans: 如果周围的景色被遮挡而无法看到……

name: you can enjoy the extraordinary sight of unbroken cloud plains that stretch out for miles before you, while the sun shines brilliantly in a clear sky.
trans: 你可以欣赏到那令人惊叹的景象：连绵不断的云层平铺在眼前，一望无际；而太阳则在清澈的天空下闪耀着耀眼的光芒。

name: The journey is so smooth that there is nothing to prevent you from reading or sleeping.
trans: 旅途非常平稳，没有任何因素会妨碍你阅读或睡觉。

name: However you decide to spend your time, one thing is certain: you will arrive at your destination fresh and uncrumpled.
trans: 无论你如何安排自己的时间，有一点是肯定的：当你到达目的地时，你依然会保持精神饱满、状态良好（即“精神焕发、毫无疲惫感”）。

name: You will not have to spend the next few days recovering from a long and arduous journey.
trans: 在接下来的几天里，你不必花费时间来恢复体力——毕竟你刚刚完成了一段漫长而艰辛的旅程。

name: The power of the press
trans: 媒体的力量
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Does the writer think the parents were lucky or unlucky to gain prosperity in this way? Why?
trans: 作者认为，这些父母通过这种方式获得财富是幸运的，还是不幸的？为什么？
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: In democratic countries any efforts to restrict the freedom of the press are rightly condemned.
trans: 在民主国家中，任何限制新闻自由的行为都应受到谴责。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: However, this freedom can easily be abused.
trans: 然而，这种自由很容易被滥用。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Stories about people often attract far more public attention than political events.
trans: 关于普通人的故事往往比政治事件更能吸引公众的注意力。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Though we may enjoy reading about the lives of others,
trans: 虽然我们可能会喜欢阅读关于他人生活的故事，
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: it is extremely doubtful whether we would equally enjoy reading about ourselves.
trans: 我们是否也会同样喜欢阅读关于自己的内容，这一点实在非常值得怀疑。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Acting on the contention that facts are sacred,
trans: 基于“事实是神圣的”这一观点，
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: reporters can cause untold suffering to individuals by publishing details about their private lives.
trans: 记者通过公开个人的私生活细节，可能会给这些人带来难以估量的痛苦。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Newspapers exert such tremendous influence that they can not only bring about major changes to the lives of ordinary people but can even overthrow a government.
trans: 报纸的影响力极其巨大；它们不仅能够对普通人的生活产生重大影响，甚至有可能推翻一个政府。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: The story of a poor family that acquired fame and fortune overnight, dramatically illustrates the power of the press.
trans: 这个关于一个贫困家庭如何一夜之间获得名望和财富的故事，生动地展示了媒体的影响力。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: The family lived in Aberdeen, a small town of 23, 000 inhabitants in South Dakota.
trans: 这家人住在阿伯丁（Aberdeen），一个位于南达科他州（South Dakota）的小镇上，该镇共有23,000名居民。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: As the parents had five children, life was a perpetual struggle against poverty.
trans: 由于这对父母有五个孩子，他们的生活始终在与贫困作斗争。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: They were expecting their sixth child and were faced with even more pressing economic problems.
trans: 他们即将迎来第六个孩子，同时也面临着更加紧迫的经济问题。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: If they had only had one more child, the fact would have passed unnoticed.
trans: 如果他们再多要一个孩子的话，这件事可能就会被忽视、无人注意了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: They would have continued to struggle against economic odds and would have lived in obscurity.
trans: 他们本会继续在艰难的经济环境中挣扎，过着默默无闻的生活。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: But they suddenly became the parents of quintuplets, four girls and a boy, an event which radically changed their lives.
trans: 但他们突然成为了五胞胎的父母——四个女孩和一个男孩，这一事件彻底改变了他们的生活。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: The day after the birth of the five children, an aeroplane arrived in Aberdeen bringing sixty reporters and photographers.
trans: 在五个孩子出生的第二天，一架飞机抵达阿伯丁，带来了六十名记者和摄影师。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: The rise to fame was swift.
trans: 他的成名之路非常迅速。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Television cameras and newspapers carried the news to everyone in the country.
trans: 电视摄像机与报纸将这一消息传遍了全国的每一个人。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Newspapers and magazines offered the family huge sums for the exclusive rights to publish stories and photographs.
trans: 报纸和杂志向这家人提供了巨额报酬，以获得独家报道这些事件和发布相关照片的权利。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Gifts poured in not only from unknown people,
trans: 礼物不仅来自素未谋面的人……
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
trans: 而是来自那些希望宣传自己产品的婴儿食品制造商和肥皂制造商。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: The old farmhouse the family lived in was to be replaced by a new $500, 000 home.
trans: 他们曾经居住的旧农舍将被一座价值50万美元的新房子所取代。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Reporters kept pressing for interviews so lawyers had to be employed to act as spokesmen for the family at press conferences.
trans: 记者们不断要求进行采访，因此公司不得不聘请律师在新闻发布会上作为家属的发言人。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: While the five babies were still quietly sleeping in oxygen tents in a hospital nursery,
trans: 当这五个婴儿还在医院婴儿房的氧气帐篷里安静地睡着时……
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: their parents were paying the price for fame.
trans: 他们的父母正在为他们的名气付出代价。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: It would never again be possible for them to lead normal lives.
trans: 他们再也无法过上正常的生活了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: They had become the victims of commercialization, for their names had acquired a market value.
trans: 他们成为了商业化的受害者，因为他们的名字已经具有了市场价值。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Instead of being five new family members, these children had immediately become a commodity.
trans: 这些孩子并没有成为家庭中的新成员（即没有得到应有的关爱和接纳），反而立刻被当作商品来对待了。
lesson: NCE3 · The Power of the Press

name: Do it yourself
trans: 自己动手做吧。

name: Did the writer repair his lawn mower in the end? Why/Why not?
trans: 最后，作者修好了他的割草机吗？为什么修好（或者为什么没有修好）？

name: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves,
trans: 我们对为自己做事的热情是如此之强烈。

name: that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labour.
trans: 这意味着我们越来越不依赖专业劳动力了。

name: No one can plead ignorance of a subject any longer, for there are countless do-it-yourself publications.
trans: 如今，再没有人能够以“对某个主题一无所知”为借口了，因为市面上有数不胜数的 DIY（自己动手做）类出版物可供参考。

name: Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
trans: 配备了合适的工具和材料后，新婚夫妇便兴高采烈地开始装饰自己的家。

name: Men, particularly, spend hours of their leisure time installing their own fireplaces,
trans: 尤其是男性，他们会花费大量的闲暇时间来自己安装壁炉。

name: laying out their own gardens; building garages and making furniture.
trans: 他们自己规划花园的布局，建造车库，并制作家具。

name: Some really keen enthusiasts go so far as to build their own computers.
trans: 一些非常热衷的爱好者甚至会自己组装电脑。

name: Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze not only by running special advisory services for novices,
trans: 商店们不仅为初学者提供专门的咨询服务，还通过各种方式迎合了人们“自己动手做”的潮流。

name: but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
trans: 而是通过向消费者提供一些零散的部件，让他们可以在家中自己将这些部件组装起来。

name: Such things provide an excellent outlet for pent up creative energy, but unfortunately not all of us are born handymen.
trans: 这类活动为人们提供了释放内心创造力的绝佳途径，可惜并不是每个人天生就擅长动手做事（或：并不是每个人天生都具备动手能力）。

name: Some wives tend to believe that their husbands are infinitely resourceful and can fix anything.
trans: 有些妻子总是认为自己的丈夫无所不能，什么问题都能解决。

name: Even men who can hardly drive a nail in straight are supposed to be born electricians, carpenters, plumbers and mechanics.
trans: 即使是那些连把钉子都钉不直的男人，也被认为天生就适合从事电工、木匠、水管工或机械师等工作。

name: When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged, or vacuum cleaners fail to operate,
trans: 当灯泡烧坏时，家具就会变得摇摇晃晃；当管道堵塞时，水就无法正常流动；而当吸尘器无法正常工作时，清洁工作也就无法完成了。

name: some women assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
trans: 有些女性认为，她们的丈夫会想办法把事情解决好。

name: The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game is that sometimes even men live under the delusion that they can do anything,
trans: 自助游戏（即玩家需要自己完成所有任务的游戏）最糟糕的地方在于：有时候，就连男性也会误以为自己无所不能。

name: even when they have repeatedly been proved wrong.
trans: 即使他们的观点已经被多次证明是错误的，他们仍然坚持自己的立场。

name: It is a question of pride as much as anything else.
trans: 这不仅仅是一个关乎利益的问题，更是一个关乎尊严和自豪感的问题。

name: Last spring my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
trans: 去年春天，我妻子建议我请一位专业人士来检查一下我们的割草机。

name: It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
trans: 它在前一个夏天就坏掉了，虽然我答应过要修理它，但一直没能抽空去修。

name: I would not hear of the suggestion and said that I would fix it myself.
trans: 我根本不会考虑这个建议，而是表示我会自己解决这个问题。

name: One Saturday afternoon, I hauled the machine into the garden and had a close look at it.
trans: 一个星期六的下午，我把那台机器搬到了花园里，仔细地观察了它一番。

name: As far as I could see, it needed only a minor adjustment:
trans: 据我所见，它只需要进行微小的调整即可。

name: a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil and it would be as good as new.
trans: 只要在这里拧紧一个螺丝，再在那里稍微调紧一点，再滴上一点油，它就能像新的一样好用啦。

name: Inevitably the repair job was not quite so simple.
trans: 不可避免地，这次维修工作并没有那么简单。

name: The mower firmly refused to mow, so I decided to dismantle it.
trans: 那台割草机坚决不肯工作（即不肯进行割草操作），于是我决定把它拆开检查。

name: The garden was soon littered with chunks of metal which had once made up a lawn mower.
trans: 花园里很快就散落着许多金属碎片——那些碎片原本是割草机的一部分。

name: But I was extremely pleased with myself. I had traced the cause of the trouble.
trans: 但我对自己感到非常满意。我已经找到了问题的根源。

name: One of the links in the chain that drives the wheels had snapped.
trans: 驱动机器运转的链条中的某个环节断裂了。

name: After buying a new chain I was faced with the insurmountable task of putting the confusing jigsaw puzzle together again.
trans: 买了一条新链条后，我面临着一个看似无法完成的任务：那就是重新组装这个复杂得像拼图一样的装置。

name: I was not surprised to find that the machine still refused to work after I had reassembled it,
trans: 当我重新组装好这台机器后，发现它仍然无法正常工作时，我并不感到惊讶。

name: for the simple reason that I was left with several curiously shaped bits of metal which did not seem to fit anywhere.
trans: 原因很简单：我手里留着几块形状奇特的金属碎片，它们似乎根本无法被用到任何地方（即没有合适的用途）。

name: I gave up in despair.
trans: 我绝望地放弃了。

name: The weeks passed and the grass grew.
trans: 几周过去了，草也长高了。

name: When my wife nagged me to do something about it,
trans: 当我妻子催促我采取行动时……

name: I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower or let the grass grow.
trans: 我告诉她，要么我得买一台新的割草机，要么就任由草继续长下去。

name: Needless to say our house is now surrounded by a jungle.
trans: 不用说，我们的房子现在被一片“丛林”包围了（即周围长满了各种植物）。

name: Buried somewhere in deep grass there is a rusting lawn mower which I have promised to repair one day.
trans: 在茂密的草丛中，埋着一把生锈的割草机；我曾承诺有朝一日一定会把它修好。

name: Too high a price?
trans: 价格太高了吗？

name: What does the writer describe as an 'amusing old-fashioned source of noise' ?
trans: 作者将什么描述为“一种有趣的老式噪音来源”？

name: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, overindustrialized planet.
trans: 污染是我们这个人口过剩、过度工业化的星球所必须付出的代价。

name: When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish:
trans: 仔细想想，处理垃圾其实只有四种方法：

name: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
trans: 把它扔掉、烧掉，或者把它改造成可以再次使用的东西；尽量减少它的生产量。

name: We keep trying all four methods, but sheer volume of rubbish we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us.
trans: 我们一直在尝试这四种方法，但全球产生的垃圾数量实在庞大，几乎让我们应接不暇。

name: Rubbish, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet.
trans: 然而，垃圾仅仅是污染我们地球问题的一个方面罢了。

name: The need to produce ever increasing quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution.
trans: 对廉价食品日益增长的需求导致了另一种形式的污染。

name: Industriallized farming metheods produce cheap meat products: beef, pork and chicken.
trans: 工业化农业生产方式能够制造出价格低廉的肉类产品，包括牛肉、猪肉和鸡肉。

name: The use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables.
trans: 使用农药和化肥可以生产出价格低廉的谷物和蔬菜。

name: The price we pay for cheap food may be already too high:
trans: 我们为廉价食品所支付的价格可能已经太高了。

name: Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in cattle, salmonella in chicken and eggs, and listeria in dairy products.
trans: 牛的疯牛病（BSE）、鸡肉和鸡蛋中的沙门氏菌、乳制品中的李斯特菌……

name: And if you think you'll abandon meat and become a vegetarian,
trans: 如果你打算放弃吃肉、成为素食者，

name: you have the choice of very expensive organically-grown vegetables
trans: 你也有选择：要么购买价格昂贵的有机蔬菜，

name: or a steady diet of pesticides every time you think you're eating fresh salads and vegetables,
trans: 要么每次以为自己在吃新鲜沙拉或蔬菜时，其实都在摄入农药；

name: or just having an innocent glass of water!
trans: 或者，你也可以选择简单地喝一杯水……

name: However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that particularly affects urban area and invades our daily lives, and that is noise.
trans: 然而，还有一种更为隐蔽的污染形式，它尤其影响城市地区，并渗透到我们的日常生活中，那就是噪音。

name: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.
trans: 防盗警报在日夜任何时候突然响起，不仅会惹恼路人，反而会帮助窃贼作案；

name: Car alarms constantly scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation.
trans: 汽车警报声在街上不断刺耳地鸣叫，令人极度烦躁。

name: A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed (surprisingly?)
trans: 最近一项关于噪音影响的调查显示（令人惊讶的是），

name: that dogs barking incessantly in the night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from 1 to 7.
trans: 夜间狗不停地吠叫被列为噪音污染中最严重的形式（在1到7的评分体系中得分最高）。

name: The survey revealed a large number of sources of noise that we really dislike.
trans: 这项调查还揭示了许多我们非常讨厌的噪音来源：

name: Lawn mowers whining on a summer's day, late-night parties in apartment blocks,
trans: 夏日里割草机的嗡嗡声、公寓楼里的深夜聚会……

name: noisy neighbours, vehicles of all kinds,
trans: 吵闹的邻居们，各种各样的车辆……

name: especially large container trucks thundering through quiet villages,
trans: 尤其是那些巨大的集装箱卡车，在宁静的村庄里轰鸣着驶过……

name: planes and helicopters flying overhead, large radios carried round in public places and played at maximum volume.
trans: 飞机和直升机在头顶上飞过；在公共场所，人们会携带大型收音机，并将音量调至最大来播放音乐。

name: New technology has also made its own contribution to noise.
trans: 新技术本身也在一定程度上加剧了噪音问题（即：新技术的应用也导致了噪音的增加）。

name: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurant or on public transport.
trans: 很多人反对在公共场所（如餐厅或公共交通工具上）使用手机。

name: Loud conversations on mobile phones invade our thoughts or interrupt the pleasure of meeting friends for a quiet chat.
trans: 手机上大声的通话声会干扰我们的思绪，或者打断我们与朋友安静交谈的乐趣。

name: The noise pollution survey revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise.
trans: 噪音污染调查显示，噪音的来源其实是一个相当令人惊讶、甚至有点“古怪”的老式设备（或装置）。

name: It turned out to be snoring! Men were found to be the worst offenders.
trans: 原来问题出在打鼾上！研究发现，男性是打鼾问题最严重的群体。

name: It was revealed that 20% of men in their mid-thirties snore.
trans: 据调查显示，20%的三十多岁男性有打鼾的习惯。

name: This figure rises to a staggering 60% of men in their sixties.
trans: 这个比例高达60%，尤其是在六十多岁的男性中。

name: Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly,
trans: 与这些数据相比，研究发现只有5%的女性经常打鼾。

name: while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
trans: 而其他动物则不断地被它们的“喇叭声”（即叫声）吵醒，或者被迫保持清醒状态。

name: Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.
trans: 无论噪音的来源是什么，有一点是肯定的：沉默似乎已经成为了一段珍贵的回忆。

name: The silent village
trans: 寂静的村庄

name: Why was the village silent?
trans: 为什么这个村庄如此寂静？

name: In this much-travelled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.
trans: 在这个充满旅行的世界里，仍然有成千上万的地方对游客来说是无法到达的。

name: We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable.
trans: 在这个充满旅行的世界里，仍有成千上万的地方对游客来说难以到达。

name: But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen can be hostile to travellers.
trans: 我们总是认为偏远地区的村民友好且好客。

name: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable--as my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
trans: 然而，那些与外界隔绝的人——无论是与外国游客还是与自己的同胞——都可能对旅行者怀有敌意。

name: We had spent several days in a small town and visited a number of old churches in the vicinity.
trans: 真正偏远村庄的游览往往并不愉快——我和妻子在巴尔干半岛旅行时就深有体会。

name: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
trans: 我们在一个小镇上待了几天，还参观了几座古老的教堂。这些教堂不仅建筑风格独特，还保存着许多精美的壁画。

name: On the day before our departure, several bus loads of tourists descended on the town.
trans: 出发前一天，一大批游客乘巴士来到了这个小镇。

name: This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside.
trans: 这让我们难以忍受，于是我们决定在最后一天去乡村探索一番。

name: Taking a path which led out of the town, we crossed a few fields until we came to a dense wood.
trans: 我们沿着一条小路离开小镇，穿过几片田野，最终来到了一片茂密的森林。

name: We expected the path to end abruptly, but we found that it traced its way through the trees.
trans: 我们原本以为这条小路会突然结束，但实际上它蜿蜒穿过树林，继续延伸下去。

name: We tramped through the wood for over two hours until we arrived at a deep stream.
trans: 我们跋涉穿过森林，花了两个多小时的时间，终于来到了一条湍急的小溪边。

name: We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how we could get across the stream.
trans: 我们可以看到小路在另一边继续延伸，但我们完全不知道该如何穿过那条小溪。

name: Suddenly my wife spotted a boat moored to the bank.
trans: 突然，我的妻子发现有一艘船停靠在岸边。

name: In it there was a boatman fast asleep.
trans: 里面有一个正在熟睡的船夫。

name: We gently woke him up and asked him to ferry us to the other side.
trans: 我们轻轻地唤醒了他，然后请他带我们到另一边去。

name: Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us.
trans: 虽然他一开始并不愿意，但我们最终说服了他带我们一起去。

name: The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
trans: 这条小路通向一个坐落在陡峭山坡上的小村庄。

name: The place consisted of a straggling unmade road which was lined on either side by small houses.
trans: 这个地方有一条蜿蜒曲折、尚未铺好的道路，道路两旁排列着一些小房子。

name: Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked forbidding, as all the houses were built of grey mud bricks.
trans: 即使是在万里无云的蓝天下，这个村庄看起来依然令人望而生畏——所有的房屋都是用灰色的泥砖建造的。

name: The village seemed deserted,
trans: 这个村庄看起来像是被遗弃了。

name: the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
trans: 唯一的生命迹象是一只长相丑陋的黑色山羊，它被用一根短绳子拴在附近田野里的一棵树上。

name: Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of tins of sardines and had a picnic lunch.
trans: 我们坐在田野旁边那道破旧的木栅栏旁，打开了几罐沙丁鱼，然后享用了一顿野餐午餐。

name: All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
trans: 突然间，我注意到我的妻子似乎充满了恐慌（或：显得非常焦虑）。

name: Looking up I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently as we ate.
trans: 我查了一下后发现，我们周围围着一群衣衫褴褛的孩子们；当我们吃饭时，他们静静地注视着我们。

name: We offered them food and spoke to them kindly, but they remained motionless.
trans: 我们给了他们食物，并用温和的语气与他们交谈，但他们依然一动不动。

name: I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.
trans: 我得出结论：他们只是对陌生人感到害羞而已。

name: When we later walked down the main street of the village, we were followed by a silent procession of children.
trans: 后来，当我们沿着村庄的主街走去时，有一群沉默的孩子们跟在我们后面。
