name: The village which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
trans: 这个原本看似荒无人烟的村庄立刻变得热闹起来。

name: Faces appeared at windows.
trans: 人们的身影出现在窗户前。

name: Men in shirt sleeves stood outside their houses and glared at us.
trans: 那些只穿着衬衫、没有穿外套的男人们站在自家房子外面，怒视着我们。

name: Old women in black shawls peered at us from doorways.
trans: 那些披着黑色披肩的老妇人从门缝里向我们张望。

name: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
trans: 最可怕的是，竟然一点声音都听不到。

name: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
trans: 毫无疑问，我们是不受欢迎的访客。

name: We needed no further warning.
trans: 我们不需要任何进一步的警告。

name: Turning back down the main street,
trans: 拐回主街道后，

name: we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly towards the stream where we hoped the boatman was waiting.
trans: 我们加快了步伐，迅速朝小溪走去，希望船夫正在那里等着我们。

name: The ideal servant
trans: 理想的仆人

name: What was Bessie's 'little weakness' ?
trans: 贝西的“小缺点”是什么？

name: It is a good thing my aunt Harriet died years ago.
trans: 幸好我的阿姨哈丽特几年前就去世了。

name: If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation: domestic servants.
trans: 如果她今天还活着，她将无法再公开表达自己最热衷讨论的话题——也就是关于家庭佣人的看法了。

name: Aunt Harriet lived in that leisurely age when servants were employed to do housework.
trans: 哈丽特阿姨生活在那个时代：那时人们还会雇佣仆人来帮忙做家务。

name: She had a huge, rambling country house called 'The Gables'.
trans: 她拥有一座规模庞大、布局错综复杂的乡村住宅，名叫“The Gables”。

name: She was sentimentally attached to this house,
trans: 她对这栋房子怀有深厚的情感依恋。

name: for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband's death.
trans: 尽管那套房子远远超出了她的实际需求（空间太大，不符合她的居住要求），但在丈夫去世后，她仍然坚持住在那里很长时间。

name: Before she grew old, aunt Harriet used to entertain lavishly.
trans: 在哈丽特阿姨年老之前，她总是非常热情地招待客人，总是准备丰盛的美食和精彩的娱乐活动来款待他们。

name: I often visited The Gables when I was a boy.
trans: 我小时候经常去“The Gables”那个地方。

name: No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.
trans: 无论有多少客人来访，那座宏伟的房子总是保持得一尘不染、整洁有序。

name: The parquet floors shone like mirrors;
trans: 镶木地板闪闪发光，就像镜子一样。

name: highly polished silver was displayed in gleaming glass cabinets;
trans: 那些经过精心打磨的银器被陈列在闪闪发光的玻璃柜中。

name: even my uncle's huge collection of books was kept miraculously free from dust.
trans: 就连我叔叔那庞大的藏书量，也奇迹般地没有一点灰尘。

name: Aunt Harriet presided over an invisible army of servants that continuously scrubbed, cleaned, and polished.
trans: 哈丽特阿姨指挥着一支“看不见的仆人队伍”，这支队伍不断地擦拭、清洁和抛光各种物品。

name: She always referred to them as 'the shifting population',
trans: 她总是把他们称为“流动的人口”（即那些不断迁移、居无定所的人群）。

name: for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.
trans: 因为他们来得频繁，去得也快，以至于我根本没机会记住他们的名字。

name: Though my aunt pursued what was, in those days an enlightened policy,
trans: 尽管我的姑姑在当时推行了一项被认为具有前瞻性的政策，

name: in that she never allowed her domestic staff to work more than eight hours a day, she was extremely difficult to please.
trans: 因为她从不允许家中的佣人每天工作超过八小时，所以她非常难以取悦。

name: While she always criticized the fickleness of human nature,
trans: 虽然她总是批评人性的善变，

name: she carried on an unrelenting search for the ideal servant to the end of her days,
trans: 她一生都在不懈地寻找那个理想的仆人，直到生命的最后一刻。

name: even after she had been sadly disillusioned by Bessie.
trans: 即使在她被贝西（Bessie）彻底打消了所有希望之后……

name: Bessie worked for aunt Harriet for three years.
trans: 贝西在哈丽特阿姨家工作了三年。

name: During that time she so gained my aunt's confidence, that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.
trans: 在那段时间里，她赢得了我阿姨的充分信任，以至于被委以管理所有家务人员的重任。

name: Aunt Harriet could not find words to praise Bessie's industriousness and efficiency.
trans: 哈丽特阿姨实在找不到合适的词语来赞扬贝西的勤奋和高效。

name: In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.
trans: 除了拥有其他各种技能外，贝西还是一位烹饪高手。

name: She acted the role of the perfect servant for three years before Aunt Harriet discovered her 'little weakness'.
trans: 她扮演了“完美仆人”的角色长达三年，直到哈丽特阿姨发现了她的“小缺点”。

name: After being absent from The Gables for a week,
trans: 在缺席了《The Gables》节目一周之后……

name: my aunt unexpectedly returned one afternoon with a party of guests and instructed Bessie to prepare dinner.
trans: 一天下午，我的阿姨突然带着一群客人回来了，她吩咐贝西准备晚餐。

name: Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.
trans: 这顿饭的质量远低于平时的标准；而且贝西似乎也走不稳了。

name: She bumped into the furniture and kept mumbling about the guests.
trans: 她撞到了家具，然后不停地嘟囔着关于那些客人的事情。

name: When she came in with the last course--a huge pudding--she tripped on the carpet
trans: 当她端着最后一道菜（一道巨大的布丁）进来时，她在地毯上绊倒了。

name: and the pudding went flying through the air, narrowly missed my aunt, and crashed on the dining table with considerable force.
trans: 布丁突然飞到了空中，差点撞到我的阿姨，然后猛烈地摔在了餐桌上。

name: Though this caused great mirth among the guests, Aunt Harriet was horrified.
trans: 虽然这引起了在场宾客们的阵阵笑声，但哈丽特阿姨却感到非常震惊。

name: She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.
trans: 她勉强得出结论：贝西肯定是喝醉了。

name: The guests had, of course, realized this from the moment Bessie opened the door for them and, long before the final catastrophe,
trans: 当然，客人们从贝西为他们开门的那一刻起就意识到了这一点；早在最终灾难发生之前，他们就已经察觉到了不对劲。

name: had had a difficult time trying to conceal their amusement.
trans: 他们很难掩饰自己的笑意。

name: The poor girl was dismissed instantly.
trans: 那个可怜的女孩立刻就被解雇了。

name: After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles of all shapes and sizes neatly stacked in what had once been Bessie's wardrobe.
trans: 在她离开后，哈丽特阿姨发现：曾经是贝西衣柜的地方，现在整齐地堆放着一堆堆形状各异、大小不一的空酒瓶。

name: They had mysteriously found their way there from the wine cellar!
trans: 它们竟然神秘地从酒窖里找到了通往那里的路！

name: New Year resolutions
trans: 新年决心

name: What marked the end of the writer's New Year resolutions?
trans: 是什么标志着这位作家新年决心的结束呢？

name: The New Year is a time for resolutions.
trans: 新年是一个制定新目标的时刻。

name: Mentally, at least, most of us could compile formidable lists of 'dos' and 'don'ts'.
trans: 至少在精神层面上，我们大多数人都能列出一份详尽的“该做”与“不该做”的清单。

name: The same old favourites recur year in year out with monotonous regularity.
trans: 那些老掉牙的、令人厌烦的节目每年都如出一辙地重复上演，毫无新意可言。

name: We resolve to get up earlier each morning, eat less,
trans: 我们决定每天早上早起一些，少吃一些食物。

name: find more time to play with the children, do a thousand and one jobs about the house,
trans: 多花些时间陪孩子们玩耍，同时还要处理家里的各种琐事（比如打扫卫生、做饭、洗衣服等等）。

name: be nice to people we don't like, drive carefully, and take the dog for a walk every day.
trans: 对待那些我们不喜欢的人也要友善；开车时要小心谨慎；每天还要带狗狗去散步。

name: Past experience has taught us that certain accomplishments are beyond attainment.
trans: 过去的经验告诉我们，有些成就其实是无法实现的。

name: If we remain inveterate smokers, it is only because we have so often experienced the frustration that results from failure.
trans: 如果我们仍然坚持吸烟，那只是因为我们太多次地经历了因吸烟失败而带来的挫败感。

name: Most of us fail in our efforts at sel-improvement because our schemes are too ambitious and we never have time to carry them out.
trans: 我们大多数人在自我提升的努力中都失败了，原因在于我们的计划过于雄心勃勃，以至于我们根本没有时间去实施它们。

name: We also make the fundamental error of announcing our resolutions to everybody
trans: 我们还有一个根本性的错误：那就是把我们的决心或计划公之于众。

name: so that we look even more foolish when we slip back into our bad old ways.
trans: 这样，当我们重新回到那些糟糕的老习惯时，看起来就会更加愚蠢了。

name: Aware of these pitfalls, this year I attempted to keep my resolutions to myself.
trans: 意识到这些潜在的陷阱，今年我决定将自己的新年决心只对自己保密（即不告诉任何人）。

name: I limited myself to two modest ambitions: to do physical exercises every morning and to read more of an evening.
trans: 我给自己设定了两个简单的目标：每天早上坚持做体育锻炼，晚上多读书。

name: An all-night party on New Year's Eve provided me with a good excuse for not carrying out either of these new resolutions on the first day of the year,
trans: 新年前夜的通宵派对为我提供了一个很好的借口，让我能够在新年的第一天不执行任何这些新年决心。

name: but on the second, I applied myself assiduously to the task.
trans: 但第二次时，我全身心地投入到这项任务中，付出了极大的努力。

name: The daily exercises lasted only eleven minutes and I proposed to do them early in the morning before anyone had got up.
trans: 每天的锻炼时间只有十一分钟，我建议在清晨大家还没起床的时候进行这些锻炼。

name: The self-discipline required to drag myself out of bed 11 minutes earlier than usual was considerable.
trans: 为了比平时早11分钟起床，我必须克服极大的自我惰性（即强烈的懒惰心理）。

name: Nevertheless, I managed to creep down into the living room for two days before anyone found me out.
trans: 尽管如此，我还是设法悄悄地躲进了客厅，并在那里待了两天，直到最后才被人发现。

name: After jumping about on the carpet and twisting the human frame into uncomfortable positions,
trans: 在毯子上跳来跳去、把人的身体扭成各种不舒服的姿势之后……

name: I sat down at the breakfast table in an exhausted condition.
trans: 我疲惫不堪地坐到了早餐桌前。

name: It was this that betrayed me.
trans: 正是这一点背叛了我。

name: The next morning the whole family trooped in to watch the performance.
trans: 第二天早上，全家人都聚在一起观看这场表演。

name: That was really unsettling but I fended off the taunts and jibes of the family good-humouredly and soon everybody got used to the idea.
trans: 那确实让人感到不安，但我以乐观的态度回应了家人的嘲笑和讥讽，很快大家都接受了这个事实。

name: However, my enthusiasm waned.
trans: 然而，我的热情逐渐消退了。

name: The time I spent at exercises gradually diminished.
trans: 我花在锻炼上的时间逐渐减少了。

name: Little by little the eleven minutes fell to zero.
trans: 慢慢地，那十一分钟的时间一分一秒地过去了，最终归零了。

name: By January 10th, I was back to where I had started from.
trans: 到了1月10日，我又回到了起点。

name: I argued that if I spent less time exhausting myself at exercises in the morning,
trans: 我认为，如果我早上在锻炼上花费的时间少一些，就不会那么容易精疲力竭了。

name: I would keep my mind fresh for reading when I got home from work.
trans: 我会在下班回家后，通过一些轻松的活动来让大脑保持清醒、放松的状态，以便更好地进行阅读。

name: Resisting the hypnotizing effect of television,
trans: 抗拒电视的催眠效果……

name: I sat in my room for a few evenings with my eyes glued to a book.
trans: 有几个晚上，我一直坐在房间里，眼睛紧盯着书本看个不停。

name: One night, however, feeling cold and lonely, I went downstairs and sat in front of the television pretending to read.
trans: 然而，有一天晚上，我感到寒冷又孤独，于是下楼坐在电视机前，假装在看书。

name: That proved to be my undoing, for I soon got back to my old bad habit of dozing off in front of the screen.
trans: 结果这成了我的祸根——因为我很快又恢复了那个老毛病：在屏幕前打瞌睡。

name: I still haven't given up my resolution to do more reading.
trans: 我仍然没有放弃多读书的决心。

name: In fact, I have just bought a book entitled How to Read a Thousand Words a Minute.
trans: 事实上，我刚刚买了一本书，书名是《如何一分钟读完一千个单词》。

name: Perhaps it will solve my problem, but I just haven't had time to read it!
trans: 也许这本书能解决我的问题，只是我还没时间去读它罢了！

name: Predicting the future
trans: 预测未来

name: What was the 'future' electronic development that Leon Bagrit wasn't able to foresee?
trans: 莱昂·巴格里特未能预见的、未来电子技术的发展是什么？

name: Predicting the future is notoriously difficult.
trans: 预测未来向来是一件极其困难的事情。

name: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, for example,
trans: 谁能想到呢？比如说，在20世纪70年代中期……

name: that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people's homes as TV sets?
trans: 到20世纪末，计算机会在人们的家中变得像电视机一样普遍吗？

name: In the 1970s, computers were common enough,
trans: 在20世纪70年代，计算机已经变得相当普及了。

name: but only in big business, government departments and large organizations.
trans: 但这仅限于大企业、政府部门以及大型组织。

name: These were the so-called mainframe machines.
trans: 这些就是所谓的“大型机”（mainframe machines）。

name: Mainframe computers were very large indeed often occupying whole air-conditioned rooms,
trans: 大型机确实体积庞大，常常占据整个装有空调的房间。

name: employing full-time technicians and run on specially-written software.
trans: 这些系统配备了全职技术人员进行维护，并运行着专门开发的软件。

name: Though these large machines still exist,
trans: 尽管这些大型机器仍然存在，

name: many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
trans: 它们的许多功能已经被功能强大、体积小巧的个人电脑（通常称为“PC”）所取代了。

name: In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair, was launched in the USA.
trans: 1975年，一种名为 Altair 的早期计算机在美国问世。

name: It can properly be described as the first 'home computer' and it pointed the way to the future.
trans: 它完全可以被称作第一台“家用电脑”，并且为未来的发展方向指明了方向。

name: This was followed, at the end of the 1970s, by a machine called an Apple.
trans: 随后，在20世纪70年代末，出现了一种名为“Apple”的机器。

name: In the early 1980s, the computer giant, IBM produced the world's first Personal Computer.
trans: 20世纪80年代初，计算机巨头IBM推出了世界上第一台个人电脑（Personal Computer）。

name: This ran on an 'operating system' called DOS,
trans: 这个程序运行在一个名为 DOS 的“操作系统”上。

name: produced by a then small company named Microsoft.
trans: 这款产品是由当时还是一家小型公司的微软（Microsoft）开发的。

name: The IBM Personal Computer was widely copied.
trans: IBM个人电脑被广泛地模仿和复制。

name: From those humble beginnings,
trans: 从那些卑微的起点开始，

name: we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
trans: 我们已经见证了如今广泛使用的、用户友好的家用电脑和多媒体设备的不断发展。

name: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman,
trans: 考虑到这些发展都发生得如此之近，更令人惊讶的是：早在20世纪60年代，就有一位英国人……

name: Leon Bagrit, was able to predict some of the uses of computers which we know today.
trans: 莱昂·巴格里特（Leon Bagrit）成功预测了计算机的一些现今已被广泛应用的用途。

name: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves and would 'rule the world', which people liked to believe in those days.
trans: 巴格里特驳斥了这样一种观点：计算机能够学会“自主思考”并“统治世界”。在那个时候，许多人确实相信这种可能性。

name: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand,
trans: 巴格里特预见了一个时代：那时计算机会变得足够小巧，可以放在手中使用。

name: when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alterative routes,
trans: 当它们能够提供关于交通拥堵的信息，并建议替代路线时……

name: when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses,
trans: 当这些技术被应用于医院时，它们将帮助医生诊断疾病。

name: when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
trans: 当这些技术能够减轻办公室工作人员和会计们的那些枯燥、重复性的文书工作时……

name: All these computer uses have become commonplace.
trans: 所有这些计算机的使用方式都已经变得非常普遍了。

name: Of course, Leon Bagrit couldn't possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet,
trans: 当然，莱昂·巴格里特根本不可能预见到互联网的发展。

name: the worldwide system that enables us to communicate instantly with anyone in any part of the world by using computers linked to telephone networks.
trans: 这个全球性的系统让我们能够通过连接到电话网络的计算机，与世界上任何地方的任何人即时进行交流。

name: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information on every known subject,
trans: 他也无法预见到我们如何能够利用互联网来获取关于所有已知主题的信息。

name: so we can read it on a screen in our homes and even print it as well if we want to.
trans: 这样我们就可以在家里的屏幕上阅读它了；如果需要的话，也可以将其打印出来。

name: Computers have become smaller and smaller, more and more powerful and cheaper and cheaper.
trans: 计算机变得越来越小，性能越来越强大，价格也越来越便宜。

name: This is what makes Leon Bagrit's predictions particularly remarkable.
trans: 这正是让莱昂·巴格里特的预测显得格外引人注目的原因。

name: If he, or someone like him, were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.
trans: 如果他，或者像他这样的人，今天还活着，他或许能够告诉我们未来五十年会发生什么。

name: Mud is mud
trans: 泥就是泥；无论它在哪里，本质都是一样的。

name: Why did Harry decide to give up his little game?
trans: 为什么哈利决定放弃他的那个小把戏（或：为什么哈利决定不再玩那个小游戏）？

name: My cousin, Harry, keeps a large curiously-shaped bottle on permanent display in his study.
trans: 我的表弟哈里在他的书房里永久性地展示着一个形状非常奇特的瓶子。

name: Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green,
trans: 尽管这个瓶子的颜色是一种淡雅的绿色，

name: an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, greyish substance.
trans: 一个细心的访客很快就会注意到，这个空间里充满了某种看起来像浓稠的、灰褐色的物质。

name: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
trans: 如果你问哈利瓶子里装的是什么，他会告诉你里面装的是香味的泥浆。

name: If you expressed doubt or surprise, he would immediately invite you to smell it and then to rub some into your skin.
trans: 如果你表现出怀疑或惊讶，他就会立刻邀请你闻一闻这种物质，然后让你把它涂抹在皮肤上。

name: The brief experiment would dispel any further doubts she might have.
trans: 这个简短的实验将会消除她可能存在的任何疑虑。

name: The bottle really does contain perfumed mud.
trans: 这个瓶子里确实装着带有香味的泥浆。

name: How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story which he is fond of relating.
trans: 哈利是如何得到这些奇怪物品的，这本身就是一个有趣的故事，而他也很喜欢讲这个故事。

name: Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.
trans: 此外，买到这个瓶子后，他改掉了自己多年来一直养成的一个坏习惯。

name: Harry used to consider it a great joke to go into expensive cosmetic shops and make outrageous requests for goods that do not exist.
trans: 哈里过去常常觉得：去那些高档的化妆品店，然后提出一些根本不存在的商品、并要求购买这些商品，这简直是个天大的笑话。

name: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
trans: 他总能即兴想出一些奇特、富有想象力的名字。

name: On entering a shop,
trans: 当走进一家商店时，

name: he would ask for a new perfume called 'Scented Shadow' or for 'insoluble bath cubes'.
trans: 他会要求购买一款名为“Scented Shadow”的新香水，或者“insoluble bath cubes”（即不可溶解的浴盐块）。

name: If a shop assistant told him she had not heard of it, he would pretend to be considerably put out.
trans: 如果店员告诉他她从未听说过那个产品，他就会假装非常失望（或很不高兴）。

name: He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock
trans: 他很喜欢听到这样的消息：他想象中的某个产品暂时缺货了。

name: and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
trans: 他会诚实地承诺会在未来的某个时候再次打电话，但当然，他从未兑现过这个承诺。

name: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
trans: 我实在无法理解：哈利在那些表演过程中是如何始终保持面无表情的……

name: Harry does not need to be prompted to explain how he bought his precious bottle of mud.
trans: 哈利根本不需要别人提醒，他就能解释自己是如何买到那瓶珍贵的“泥”的。

name: One day, he went to an exclusive shop in London and asked for 'Myrolite'.
trans: 有一天，他去了伦敦的一家高档商店，询问是否有“Myrolite”这种商品。

name: The shop assistant looked puzzled and Harry repeated the word, slowly stressing each syllable.
trans: 店员看起来很困惑，于是哈利又重复了这个词，慢慢地、一个音节一个音节地念了出来。

name: When the woman shook her head in bewilderment,
trans: 当那位女士困惑地摇头时……

name: Harry went on to explain that 'myrolite' was a hard, amber-like substance which could be used to remove freckles.
trans: 哈里接着解释说，“myrolite”是一种质地坚硬、呈琥珀色的物质，可以用来去除雀斑。

name: This explanation evidently conveyed something to the woman who searched shelf after shelf.
trans: 这个解释显然让那位在货架间翻找东西的女士明白了些什么。

name: She produced all sorts of weird concoctions, but none of them met with Harry's requirements.
trans: 她制作了各种各样的奇怪混合物，但没有一种能满足哈里的要求。

name: When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.
trans: 当哈里装出一副有点恼火的样子时，助手答应会帮他订购一些东西。

name: Intoxicated by his success, Harry then asked for perfumed mud.
trans: 被自己的成功冲昏了头脑，哈里随后要求得到那种带有香味的泥浆。

name: He expected the assistant to look at him in blank astonishment.
trans: 他期待着助手会惊讶地、一脸茫然地看着他。

name: However, it was his turn to be surprised, for the woman's eyes immediately lit up
trans: 然而，轮到他感到惊讶了——因为那个女人的眼睛立刻亮了起来。

name: and she fetched several bottles which she placed on the counter for Harry to inspect.
trans: 然后她拿来了几瓶酒，把它们放在柜台上让哈里查看。

name: For once, Harry had to admit defeat.
trans: 这一次，哈利不得不承认自己失败了。

name: He picked up what seemed to be the smallest bottle and discreetly asked the price.
trans: 他拿起了那个看起来是最小的瓶子，然后悄悄地询问了价格。

name: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
trans: 他很高兴只被罚了二十英镑，于是急忙逃走了，同时紧紧地把那个珍贵的瓶子夹在腋下。

name: From then on, Harry decided that this little game he had invented might prove to be expensive.
trans: 从那以后，哈利意识到自己发明的这个“小游戏”可能会带来严重的后果（或者：这个小游戏可能会让他付出沉重的代价）。

name: The curious bottle which now adorns the bookcase in his study was his first and last purchase of rare cosmetics.
trans: 那个现在摆放在他书房书架上的奇特瓶子，是他第一次也是最后一次购买的稀有化妆品。

name: In the public interest
trans: 为了公共利益

name: What could not be reported in the official files?
trans: 有哪些内容是无法被记录在官方文件中的呢？

name: The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies.
trans: 斯堪的纳维亚国家因其开明的社会政策而受到全世界的广泛赞誉。

name: Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officers.
trans: 瑞典已经建立了一套非常完善的制度，旨在保护公民免受专横或无能的公职人员的侵害。

name: The system has worked so well, that it has been adopted in other countries too.
trans: 该系统运行得非常出色，因此也被其他国家采纳使用了。

name: The Swedes were the first to recognize that public officials like civil servants,
trans: 瑞典人是最早意识到像公务员这样的公职人员的重要性的人。

name: police officers, health inspectors or tax-collectors can make mistakes or act over-zealously in the belief that they are serving the public.
trans: 警察、卫生检查员或税务官员都可能犯错，或者因为自认为是在为公众服务而表现得过于热心（即行为过于激进）。

name: As long ago as 1809, the Swedish Parliament introduced a scheme to safeguard the interest of the individual.
trans: 早在1809年，瑞典议会就出台了一项旨在保护个人权益的方案。

name: A parliamentary committee representing all political parties appoints a person who is suitably qualified to investigate private grievances against the State.
trans: 一个代表所有政党的议会委员会，会任命一位具备适当资格的人来调查公民对政府提出的个人投诉（即私人不满）。

name: The official title of the person is 'Justiteombudsman', but the Swedes commonly refer to him as the 'J.O.' or 'Ombudsman'.
trans: 这个人的正式头衔是“司法监察专员”（Justice Ombudsman），但瑞典人通常称他为“J.O.”或“Ombudsman”。

name: The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure.
trans: 监察专员不受政治压力的影响。

name: He investigates complaints large and small that come to him from all levels of society.
trans: 他负责调查来自社会各个阶层的各种投诉，无论这些投诉的规模大小如何。

name: As complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of 1, 200 letters a year.
trans: 由于投诉必须以书面形式提出，因此监察专员每年平均会收到 1,200 封来信。

name: He has eight lawyer assistants to help him and he examines every single letter in detail.
trans: 他有八名律师助理协助他工作，他会仔细审查每一封信的内容。

name: There is nothing secretive about the Ombudsman's work, for his correspondence is open to public inspection.
trans: 监察专员的工作没有任何保密性；他的所有通信记录都可供公众查阅。

name: If a citizen's complaint is justified the Ombudsman will act on his behalf.
trans: 如果公民的投诉是合理的，监察专员将会代表该公民采取行动。

name: The action he takes varies according to the nature of the complaint.
trans: 他采取的行动会根据投诉的性质而有所不同。

name: He may gently reprimand an official or even suggest to parliament that a law be altered.
trans: 他可能会温和地告诫某位官员，甚至向议会提出修改法律的建议。

name: The following case is a typical example of the Ombudsman's work.
trans: 以下案例是监察专员工作的典型例子。

name: A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman complaining that he had been ill-treated by the police,
trans: 一位居住在瑞典村庄的外国人写信给监察专员，投诉称自己受到了警方的虐待。

name: simply because he was a foreigner.
trans: 仅仅因为他是外国人。

name: The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the Chief of Police in the district asking him to send a record of the case.
trans: 监察专员立即致函该地区的警察局长，要求他提供该案件的详细记录。

name: There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner's complaint was justified
trans: 记录中没有任何内容表明那位外国人的投诉是合理的（或：记录中没有任何证据支持该外国人的投诉）。

name: and the Chief of Police strongly denied the accusation.
trans: 警方局长强烈否认了这一指控。

name: It was impossible for the Ombudsman to take action,
trans: 监察员根本无法采取任何行动。

name: but when he received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village,
trans: 但是当他收到同一村庄里另一位外国人类似的投诉时……

name: he immediately sent one of his lawyers to investigate the matter.
trans: 他立即派了自己的律师去调查这件事。

name: The lawyer ascertained that a policeman had indeed dealt roughly with foreigners on several occasions.
trans: 律师证实，确实有警察在多次场合中对外国人采取了粗暴的态度。

name: The fact that the policeman was prejudiced against foreigners could not be recorded in the official files.
trans: 这名警察对外国人存在偏见这一事实，无法被记录在官方文件中。

name: It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts.
trans: 只有通过派遣他的代表去核实事实，监察员才得以发现这一情况。

name: The policeman in question was severely reprimanded
trans: 这名涉事的警察受到了严厉的处分。

name: and was informed that if any further complaints were lodged against him, he would be prosecuted.
trans: 并且被告知，如果再有人对他提出投诉，他将会被起诉。

name: The Ombudsman's prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.
trans: 监察专员的迅速行动立即制止了这一可能被忽视的不良行为。

name: Instinct or cleverness?
trans: 是本能，还是智慧？

name: Was the writer successful in protecting his peach tree? Why not?
trans: 作者成功保护了他的桃树吗？为什么没有呢？

name: We have been brought up to fear insects.
trans: 我们从小就被教导要害怕昆虫。

name: We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good.
trans: 我们认为它们是毫无必要的生物，带来的危害远大于好处。

name: We continually wage war on them, for they contaminate our food, carry diseases, or devour our crops.
trans: 我们一直在与它们作斗争——因为它们会污染我们的食物、传播疾病，或者啃食我们的庄稼。

name: They sting or bite without provocation; they fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights, or beat against our lighted windows.
trans: 它们会无缘无故地蜇人或咬人；在夏夜，它们会不请自来地飞进我们的房间，或者撞击我们亮着的窗户。

name: We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects like spiders or wasps, but of quite harmless ones like moths.
trans: 我们不仅害怕像蜘蛛或黄蜂这样的令人不快的昆虫，也害怕像蛾子这样其实完全无害的昆虫。

name: Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.
trans: 阅读关于他们的信息确实能增加我们的理解，但并不会消除我们的恐惧。

name: Knowing that the industrious ant lives in a highly organized society
trans: 我们知道，勤劳的蚂蚁生活在一种高度有序的社会中。

name: does nothing to prevent us from being filled with revulsion when we find hordes of them crawling over a carefully prepared picnic lunch.
trans: 这丝毫无法阻止我们看到成群这样的生物爬在我们精心准备的野餐食物上时感到极度厌恶。

name: No matter how much we like honey,
trans: 无论我们多么喜欢蜂蜜，

name: or how much we have read about the uncanny sense of direction which bees possess, we have a horror of being stung.
trans: 无论我们读过多少关于蜜蜂惊人方向感的描述，我们仍然对被蜜蜂蜇伤感到恐惧。

name: Most of our fears are unreasonable, but they are impossible to erase.
trans: 我们的大多数恐惧都是毫无道理的，但它们却无法被彻底消除。

name: At the same time, however, insects are strangely fascinating.
trans: 然而，昆虫同时又有一种奇妙的魅力，让人着迷。

name: We enjoy reading about them, especially when we find that, like the praying mantis, they lead perfectly horrible lives.
trans: 我们喜欢阅读关于它们的内容，尤其是当发现它们（就像螳螂一样）过着极其糟糕的生活时。

name: We enjoy staring at them, entranced as they go about their business, unaware (we hope) of our presence.
trans: 我们喜欢凝视着他们，看着他们忙着自己的事情；希望他们没有察觉到我们的存在。

name: Who has not stood in awe at the sight of a spider pouncing on a fly,
trans: 谁没有在看到蜘蛛突然扑向一只苍蝇的瞬间感到惊叹呢？

name: or a column of ants triumphantly bearing home an enormous dead beetle?
trans: 或者是一队蚂蚁，胜利地抬着一只巨大的死甲虫回家？

name: Last summer I spent days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
trans: 去年夏天，我在花园里待了好几天，观察成千上万的蚂蚁爬上我那棵珍贵的桃树的树干。

name: The tree has grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
trans: 这棵树生长在房子背风的一侧，紧靠着一面温暖的墙壁。

name: I am especially proud of it,
trans: 我对此感到特别自豪。

name: not only because it has survived several severe winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
trans: 不仅因为它经受住了几个严冬的考验，还因为它偶尔会结出美味的桃子。

name: During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
trans: 夏天时，我注意到树上的叶子开始枯萎了。

name: Clusters of tiny insects called aphides were to be found on the underside of the leaves.
trans: 在叶子的背面，可以发现一群被称为蚜虫的微小昆虫。

name: They were visited by a large colony of ants which obtained a sort of honey from them.
trans: 有一大群蚂蚁造访了它们，并从它们身上获取了一种类似蜂蜜的物质。

name: I immediately embarked on an experiment which even though it failed to get rid of the ants kept me fascinated for twenty-four hours.
trans: 我立刻开始了一项实验。尽管这项实验未能彻底消灭那些蚂蚁，但它让我着迷了整整24个小时。

name: I bound the base of the tree with sticky tape, making it impossible for the ants to reach the aphides.
trans: 我用透明胶带把树干的底部粘住了，这样蚂蚁就无法接触到蚜虫了。

name: The tape was so sticky that they did not dare to cross it.
trans: 胶带粘性太强了，他们不敢去穿过它。

name: For a long time, I watched them scurrying around the base of the tree in bewilderment.
trans: 很长一段时间里，我都困惑地看着它们在树根周围慌乱地穿梭来去。

name: I even went out at midnight with a torch and noted with satisfaction (and surprise)
trans: 我甚至在午夜时分拿着火把出门，并带着满足感（以及惊讶）记录下了所见的一切。

name: that the ants were still swarming around the sticky tape without being able to do anything about it.
trans: 那些蚂蚁仍在粘性胶带周围忙碌着，却对这种情况无能为力。

name: I got up early next morning hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
trans: 第二天早上我早早起床，希望看到蚂蚁们已经绝望地放弃了。

name: Instead, I saw that they had discovered a new route.
trans: 相反，我发现他们发现了一条新的路线。

name: They were climbing up the wall of the house and then on to the leaves of the tree.
trans: 它们沿着房子的墙壁爬上去，然后又爬到了树上的叶子上。

name: I realized sadly that I had been completely defeated by their ingenuity.
trans: 遗憾的是，我发现自己完全被他们的聪明才智给打败了。

name: The ants had been quick to find an answer to my thoroughly unscientific methods!
trans: 蚂蚁们很快就找到了对我那些完全不科学的方法的“答案”！

name: From the earth: Greetings
trans: 来自地球的问候：

name: Which life forms are most likely to develop on a distant planet?
trans: 哪些生命形式最有可能在遥远的行星上出现？

name: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.
trans: 天文学的最新发展使得我们能够探测到我们自己的银河系以及其他星系中的行星。

name: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.
trans: 天文学的最新进展使我们能够探测到我们银河系及其他星系中的行星。

name: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
trans: 这是一个重大成就，因为相对于其他天体而言，行星体积非常小，且本身并不发光。

name: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
trans: 找到行星已经相当困难，而在行星上寻找生命则更加艰巨。

name: In our own solar system, for example, Venus is far to hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
trans: 首先需要回答的问题是：行星是否真的能够支持生命存在。

name: Only the Earth provides ideal conditions, and even here it has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.
trans: 以我们的太阳系为例，金星温度过高，而火星则过于寒冷，都无法维持生命。

name: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star, that is its 'sun'.
trans: 只有地球具备了理想的生存条件；即便如此，植物和动物的进化也花费了超过40亿年的时间。

name: Imagine a star up to twenty times larger, brighter and hotter than our own sun.
trans: 一个行星能否支持生命，取决于其恒星（即它的“太阳”）的大小和亮度。

name: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
trans: 想象一下：如果有一颗恒星比我们的太阳大20倍、亮度高20倍、温度也高20倍，那么行星必须距离这颗恒星非常遥远，才有可能存在生命。

name: Alternatively, if the star were small,
trans: 或者，如果那颗恒星非常小的话……

name: the life-supporting planet would have to have a close orbit round it and also provide the perfect conditions for life forms to develop.
trans: 这颗能够维持生命的行星必须拥有一个靠近该恒星的轨道，并且必须提供适合生命形式发展的完美条件。

name: But how would we find such a planet?
trans: 但是，我们该如何找到这样一颗行星呢？

name: At present, there is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
trans: 目前，还没有任何现有的望远镜能够探测到生命的存在。

name: The development of such a telescope will be one of the great astronomical projects of the 21st century.
trans: 开发这样的望远镜将是21世纪最重要的天文项目之一。

name: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
trans: 使用地球上的望远镜，是不可能在其他行星上寻找生命的。

name: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope
trans: 我们自身的温暖环境，以及望远镜所产生的热量……

name: would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
trans: 这将使得检测像行星这样微小的物体变得不可能。

name: Even a telescope in orbit round the earth, like the very successful Hubble telescope,
trans: 即使是像哈勃望远镜这样非常成功的、位于地球轨道上的望远镜，

name: would not be suitable because of the dust particles in our solar system.
trans: 由于太阳系中存在大量的尘埃颗粒，这种方法并不适用。

name: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space,
trans: 要在外太空寻找生命，望远镜必须位于距离地球与木星相当远的地方。

name: because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our own solar system.
trans: 因为当我们朝着太阳系的外围移动时，那里的尘埃浓度会变得越来越低（即尘埃变得越来越稀薄）。

name: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star,
trans: 一旦我们发现了一颗行星，我们就必须想办法遮挡掉来自该行星恒星的光线。

name: so that we would be able to 'see' the planet properly and analyse its atmosphere.
trans: 这样我们就能清楚地“看到”这颗行星，并分析其大气层了。

name: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than 'little green men'.
trans: 首先，我们寻找的是植物生命，而不是所谓的“小绿人”。

name: The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.
trans: 最有可能在行星上生存的生命形式是细菌。

name: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
trans: 正是细菌产生了我们地球上所呼吸的氧气。

name: For most of the earth's history they have been the only form of life on our planet.
trans: 在地球历史的大部分时间里，它们都是地球上唯一的生命形式。

name: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.
trans: 作为地球人，我们始终怀揣着这样的希望：有一天，外星的小绿人会来到我们身边，我们能够与他们进行交流。

name: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.
trans: 然而，这种希望始终只存在于科幻作品的范畴之中。

name: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
trans: 如果我们能够在另一颗行星上发现像细菌这样的简单生命形式，那将彻底改变我们对自己的认知。

name: As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.
trans: 正如NASA的丹尼尔·戈尔丁所说：“在其它地方发现生命将会改变一切。”

name: No human endeavour or thought would be unchanged by it.'
trans: 没有任何人类的努力或思考会因此而发生改变。

name: Our neighbour, the river
trans: 我们的邻居——河流

name: Why had the neighbours left their farm?
trans: 为什么邻居们离开了他们的农场？

name: The river which forms the eastern boundary of our farm has always played an important part in our lives.
trans: 为什么邻居们离开了他们的农场？

name: Without it we could not make a living.
trans: 这条河流构成了我们农场的东边界，它一直都在我们的生活中扮演着重要的角色。

name: There is only enough spring water to supply the needs of the house so we have to pump from the river for farm use.
trans: 没有它，我们就无法谋生。

name: We tell the river all our secrets.
trans: 这里的泉水仅够满足房屋的需求，因此我们必须从河里抽水来用于农场灌溉。

name: We know instinctively, just as beekeepers with their bees,
trans: 我们会把所有的秘密都告诉这条河流。

name: that misfortune might overtake us if the important events of our lives were not related to it.
trans: 我们凭直觉明白：就像养蜂人照顾他们的蜜蜂一样，如果我们生活中的重要事件与这条河流无关，那么不幸可能会降临到我们身上。

name: We have special river birthday parties in the summer.
trans: 夏天，我们会为这条河流举办特别的“生日派对”。

name: Sometimes we go upstream to a favourite backwater,
trans: 有时我们会去上游一个我们喜欢的小水湾，

name: sometimes we have our party at the boathouse,
trans: 有时则会在船屋里举行派对。

name: which a predecessor of ours at the farm built in the meadow hard by the deepest pool for swimming and diving.
trans: 这是我们农场的一位前辈在草地上建造的——具体位置就在最深的游泳池旁边，专门用于游泳和潜水。

name: In a heat wave we choose a midnight birthday party and that is the most exciting of all.
trans: 在热浪期间，我们选择在午夜举办生日派对——这真的是所有庆祝方式中最令人兴奋的。

name: We welcome the seasons by the riverside, crowning the youngest girl with flowers in the spring,
trans: 我们在河边迎接四季的更替；春天来临时，我们会用鲜花为最年幼的女孩戴上花环。

name: holding a summer festival on Midsummer Eve, giving thanks for the harvest in the autumn, and throwing a holly wreath into the current in the winter.
trans: 在仲夏夜举办夏季庆典，感谢秋天的丰收；而在冬天，则将冬青花环抛入河流中。

name: After a long period of rain the river may overflow its banks.
trans: 经过长时间的降雨，河流可能会泛滥出河岸。

name: This is a rare occurrence as our climate seldom goes to extremes.
trans: 这种情况非常罕见，因为我们的气候很少会变得极端（即很少出现极端的温度或天气条件）。

name: We are lucky in that only the lower fields,
trans: 我们很幸运，因为只有下方的田地受到了影响（或：只有下方的田地受到了损害）。

name: which make up a very small proportion of our farm, are affected by flooding,
trans: 这些区域仅占我们农场的很小一部分，但却受到了洪水的影响。

name: but other farms are less favourably sited, and flooding can sometimes spell disaster for their owners.
trans: 但其他农场的地理位置较为不利，洪水有时会对农场主造成严重的灾难性后果。

name: One bad winter we watched the river creep up the lower meadows.
trans: 有一个严冬，我们眼睁睁看着河水逐渐淹没了下游的草地。

name: All the cattle had been moved into stalls and we stood to lose little.
trans: 所有的牛都被赶进了牛棚里，所以我们几乎不会有什么损失。

name: We were, however, worried about our nearest neighbours, whose farm was low lying and who were newcomers to the district.
trans: 然而，我们很担心我们的近邻——他们的农场位于地势较低的地方，而且他们是刚搬到这个地区来的新居民。

name: As the floods had put the telephone out of order, we could not find out how they were managing.
trans: 由于洪水导致电话无法正常使用，我们无法了解他们目前的情况（即他们是如何应对这些困难的）。

name: From an attic window we could get a sweeping view of the river where their land joined ours,
trans: 从阁楼的窗户里，我们可以看到河流的全景；他们的土地与我们的土地在那里交汇。

name: and at the most critical juncture we took turns in watching that point.
trans: 在最关键的时刻，我们轮流负责监视那个地点（或目标）。

name: The first sign of disaster was a dead sheep floating down.
trans: 灾难的第一个征兆是一只死羊漂浮在水面上。

name: Next came a horse, swimming bravely,
trans: 接下来是一匹马，它勇敢地游着。

name: but we were afraid that the strength of the current would prevent its landing anywhere before it became exhausted.
trans: 但我们担心，水流的冲击力会使得它无法在电池耗尽之前成功降落在任何地方。

name: Suddenly a raft appeared, looking rather like Noah's ark, carrying the whole family, a few hens, the dogs, a cat, and a bird in a cage.
trans: 突然，一只木筏出现了，它看起来很像诺亚方舟；木筏上载着整个家庭、几只母鸡、几只狗、一只猫，以及一只关在笼子里的鸟。

name: We realized that they must have become unduly frightened by the rising flood,
trans: 我们意识到，他们一定是被不断上涨的洪水吓坏了。

name: for their house, which had sound foundations, would have stood stoutly even if it had been almost submerged.
trans: 他们的房子地基非常坚固，即使几乎被水淹没，也能依然屹立不倒。

name: The men of our family waded down through our flooded meadows with boat hooks,
trans: 我们家族的男人们手持鱼钩，涉水穿过被洪水淹没的草地。

name: in the hope of being able to grapple a corner of the raft and pull it out of the current towrds our bank.
trans: 我们希望能抓住木筏的某个角落，然后把它从湍急的水流中拉到我们的岸边。

name: We still think it a miracle that they were able to do so.
trans: 我们仍然认为他们能够做到这一点简直是个奇迹。

name: Back in the old country
trans: 回到故乡
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: Did the narrater find his mother's grave?
trans: 叙述者找到他母亲的坟墓了吗？
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map.
trans: 我停下来，让车子冷却一下，同时仔细研究地图。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I had expected to be near my objective by now, but everything still seemed alien to me.
trans: 我本以为自己应该已经接近目的地了，但周围的一切依然让我感到陌生。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I was only five when my father had taken me abroad, and that was eighteen years ago.
trans: 我五岁的时候，父亲把我带到了国外，那已经是十八年前的事了。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: When my mother had died after a tragic accident, he did not quickly recover from the shock and loneliness.
trans: 母亲在一次悲剧性的事故中去世后，他久久无法从震惊和孤独中走出来。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: Everything around him was full of her presence, continually reopening the wound.
trans: 他身边的每一样东西都让他想起她，那些回忆不断重新揭开他的伤痛。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: So he decided to emigrate.
trans: 于是，他决定移民。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: In the new country he became absorbed in making a new life for the two of us, so that he gradually ceased to grieve.
trans: 在新的国家里，他全身心地投入到为我们俩创造新生活的过程中，渐渐地，他的悲伤也减轻了。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: He did not marry again and I was brought up without a woman's care; but I lacked for nothing, for he was both father and mother to me.
trans: 他再也没有再婚，我在没有女性照顾的环境中长大；不过我并不缺乏什么，因为父亲同时扮演着母亲的角色。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: He always meant to go back one day, but not to stay.
trans: 他一直说总有一天会回去，但并不是为了定居。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: His roots and mine had become too firmly embedded in the new land.
trans: 他的根基和我的根基都已经深深地扎根在这片新的土地上。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: But he wanted to see the old folk againand to visit my mother's grave.
trans: 但他还是想再见到那些老人，也想去看看我母亲的坟墓。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: He became mortally ill a few months before we had planned to go and, when he knew that he was dying, he made me promise to go on my own.
trans: 就在我们计划出发的几个月前，他突然病重，生命垂危。当他知道自己时日无多时，他让我答应一定要继续完成我们的旅程，即使没有他陪伴。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I hired a car the day after landing and bought a comprehensive book of maps,
trans: 我落地后的第二天就租了一辆车，并买了一本内容详尽的地图册。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: which I found most helpful on the cross-country journey, but which I did not think I should need on the last stage.
trans: 这在我长途旅行的过程中确实非常有用，不过我觉得在最后一段旅程中应该并不需要它。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: It was not that I actually remembered anything at all.
trans: 其实我根本什么都不记得了。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: But my father had described over and over again what we should see at every milestone after leaving the nearest town,
trans: 但我父亲一遍又一遍地描述过，在离开最近的那个小镇之后，我们在每一个重要的里程碑处应该看到什么。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: so that I was positive I should recognize it as familiar territory.
trans: 这样我就能确定：这应该是一个我熟悉的环境（或场景）。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: Well, I had been wrong, for I was now lost.
trans: 好吧，我错了——因为我现在真的迷路了。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I looked at the map and then at the milometer.
trans: 我先看了看地图，然后又看了看里程表。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I had come ten miles since leaving the town and at this point, according to my father,
trans: 自从离开小镇后，我已经走了十英里。据我父亲说，
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I should be looking at farms and cottages in a valley,
trans: 我应该去看看山谷里的农场和小屋。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: with the spire of the church of our village showing in the far distance.
trans: 远处，我们村庄教堂的尖顶清晰可见。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I could see no valley, no farms, no cottages and no church spire-only a lake.
trans: 我看不到任何山谷、农场、小屋，也没有教堂的尖塔——只有一片湖泊。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I decided that I must have taken a wrong turning somewhere.
trans: 我意识到自己肯定在某个地方走错了路（即选择了错误的方向或路径）。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: So I drove back to the town and began to retrace the route, taking frequent glances at the map.
trans: 于是我开车回到了镇上，开始沿着原来的路线返回，同时不时地查看地图。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I landed up at the same corner.
trans: 我最终还是回到了那个同样的角落。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: The curious thing was that the lake was not marked on the map.
trans: 奇怪的是，这个湖泊在地图上根本没有标注。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I felt as if I had stumbled into a nightmare country, as you sometimes do in dreams.
trans: 我感觉自己仿佛闯入了一个噩梦般的国度——就像在梦中有时会遇到的那样。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: And, as in a nightmare, there was nobody in sight to help me.
trans: 就像在噩梦中一样，周围根本没有人能够帮助我。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: Fortunately for me, as I was wondering what to do next,
trans: 幸运的是，就在我思考接下来该做什么的时候……
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: there appeared on the horizon a man on horseback, riding in my direction.
trans: 地平线上出现了一个骑马的人，他正朝我的方向走来。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I waited till he came near, then I asked him the way to our old village.
trans: 我等到他走过来，然后问他去我们老村庄的路。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: He said that there was now no village.
trans: 他说，那个村庄现在已经不存在了。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: I thought he must have misunderstood me, so I repeated its name.
trans: 我以为他一定误解了我的意思，于是我又重复了一遍那个名字。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: This time he pointed to the lake.
trans: 这次他指向了那个湖泊。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: The village no longer existed because it had been submerged, and all the valley too.
trans: 那个村庄已经不存在了——因为它被水淹没了，整个山谷也都消失了。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: The lake was not a natural one, but a man-made reservoir.
trans: 那个湖泊并不是天然的，而是一个人工建造的水库。
lesson: NCE3 · Back in the Old Country

name: A spot of bother
trans: 一个小麻烦；一点小问题。

name: What did the old lady find when she got home?
trans: 那位老太太回家后发现了什么？

name: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats where she lived.
trans: 那位老太太很高兴能够回到她居住的公寓楼。

name: Her shopping had tired her and her basket had grown heavier with every step of the way home.
trans: 她的购物让她感到疲惫不堪；而随着她一步步往家走，她手中的购物篮也越来越重了。

name: In the lift her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest;
trans: 在电梯里，她的思绪都在午餐和好好休息的事情上。

name: but when she got out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door was open.
trans: 但当她走到自己所在的楼层时，她突然发现前门是开着的，这一发现让她完全忘记了之前发生的一切。

name: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help the next morning for such a monstrous piece of negligence,
trans: 她在想，第二天早上一定要严厉责备她的家政人员，因为这种疏忽实在太严重了。

name: when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks.
trans: 当她想起家政人员离开后自己去了购物，而且知道自己已经把两把钥匙都插进了相应的锁孔里时……

name: She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open,
trans: 她缓缓走进大厅，立刻注意到所有的房间门都敞开着。

name: yet following her regular practice she had shut them before going out.
trans: 然而，按照她平时的习惯，她在出门前还是把它们关上了。

name: Looking into the drawing room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk.
trans: 她走进客厅，看到她的书桌旁一片混乱的景象。

name: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
trans: 当时就很明显了：在她的不在期间，窃贼强行进入了房子。

name: Her first impulse was to go round all the rooms looking for the thieves,
trans: 她的第一反应是去各个房间寻找小偷。

name: but then she decided that at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her,
trans: 但后来她想，以她的年纪来说，有个人陪在身边可能会更稳妥些。

name: so she went to fetch the porter from his basement.
trans: 于是她下楼去把门房从他的地下室叫了出来。

name: By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea, while he telephoned the police.
trans: 这时，她的双腿已经开始颤抖了，于是她坐下来喝了一杯浓茶；与此同时，他拨打了报警电话。

name: Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the porter's assistance to search for any intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
trans: 随后，她恢复了镇定，便在门卫的协助下准备出发，去搜寻可能还潜伏在她公寓里的入侵者。

name: They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing,
trans: 他们走过一个又一个房间，小心翼翼地避免触碰任何东西。

name: as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints.
trans: 因为他们不想妨碍警方寻找指纹的工作。

name: The chaos was inconceivable.
trans: 那种混乱简直难以想象。

name: She had lived in the flat for thirty years and was a veritable magpie at hoarding:
trans: 她已经在这套公寓里住了三十年，是个十足的“收集狂”——总是喜欢囤积各种东西。

name: and it seemed as though everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over and over.
trans: 仿佛她拥有的一切都被彻底翻了个个儿，被彻底弄乱了。

name: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.
trans: 至少，把她那些早就该扔掉的东西整理好这件事，现在对她来说变得容易多了。

name: Then a police inspector arrived with a constable and she told them of her discovery of the ransacked flat.
trans: 随后，一名警督带着一名警察来到了现场，她向他们报告了自己发现公寓被洗劫的情况。

name: The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the constable checked that the front door locks had not been forced,
trans: 检查员开始寻找指纹，而警察则确认前门的锁没有被强行破坏。

name: thereby proving that the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
trans: 由此可以证明，窃贼要么使用了万能钥匙，要么是从阳台上进入屋内的。

name: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.
trans: 没有发现任何指纹的痕迹，但检查员发现了一个脏兮兮的红色包裹，里面装着一些首饰。那位老妇人声称这些首饰并不属于她。

name: So their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars' first job that day and they must have been disturbed.
trans: 显然，他们当天进入这套公寓并不是第一次作案；他们肯定遇到了什么干扰（或者：他们的行动被别人发现了）。

name: The inspector then asked the old lady to try to check what was missing by the next day,
trans: 然后，检查员让那位老太太在第二天之前试着看看到底少了什么东西。

name: and advised her not to stay alone in the flat for a few nights.
trans: 并建议她在接下来的几个晚上不要独自待在公寓里。

name: The old lady thought he was a fussy creature,
trans: 那位老太太认为他是个挑剔的人。

name: but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
trans: 但由于门房同意了他的请求，她便给女儿打了电话，请求她的帮助来处理这个她所说的“小麻烦”。

name: Collecting
trans: 收集；采集

name: What in particular does a person gain when he or she becomes a serious collector?
trans: 一个人成为真正的收藏家后，具体能获得什么呢？

name: People tend to amass possessions, sometimes without being aware of doing so.
trans: 人们往往会积累财物，有时甚至自己都没有意识到这一点。

name: Indeed they can have a delightful surprise when they find something useful which they did not know they owned.
trans: 确实，当他们发现某些自己原本不知道拥有的、但却非常实用的东西时，会感到非常惊喜。

name: Those who never have to move house become indiscriminate collectors of what can only be described as clutter.
trans: 那些从未搬过家的人，会无差别地收集各种杂物——这些杂物其实只能被归类为“杂乱无章的堆积物”。

name: They leave unwanted objects in drawers, cupboards and attics for years, in the belief that they may one day need just those very things.
trans: 他们把不需要的物品放在抽屉、橱柜或阁楼里多年，认为有朝一日自己可能会用到那些东西。

name: As they grow old, people also accumulate belongings for two other reasons,
trans: 随着年龄的增长，人们积累物品还有另外两个原因：

name: lack of physical and mental energy, both of which are essential in turning out and throwing away, and sentiment.
trans: 缺乏体力和精力——这两者都是完成某项任务所必需的；同时，也缺乏相应的情绪（或：缺乏完成任务的积极态度或动力）。

name: Things owned for a long time are full of associations with the past,
trans: 那些已经拥有很长时间的东西，都承载着与过去相关的种种回忆和情感联系。

name: perhaps with relatives who are dead, and so they gradually acquire a value beyond their true worth.
trans: 也许这些物品与已经去世的亲人有关联，因此它们逐渐被赋予了超出其实际价值的意义（或：这些物品因为与逝去亲人的联系而变得更有价值）。

name: Some things are collected deliberately in the home in an attempt to avoid waste.
trans: 有些物品是人们特意在家里收集起来的，目的是为了减少浪费。

name: Among these I would list string and brown paper,
trans: 在这些物品中，我会列出“string”（一种线状材料）和“brown paper”（棕色纸）。

name: kept by thrifty people when a parcel has been opened, to save buying these two requisites.
trans: 节俭的人在拆开包裹后，会保留这些物品，以避免再次购买这两样必需品。

name: Collecting small items can easily become a mania.
trans: 收集小物件很容易变成一种强迫性行为（或者说，一种难以控制的癖好）。

name: I know someone who always cuts sketches out from newspapers of model clothes that she would like to buy if she had the money.
trans: 我认识一个人，她总是从报纸上剪下那些她想要购买的模特服装的图片；如果她有钱的话，一定会买下这些衣服。

name: As she is not rich, the chances that she will ever be able to afford such purchases are remote;
trans: 由于她并不富裕，她能够负担得起这类购买的费用的可能性微乎其微。

name: but she is never sufficiently strongminded to be able to stop the practice.
trans: 但她始终缺乏足够的意志力，因此无法阻止这种行为（或：她始终无法坚定自己的立场，从而无法阻止这种不良现象的发生）。

name: It is a harmless habit, but it litters up her desk to such an extent that every time she opens it, loose bits of paper fall out in every direction.
trans: 这其实是个无伤大雅的习惯，但这个习惯让她的办公桌变得非常杂乱——每次她打开桌子时，都会有一堆散落的纸屑从各个方向掉出来。

name: Collecting as a serious hobby is quite different and has many advantages.
trans: 将收藏作为一种严肃的爱好来从事，其实有着许多独特的优势。

name: It provides relaxation for leisure hours, as just looking at one's treasures is always a joy.
trans: 它为休闲时光带来了放松与愉悦；仅仅欣赏自己的收藏品，本身就是一种享受。

name: One does not have to go outside for amusement, since the collection is housed at home.
trans: 人们不必外出寻找娱乐方式，因为这些藏品都收藏在家里。

name: Whatever it consists of, stamps, records, first editions of books, china, glass,
trans: 无论这些东西是什么——印章、记录、书籍的初版、瓷器、玻璃制品……

name: antique furniture, pictures, model cars, stuffed birds, toy animals, there is always something to do in connection with it,
trans: 古董家具、画作、模型汽车、毛绒玩具、玩具动物……总有一些事情可以与它们相关联、可以去做。

name: from finding the right place for the latest addition, to verifying facts in reference books.
trans: 从为最新添加的内容找到合适的位置，到在参考书中核实事实……

name: This hobby educates one not only in the chosen subject, but also in general matters which have some bearing on it.
trans: 这个爱好不仅能让人在所选择的领域内学到知识，还能帮助人们了解与该领域相关的一些通用性知识。

name: There are also other benefits.
trans: 还有其他一些好处。

name: One wants to meet like-minded collectors, to get advice, to compare notes, to exchange articles, to show off the latest find.
trans: 人们希望结识志同道合的收藏家，向他们请教建议，交流彼此的收藏心得，互相分享文章，以及展示自己最近发现的珍品。

name: So one's circle of friends grows.
trans: 因此，一个人的朋友圈子也会逐渐扩大。

name: Soon the hobby leads to travel, perhaps to a meeting in another town,
trans: 很快，这个爱好就发展成了旅行的动力——也许会促使我去另一个城镇参加某个会议。

name: possibly a trip abroad in search of a rare specimen, for collectors are not confined to any one country.
trans: 也许他们会去国外寻找稀有的标本，因为收藏家们并不局限于某个特定的国家。

name: Over the years, one may well become an authority on one's hobby and will very probably be asked to give informal talks to little gatherings
trans: 随着时间的推移，一个人很可能会在自己的爱好领域成为专家，并且很可能会被邀请在一些小型聚会上进行非正式的演讲。

name: and then, if successful, to larger audiences.
trans: 然后，如果成功的话，就会面向更广泛的受众群体进行推广。

name: In this way self-confidence grows, first from mastering a subject, then from being able to talk about it.
trans: 通过这种方式，自信心得以培养：首先是通过掌握某个学科的知识，然后是通过能够就该学科进行讨论或表达自己的观点来增强自信心。

name: Collecting, by occupying spare time so constructively, makes a person contented, with no time for boredom.
trans: 通过利用空闲时间来从事有意义的活动，一个人会感到满足，从而不会有无聊的感觉。

name: Too early and too late
trans: 既太早，又太晚。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Why did the young girl miss the train?
trans: 为什么那个小女孩错过了火车？
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Punctuality is a necessary habit in all public affairs in civilized society.
trans: 在文明社会的所有公共事务中，守时是一种必不可少的习惯。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Without it, nothing could ever be brought to a conclusion; everything would be in a state of chaos.
trans: 没有它，一切都无法完成或达到最终状态；一切都将陷入混乱之中。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Only in a sparsely-populated rural community is it possible to disregard it.
trans: 只有在人口稀少的农村社区，人们才有可能忽视这个问题（或：只有在这样的环境中，人们才有可能对这个问题视而不见）。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: In ordinary living, there can be some tolerance of unpunctuality.
trans: 在日常生活中，对于迟到这种行为，人们通常可以有一定的宽容度。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The intellectual, who is working on some abstruse problem, has everything coordinated and organized for the matter in hand.
trans: 这位正在研究某个复杂问题的学者，已经将自己手头的工作所需的一切资料和信息都整理得井井有条、有条不紊了。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: He is therefore forgiven if late for a dinner party.
trans: 因此，如果他因为晚到而错过了晚宴，也是可以被原谅的。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: But people are often reproached for unpunctuality when their only fault is cutting things fine.
trans: 但是，人们常常因为不守时而受到指责，而他们真正的过错其实只是稍微提前完成了任务（即比原定时间提前完成了工作）。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: It is hard for energetic, quick-minded people to waste time,
trans: 对于那些精力充沛、思维敏捷的人来说，浪费时间是一件很难做到的事情。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: so they are often tempted to finish a job before setting out to keep an appointment.
trans: 因此，他们常常会忍不住在赴约之前先把工作完成。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: If no accidents occur on the way, like punctured tyres, diversions of traffic, sudden descent of fog, they will be on time.
trans: 如果途中没有发生任何意外（比如轮胎爆裂、交通延误、雾突然变浓等情况），他们就能准时到达。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: They are often more industrious, useful citizens than those who are never late.
trans: 他们通常比那些从不迟到的人更勤奋、更有用，是更值得信赖的公民。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The over-punctual can be as much a trial to others as the unpunctual.
trans: 那些总是提前到达的人，可能会给别人带来同样的困扰——甚至比那些不守时的人更麻烦。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The guest who arrives half an hour too soon is the greatest nuisance.
trans: 那位提前半小时就到的客人真是最让人烦恼的人了。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Some friends of my family had this irritating habit.
trans: 我家的一些朋友有个让人很恼火的习惯。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The only thing to do was ask them to come half an hour later than the other guests.
trans: 唯一可行的办法就是让他们比其他客人晚半小时到达。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Then they arrived just when we wanted them.
trans: 然后他们正好在我们需要的时候到了。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: If you are catching a train, it is always better to be comfortably early than even a fraction of a minute too late.
trans: 如果你要赶火车，提前到达总是更好的选择——哪怕只是提前几分钟也好，总比迟到哪怕一小会儿要好得多。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Although being early may mean wasting a little time,
trans: 虽然提前行动可能会浪费一些时间，
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: this will be less than if you miss the train and have to wait an hour or more for the next one;
trans: 这总比你错过火车、然后不得不等待下一班火车（一个小时或更长时间）要好吧。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: and you avoid the frustration of arriving at the very moment when the train is drawing out of the station and being unable to get on it.
trans: 这样你就避免了那种令人沮丧的情况：当你赶到车站时，火车正好已经启动离开，而你却无法上车。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: An even harder situation is to be on the platform in good time for a train and still to see it go off without you.
trans: 更糟糕的情况是：你虽然及时赶到了火车站，却还是眼睁睁看着火车在你离开后驶离了。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Such an experience befell a certain young girl the first time she was travelling alone.
trans: 这样的经历发生在一个年轻女孩第一次独自旅行的时候。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: She entered the station twenty minutes before the train was due,
trans: 她在火车预计到达时间的前二十分钟进入了车站。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: since her parents had impressed upon her
trans: 因为她的父母一直向她灌输这样的观念（或：因为她的父母让她明白了这一点）。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: that it would be unforgivable to miss it and cause the friends with whom she was going to stay to make two journeys to meet her.
trans: 错过这个机会是不可原谅的；这会让那些本来要和她一起旅行的朋友们不得不额外跑两次路来见她。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: She gave her luggage to a porter and showed him her ticket.
trans: 她把行李交给了行李员，并出示了自己的机票。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: To her horror he said that she was two hours too soon.
trans: 令她惊恐的是，他说她来得太早了——比预定的时间早了两个小时。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: She felt in her handbag for the piece of paper on which her father had written down all the details of the journey and gave it to the porter.
trans: 她在手提包里寻找那张纸，上面写着父亲记录的所有旅行细节，然后把纸交给了行李员。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: He agreed that a train did come into the station at the time on the paper and that it did stop, but only to take on mail, not passengers.
trans: 他承认，根据记录，当时确实有一列火车驶入了车站并且停了下来，但那列火车只是来取邮件的，并没有搭载乘客。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The girl asked to see a timetable, feeling sure that her father could not have made such a mistake.
trans: 女孩要求查看时刻表，因为她确信她的父亲不可能犯这样的错误。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The porter went to fetch one and arrived back with the station master,
trans: 门卫去拿了一个东西，然后带着站长回来了。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: who produced it with a flourish and pointed out a microscopic 'o' beside the time of the arrival of the train at his station;
trans: 是谁精心制作了这个东西的？他们还在火车到达车站的时间旁边标出了一个微小的“o”符号。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: this little 'o' indicated that the train only stopped for mail.
trans: 这个小小的“O”符号表示火车只是为了取邮件而停靠的。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: Just as that moment the train came into the station.
trans: 就在那一刻，火车驶进了车站。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: The girl, tears streaming down her face, begged to be allowed to slip into the guard's van.
trans: 女孩泪流满面，恳求允许她爬进火车的守卫车厢。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: But the station master was adamant: rules could not be broken.
trans: 但车站站长坚决反对：规则是不能被打破的。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late

name: And she had to watch that train disappear towards her destination while she was left behind.
trans: 她只能眼睁睁看着火车驶向目的地，而自己却被留在了车站。
lesson: NCE3 · Too Early and Too Late
